catalog.name: Payments and Bank Reconciliation calculations
catalog.description: Every formula, algorithm, rounding rule and worked example of the payments and bank reconciliation domain, in a structured form a rebuild can test against: the rounding and sign conventions and the four currency roles, the residual amounts of a journal item, the whole reconciliation operation from the optimisation of the plan to the pairing loop, the single-pair matching with its residual maps, its two reconciliation-currency branches, its rounding-tolerance collapse and its four exchange-difference branches, the exchange-difference entries and their reversal, the detection of a full reconciliation and the matching number, the ordering index and the four balances of a bank statement, the three currencies and three amounts of a bank transaction and the three conversions at the bank's own rate, the reconciliation of a transaction and the reconciliation models with their four counterpart amount modes, the whole register-payment arithmetic with its batches, its installments, its four totals, its payment difference and its early payment discount lines, the amounts of a payment entry, the international bank account number validation with its country templates, the seven structured payment reference schemes, the two quick response code generators, the dashboard figures of a liquidity journal, the selection of the journal, the payment method and the recipient account, and the memo of a payment.
catalog.authored_from: docs/domains/payments-and-bank-reconciliation/calculations.md, with the cash-basis quantities and the company attribution of docs/domains/payments-and-bank-reconciliation/accounting-effects.md and the rule sections of docs/domains/payments-and-bank-reconciliation/business-rules.md

records.name: Rounding a monetary value to its currency
records.purpose: The primitive every other calculation of the domain rests on: it turns a raw arithmetic result into a value the currency can actually express, so that two independent implementations agree to the last decimal.

operands.name: raw value
operands.constraints: any real number, positive or negative

operands.name: rounding step of the currency
operands.constraints: ten raised to the power of minus the number of decimal places of the currency

preconditions.condition: A currency is supplied.
preconditions.otherwise: The company currency is used, and when the item has no company currency either, the currency of the active company is used.

procedure: Read the number of decimal places of the currency and derive its rounding step as ten raised to the power of minus that number.
Divide the raw value by the rounding step.
Round the quotient to the nearest whole number, sending an exact half away from zero.
Multiply the whole number back by the rounding step.
Apply the sub-step correction that removes binary floating-point artefacts, as the multi-currency document specifies.
records.formula:
rounding_step = 10 raised to the power ( − number of decimal places of the currency )
rounded_value = round_to( currency , raw_value ) = rounding_step × nearest_whole_number( raw_value ÷ rounding_step ) , halves away from zero

rounding.what: The raw value itself.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the currency, which is one hundredth for a currency of two decimal places.
rounding.step: At the moment the primitive is called; every formula of the domain states where that is.

result.name: rounded value
result.stored_or_displayed: Whatever the calling formula stores or displays; the primitive itself stores nothing.

edge_cases.case: The raw value is exactly halfway between two multiples of the rounding step.
edge_cases.outcome: It goes away from zero, so a raw 0.005 becomes 0.01 and a raw −0.005 becomes −0.01.

edge_cases.case: The currency has zero decimal places.
edge_cases.outcome: The rounding step is one and the result is a whole number of currency units.

edge_cases.case: The raw value carries a binary floating-point artefact just below or just above a half.
edge_cases.outcome: The sub-step correction of the multi-currency document pulls it back onto the intended half before the tie-break is applied.

worked_examples.description: A currency of two decimal places
worked_examples.narrative: The quotient is 199999.5, an exact half, which goes away from zero to 200000, and multiplying back by one hundredth gives 2000.00.

worked_examples.description: A negative exact half
worked_examples.narrative: Half away from zero sends a negative half further from zero, so the result is minus one hundredth and not zero.

records.name: The zero test for a currency
records.purpose: Decides whether an amount counts as nothing in a given currency, which is how every exhaustion, settlement and completeness test in the domain is expressed.

operands.name: value
operands.constraints: any real number

operands.name: currency
operands.source: the item, the journal, the statement or the company
operands.constraints: supplies the rounding step

preconditions.condition: The currency is known.
preconditions.otherwise: The company currency is used.

procedure: Round the value to the currency.
Answer true exactly when the rounded value equals zero.
records.formula: is_zero( currency , value ) = ( round_to( currency , value ) = 0 )

rounding.what: The value being tested.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the currency.
rounding.step: Before the comparison with zero, never after.

result.name: the zero verdict
result.stored_or_displayed: Used inside other calculations; the reconciled flag of a journal item is the only place it is stored.

edge_cases.case: The value is a fraction of the rounding step, for example four thousandths in a currency of two decimal places.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds to zero and the test answers true, so the amount is treated as settled.

edge_cases.case: The value is exactly half a rounding step.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds away from zero to one full step and the test answers false.

worked_examples.description: A residual of four thousandths in a currency of two decimal places
worked_examples.narrative: Four thousandths rounds to zero, so the item counts as fully settled.

worked_examples.description: A residual of five thousandths in a currency of two decimal places
worked_examples.narrative: The exact half goes away from zero to one hundredth, so the item still carries a residual.

records.name: The three-way comparison of two amounts in a currency
records.purpose: Compares two amounts at the precision of a currency, so that a difference smaller than one rounding step never decides which side of a matching is fully consumed.

operands.name: first amount
operands.constraints: any real number

operands.name: second amount
operands.constraints: any real number

preconditions.condition: Both amounts are expressed in the same currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The comparison is meaningless; the calling formula must convert first.

procedure: Subtract the second amount from the first.
Round the difference to the currency.
Answer minus one when the rounded difference is negative, zero when it is zero, and plus one when it is positive.
records.formula:
compare( currency , a , b ) = −1 when round_to( currency , a − b ) < 0
                             =  0 when round_to( currency , a − b ) = 0
                             = +1 when round_to( currency , a − b ) > 0

rounding.what: The difference between the two amounts, not the amounts themselves.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the currency.
rounding.step: After the subtraction and before the sign is read.

result.name: the comparison verdict
result.unit_or_currency: minus one, zero or plus one
result.stored_or_displayed: Used inside other calculations; never stored.

edge_cases.case: The two amounts differ by less than half a rounding step.
edge_cases.outcome: The rounded difference is zero and the verdict is zero, so the two are treated as equal.

edge_cases.case: Both amounts are rounded already and differ by exactly one rounding step.
edge_cases.outcome: The verdict is plus one or minus one; no tie-break is involved.

worked_examples.description: Comparing six hundred with one thousand
worked_examples.narrative: The debit side is the smaller of the two, so the debit is fully matched and the credit is not.

worked_examples.description: Comparing two amounts that differ by a fraction of a cent
worked_examples.narrative: The raw difference of four thousandths rounds to zero, so both sides count as fully matched.

records.name: The two signed quantities of a journal item
records.purpose: Fixes the sign convention that every residual, every matching and every exchange difference of the domain obeys, so that a debit is always positive and a credit always negative.

operands.name: debit
operands.constraints: never negative

operands.name: credit
operands.constraints: never negative

operands.name: foreign amount
operands.constraints: carries the same sign as the balance, except on an exchange-difference line where one of the two may be zero

preconditions.condition: At most one of the debit and the credit is non-zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The item is malformed and the general ledger refuses it.

procedure: Subtract the credit from the debit to obtain the balance, in the company currency.
Read the foreign amount as the same movement expressed in the currency of the item, with the same sign.

Carry the sign of the amount into the residual: a receivable item of an unpaid customer invoice keeps a positive balance and a positive residual, and a payable item of an unpaid vendor bill keeps a negative balance and a negative residual.
Read the amount of a Payment as always positive, its direction carrying the sign, and the amount of a Bank Transaction as the bank signed it, positive for money coming in.
Read the three amounts of a Partial Reconciliation as always positive.
records.formula:
balance = debit − credit
amount_currency = the same movement expressed in the currency of the item , with the same sign as the balance

rounding.what: The balance and the foreign amount as they are stored.
rounding.precision: The company currency for the balance, the currency of the item for the foreign amount.
rounding.step: When the item is written, not when the sign is read.

result.name: the balance and the foreign amount of the item
result.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the item
result.stored_or_displayed: Both stored on the Journal Item; the balance drives every company-currency figure of the domain.

edge_cases.case: An exchange-difference line carries a balance but no foreign amount, or a foreign amount but no balance.
edge_cases.outcome: The two signs are allowed to disagree, and the item may enter both the debit queue and the credit queue of the pairing loop.

edge_cases.case: A Payment carries a zero amount.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction cannot be read from the sign; the stored direction alone decides it.

worked_examples.description: An unpaid customer invoice line of one thousand
worked_examples.narrative: The receivable line is a debit, so its balance and its residual are both positive one thousand.

worked_examples.description: An unpaid vendor bill line of one thousand
worked_examples.narrative: The payable line is a credit, so its balance and its residual are both minus one thousand.

records.name: The four currency roles of the domain
records.purpose: Names the four currencies every formula of the domain distinguishes, so that a rebuild never confuses the currency an amount is expressed in with the currency it is converted through.

operands.name: the currency of the company
operands.constraints: the currency the books are kept in; every balance is expressed in it

operands.name: the own currency of the liquidity journal
operands.constraints: the company currency when the journal names none

operands.name: the currency of a Bank Transaction as the bank reported it
operands.constraints: its foreign currency when it has one, otherwise the journal currency

operands.name: the currency of one journal item
operands.constraints: the company currency when the item carries no foreign amount

preconditions.condition: Every amount states which of the four currencies it is expressed in.
preconditions.otherwise: The formulas of the domain cannot be evaluated, because a conversion would be applied twice or not at all.

procedure: Read the company currency as the currency the books are kept in; every balance is expressed in it.
Read the journal currency as the own currency of a liquidity journal, and as the company currency when the journal names no currency.
Read the transaction currency as the currency of a Bank Transaction as the bank reported it: its foreign currency when it has one, and otherwise the journal currency.
Read the item currency as the currency of one journal item, which equals the company currency when the item carries no foreign amount.
records.formula:
company currency     = the currency the books are kept in ; every balance is expressed in it
journal currency     = the own currency of a liquidity journal , or the company currency when it names none
transaction currency = the foreign currency of a Bank Transaction when it has one , otherwise the journal currency
item currency        = the currency of one journal item , equal to the company currency when the item carries no foreign amount

rounding.what: Nothing; the four roles name currencies rather than amounts.
rounding.precision: Each currency supplies its own rounding step to the formulas that use it.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, wherever a rounding is applied.
rounding.step: Stated by each formula individually.

result.name: the four currency roles
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; every formula of the domain names the role it works in.

edge_cases.case: The journal names no currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The journal currency is the company currency and two of the four roles coincide.

edge_cases.case: The transaction names no foreign currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The transaction currency is the journal currency.

edge_cases.case: The item carries no foreign amount.
edge_cases.outcome: The item currency is the company currency and the two residuals of the item move together.

edge_cases.case: All four coincide.
edge_cases.outcome: Every conversion of the domain is an identity and no exchange difference can arise.

worked_examples.description: A company whose books are in one currency, a bank journal held in another, and a transaction reported in a third
worked_examples.narrative: All four roles are distinct, which is the case the exchange-difference rules exist for.

records.name: Deciding whether a journal item carries residual amounts
records.purpose: Separates the items that can be matched from those that cannot, which is the gate in front of every reconciliation figure of the domain.

operands.name: the reconcilable flag of the account
operands.constraints: set by configuration

operands.name: the type of the account
operands.constraints: the bank-and-cash type and the credit-card type qualify on their own

preconditions.condition: The item names an account.
preconditions.otherwise: It carries no residual and can never be matched.

procedure: Read the account of the item.
Answer that the item has residual amounts when the account allows reconciliation, or when its type is the bank-and-cash type, or when its type is the credit-card type.
Otherwise force both residuals to zero and never offer the item for matching.
records.formula:
has_residual( item ) = account allows reconciliation
                    OR account type = bank and cash
                    OR account type = credit card

rounding.what: Nothing; the decision is a truth value.
rounding.step: Before the residual formulas are evaluated.

result.name: whether the item carries residual amounts
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it gates the two stored residual fields, which are forced to zero when it is false.

edge_cases.case: The account is a liquidity account that does not allow reconciliation.
edge_cases.outcome: The item still carries residuals, because the bank-and-cash type and the credit-card type qualify on their own.

edge_cases.case: The account is an expense or income account.
edge_cases.outcome: Both residuals are zero and the item is never matched, even when it appears inside a reconciliation request.

edge_cases.case: An imported item sits on an account that does not allow reconciliation but carries a temporary matching number.
edge_cases.outcome: The deferred matching operation makes the account reconcilable before matching the group, and records that it did.

worked_examples.description: A customer receivable item
worked_examples.narrative: A trade account allows reconciliation, so the item carries residuals.

worked_examples.description: A bank account that does not allow reconciliation
worked_examples.narrative: The account type alone qualifies the item, so the liquidity line of a payment can be matched with a bank transaction.

worked_examples.description: An expense account
worked_examples.narrative: Both residuals are forced to zero and the item never enters a matching.

records.name: The matched amounts of a journal item, per side
records.purpose: Totals everything already matched against an item, separately for the matchings in which it is the debit side and those in which it is the credit side, which is the input the residual formula subtracts.

operands.name: amount of each Partial Reconciliation whose debit item is this item
operands.constraints: always positive

operands.name: debit foreign amount of each of those same Partial Reconciliations
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency stored on the matching for the debit side
operands.constraints: always positive

operands.name: amount of each Partial Reconciliation whose credit item is this item
operands.constraints: always positive

operands.name: credit foreign amount of each of those same Partial Reconciliations
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency stored on the matching for the credit side
operands.constraints: always positive

preconditions.condition: The currency stored on the matching for a side is the currency the foreign amounts of that side are summed in.
preconditions.otherwise: The rounding would use the wrong number of decimal places and the residual would drift.

procedure: Gather every Partial Reconciliation in which the item is the debit item and add their company-currency amounts, giving the amount matched as debit.
Add the debit foreign amounts of those same matchings and round the sum, not each term, to the currency stored on the matching for the debit side.
Gather every Partial Reconciliation in which the item is the credit item and add their company-currency amounts, giving the amount matched as credit.
Add the credit foreign amounts of those same matchings and round the sum, not each term, to the currency stored on the matching for the credit side.
records.formula:
matched_as_debit           = Σ amount over the partial reconciliations whose debit item is this item
matched_as_debit_currency  = round_to( item_currency , Σ debit_amount_currency over those same partial reconciliations )
matched_as_credit          = Σ amount over the partial reconciliations whose credit item is this item
matched_as_credit_currency = round_to( item_currency , Σ credit_amount_currency over those same partial reconciliations )

rounding.what: The two sums of foreign amounts. The two company-currency sums are not rounded here, because each term is already rounded to the company currency.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the currency stored on the matching for that side.
rounding.step: On the sum, after every term has been added, never on each term.

result.name: the four matched totals of the item
result.unit_or_currency: company currency for two of them, the currency of the item for the other two
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; they feed the two stored residual fields.

edge_cases.case: The item takes part in no matching at all.
edge_cases.outcome: All four totals are zero and the residuals equal the balance and the foreign amount.

edge_cases.case: The item is the debit side of one matching and the credit side of another.
edge_cases.outcome: Both pairs of totals are non-zero; the residual formula subtracts one pair and adds the other.

edge_cases.case: Each individual foreign amount would round up but the sum would not.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum is what is rounded, so the total never drifts by the accumulation of per-term roundings.

worked_examples.description: An invoice line matched twice, once by four hundred and once by five hundred and fifty
worked_examples.narrative: The invoice line is the debit item of both matchings, so the whole nine hundred and fifty is matched as debit.

records.name: The residual amounts of a journal item
records.purpose: Gives what is still open on an item in both the company currency and the currency of the item; every payment state, every dashboard figure and every matching decision reads it.

operands.name: balance
operands.constraints: the debit minus the credit

operands.name: foreign amount
operands.constraints: carries the sign of the balance

operands.name: amount matched as debit
operands.source: the Partial Reconciliations whose debit item is this item
operands.constraints: always positive

operands.name: amount matched as credit
operands.source: the Partial Reconciliations whose credit item is this item
operands.constraints: always positive

operands.name: foreign amount matched as debit
operands.source: the same matchings, rounded on the sum
operands.constraints: always positive

operands.name: foreign amount matched as credit
operands.source: the same matchings, rounded on the sum
operands.constraints: always positive

preconditions.condition: The item carries residual amounts at all.
preconditions.otherwise: Both residuals are zero and the item is never reconciled.

preconditions.condition: The item names a company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The currency of the active company is used, which happens on a record still being edited.

preconditions.condition: The item names a currency of its own.
preconditions.otherwise: The company currency is used as the currency of the item.

procedure: Take the balance, subtract the amount matched as debit and add the amount matched as credit.
Round that result to the company currency: it is the residual in the company currency.
Take the foreign amount, subtract the foreign amount matched as debit and add the foreign amount matched as credit, each of those two totals having already been rounded to the currency of the item.
Round that result to the currency of the item: it is the residual in the currency of the item.
records.formula:
amount_residual          = round_to( company_currency , balance − matched_as_debit + matched_as_credit )
amount_residual_currency = round_to( item_currency , amount_currency − matched_as_debit_currency + matched_as_credit_currency )

rounding.what: Each of the two residuals, once the whole expression has been evaluated.
rounding.precision: The company currency for the first, the currency of the item for the second.
rounding.step: After the subtraction and the addition, and after the matched foreign totals have themselves been rounded on their sums.

result.name: the residual in the company currency and the residual in the currency of the item
result.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the item
result.stored_or_displayed: Both stored on the Journal Item and recomputed after every creation and deletion of matchings.

edge_cases.case: The item takes part in no matching.
edge_cases.outcome: The residuals equal the balance and the foreign amount exactly.

edge_cases.case: The item has no company currency because the record is still being edited.
edge_cases.outcome: The currency of the active company is used for the first rounding.

edge_cases.case: The item has no currency of its own.
edge_cases.outcome: The company currency is used, and the two residuals move together.

edge_cases.case: The account does not allow reconciliation and is neither bank-and-cash nor credit-card.
edge_cases.outcome: Both residuals are zero whatever the balance is.

worked_examples.description: The worked example of the document: a customer invoice of one thousand settled twice
worked_examples.narrative: The invoice line is the debit item of both matchings, so nine hundred and fifty is subtracted from one thousand and fifty remains in both currencies.

records.name: The reconciled flag of a journal item
records.purpose: Says whether an item is completely settled, which is the condition the full-reconciliation detector and the payment states of documents read.

operands.name: residual in the company currency
operands.constraints: may be a fraction of a rounding step

operands.name: residual in the currency of the item
operands.constraints: may be a fraction of a rounding step

preconditions.condition: The item carries residual amounts at all.
preconditions.otherwise: The flag is false, because an item that can never be matched is never reconciled.

procedure: Test the residual in the company currency for zero at the precision of the company currency.
Test the residual in the currency of the item for zero at the precision of that currency.
Answer true only when both tests answer true.
records.formula: reconciled = is_zero( company_currency , amount_residual ) AND is_zero( item_currency , amount_residual_currency )

rounding.what: Each residual before it is compared with zero.
rounding.precision: The company currency for one test, the currency of the item for the other.
rounding.step: Inside each zero test, immediately before the comparison.

result.name: the reconciled flag
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Item and recomputed whenever the residuals are.

edge_cases.case: The company-currency residual is zero but a foreign residual remains.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag stays false; an exchange difference or a further matching is still owed.

edge_cases.case: The foreign residual is zero but a company-currency residual remains.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag stays false; this is the drift an exchange-difference entry closes.

edge_cases.case: Both residuals are zero but the item takes part in no matching at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag is true, yet the full-reconciliation detector still refuses to count the item as settled, because an item with no matching never closes a group.

worked_examples.description: An invoice line matched for one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five of two thousand, with the drift closed by an exchange line
worked_examples.narrative: Both residuals are zero once the exchange line of one hundred and twenty-five has been matched, so the item is reconciled.

worked_examples.description: A partially settled invoice line
worked_examples.narrative: Fifty remains in both currencies, so the flag is false and the document stays partially paid.

records.name: Optimising the reconciliation plan into nodes
records.purpose: Turns the plan a caller wrote into an ordered tree of nodes, fixing both which items meet and in which order they meet, which is what decides how a payment is spread over several documents.

operands.name: the members of the plan
operands.unit_or_currency: sets of Journal Items, or nested plans
operands.constraints: a member that is a set becomes a leaf; a member that is itself a list becomes a branch

operands.name: the due date of each item, falling back to its date
operands.constraints: the first sort key

operands.name: the currency of each item
operands.constraints: the second sort key and the key the leaf is split on

operands.name: the signed foreign amount of each item
operands.constraints: the third sort key

operands.name: the balance of each item
operands.constraints: the fourth sort key

operands.name: the reduced line sorting flag
operands.constraints: when set, only the first two sort keys are used

preconditions.condition: Every top-level node passes the eligibility check of the items it holds.
preconditions.otherwise: The whole reconciliation is refused with the message of the failing eligibility test.

preconditions.condition: A node holds at least one item.
preconditions.otherwise: The node is dropped.

procedure: Walk the plan; a member that is a set of journal items becomes a leaf, and a member that is itself a list becomes a branch whose sub-nodes are the optimised forms of its members and whose item set is the union of theirs.

For a leaf, sort its items by the due date, or by the date when there is no due date, then by the currency, then by the signed foreign amount, then by the balance; under the reduced line sorting flag keep only the first two keys.

For a leaf, look at the currencies present; when more than one is present, keep the sorted item set on the leaf and give it one sub-node per currency holding the items of that currency in the sorted order, so that items of the same currency meet each other before any cross-currency matching is attempted.
For every top-level node, run the eligibility check on its item set and drop empty nodes.
Return the list of nodes together with the union of all their items.
records.formula:
sort_key( item ) = ( due date , or date when there is none ; currency ; signed foreign amount ; balance )
sort_key_reduced( item ) = ( due date , or date when there is none ; currency )
a leaf holding more than one currency gains one sub-node per currency, holding that currency's items in the sorted order

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded; the sort compares stored amounts as they are.
rounding.step: Before any matching is computed.

result.name: the ordered list of nodes and the union of their items
result.stored_or_displayed: Held for the duration of the operation; the created matchings are attached back to the node that produced them.

edge_cases.case: The plan is a single leaf holding one currency.
edge_cases.outcome: No sub-node is created and the pairing loop runs once on the sorted set.

edge_cases.case: A leaf holds two currencies.
edge_cases.outcome: Two sub-nodes are created and walked first, so same-currency pairs are exhausted before the leaf's own set is walked.

edge_cases.case: A member is an empty set.
edge_cases.outcome: The node is dropped and contributes nothing.

edge_cases.case: The reduced line sorting flag is set.
edge_cases.outcome: Items of one due date and one currency keep the order the caller supplied, because the amount keys are not applied.

worked_examples.description: The plan of the register-payment flow: one invoice due on the tenth of March, one due on the twentieth, and the payment dated the twenty-fifth

inputs.plan: a single leaf holding the two invoice receivable items and the payment counterpart item

sorted_order: the invoice due on the tenth of March
the invoice due on the twentieth of March
debit_queue: the invoice due on the tenth of March
the invoice due on the twentieth of March

worked_examples.narrative: One currency only, so no sub-node is created; the due-date key puts the older invoice first, which is why the payment settles it in full before touching the other.

records.name: The eligibility check of a set of items
records.purpose: Refuses a reconciliation that could not produce a coherent result, and states the exact refusal, before any matching is computed.

operands.name: the matching number of each item
operands.constraints: a partial number begins with the letter P

operands.name: the reconciled flag of each item
operands.constraints: computed from the residuals

operands.name: the state of the entry of each item
operands.constraints: a cancelled entry disqualifies its items

operands.name: the account of each item
operands.constraints: must be one single account for the whole set

operands.name: the root company of each item
operands.constraints: must be one single root company for the whole set

preconditions.condition: The set is applied to a top-level node, not to a sub-node.
preconditions.otherwise: The check does not run, because the sub-node's items were already covered by the check of the node above.

procedure: Collect the partial matching numbers, those beginning with the letter P, carried by the items of the set that are not fully reconciled.

Narrow the set to the items that are not reconciled, plus the items that are reconciled but whose matching number is not one of the numbers just collected, so that a caller may pass a whole matching group of which some items are already settled.
If nothing is left after the narrowing, the check passes.
If any remaining item is reconciled, refuse with "You are trying to reconcile some entries that are already reconciled."
If any remaining item belongs to a cancelled entry, refuse with "You can not reconcile cancelled entries."
Collect the accounts of the remaining items; if there is more than one, refuse with "Entries are not from the same account: *the account display names, separated by commas*".
If the root companies of the remaining items are more than one, refuse with "Entries don't belong to the same company: *the company display names, separated by commas*".

If the single account does not allow reconciliation and its type is neither the bank-and-cash type nor the credit-card type, refuse with "Account *the account display name* does not allow reconciliation. First change the configuration of this account to allow it."

rounding.what: Nothing; the check reads flags, accounts and companies.
rounding.step: Once per top-level node, before the pairing loop.

result.name: the eligibility verdict
result.unit_or_currency: pass, or a refusal carrying its exact message
result.stored_or_displayed: Shown to the user as a refusal; nothing is stored.

edge_cases.case: The caller passes a whole matching group of which some items are already settled.
edge_cases.outcome: The narrowing keeps only the unsettled ones and the group is accepted, so a settled group can be extended.

edge_cases.case: Every item of the set is already reconciled and shares the same partial number.
edge_cases.outcome: The narrowed set is empty and the check passes without doing anything.

edge_cases.case: A reconciled item carries a partial number that no unreconciled item of the set carries.
edge_cases.outcome: It stays in the narrowed set and triggers the refusal about entries already reconciled.

edge_cases.case: The single account is a liquidity account that does not allow reconciliation.
edge_cases.outcome: The check passes, because the bank-and-cash type and the credit-card type are accepted on their own.

worked_examples.description: A second payment against an invoice already carrying a partial number

items: the invoice receivable item, not reconciled, matching number P17
the counterpart item of the second payment, not reconciled, no matching number

worked_examples.narrative: Neither item is reconciled, so both stay in the narrowed set, one account and one company are present and the account allows reconciliation: the check passes and the second matching can be created.

worked_examples.description: Two items on two different accounts

expected_outputs.message: Entries are not from the same account: Accounts Receivable, Accounts Payable

worked_examples.narrative: More than one account survives the narrowing, so the refusal names both accounts separated by a comma.

records.name: Walking a node of the plan
records.purpose: Fixes the depth-first order in which a node's sub-nodes and its own item set are processed, and the regrouping by counterparty that lets a mixed selection settle each counterparty against itself.

operands.name: the sub-nodes of the node
operands.constraints: processed in order, before the node's own set

operands.name: the item set of the node
operands.constraints: already sorted by the optimisation

operands.name: the items already recorded as fully reconciled by an earlier step of this same operation
operands.source: the running state of the operation
operands.constraints: removed from the set before anything else

operands.name: the counterparty of each item
operands.constraints: items without a counterparty sort first

preconditions.condition: The node survived the eligibility check.
preconditions.otherwise: The whole operation was already refused.

procedure: Process the sub-nodes of the node first, in order, each by this same procedure.
Then take the node's own item set and remove from it every item already recorded as fully reconciled by an earlier step of this same operation.

If the remaining items belong to more than one counterparty, re-sort them by counterparty identifier, putting the items without a counterparty first, so that the debits of a counterparty meet the credits of that same counterparty.
Run the pairing loop on the remaining items in that order.
records.formula:
process( node ) = process every sub-node in order , then process the node's own item set
remaining = the node's items minus the items already fully reconciled by this operation
if the remaining items carry more than one counterparty : re-sort by counterparty identifier , items with no counterparty first

rounding.what: Nothing; the walk only orders items.
rounding.step: Before each pairing loop.

result.name: the matchings produced by the node and the items it exhausted
result.stored_or_displayed: Attached to the node and created in one batch at the end of the operation.

edge_cases.case: Every item of the node was already exhausted by a sub-node.
edge_cases.outcome: The node's own set is empty and the pairing loop does nothing.

edge_cases.case: The node's items all belong to one counterparty.
edge_cases.outcome: The counterparty re-sort is skipped and the optimisation's order stands.

edge_cases.case: Some items carry no counterparty at all.
edge_cases.outcome: They sort first, ahead of every named counterparty.

worked_examples.description: A branch holding two currency sub-nodes

sub_nodes: the sub-node of the first currency
the sub-node of the second currency

processing_order: the sub-node of the first currency
the sub-node of the second currency
the node's own set restricted to the items still open

worked_examples.narrative: Same-currency pairs are settled first, and only what is left crosses the two currencies.

records.name: The pairing loop of a node
records.purpose: Walks an ordered list of items and produces the matchings, one debit against one credit at a time, until one of the two queues runs out.

operands.name: the ordered list of item states
operands.constraints: each state holds the item, its running residual in the company currency and its running residual in the currency of the item

operands.name: the balance of each item
operands.constraints: decides membership of the debit queue when positive and of the credit queue when negative

operands.name: the signed foreign amount of each item
operands.constraints: also decides queue membership, so one item may sit in both queues

preconditions.condition: Both queues hold at least one state.
preconditions.otherwise: The loop stops immediately and produces nothing.

procedure: Build the debit queue from the states whose item has a balance greater than zero or a signed foreign amount greater than zero, in the given order.
Build the credit queue from the states whose item has a balance less than zero or a signed foreign amount less than zero, in the given order.
Set the current debit state and the current credit state to empty.
If there is no current debit state, take the next one from the debit queue; when that queue is exhausted, stop.
If there is no current credit state, take the next one from the credit queue; when that queue is exhausted, stop.
Compute one matching between the current debit state and the current credit state, which updates both running residuals in place.
If the computation produced matching values, record them.
If the computation reports that the debit state has nothing left, mark its item fully reconciled for this operation and clear the current debit state.
If it reports the same for the credit state, do likewise, then repeat from the step that refills the current debit state.
Return the recorded matchings and the set of items marked fully reconciled.
records.formula:
debit_queue  = the states whose item has balance > 0 OR signed foreign amount > 0 , in the given order
credit_queue = the states whose item has balance < 0 OR signed foreign amount < 0 , in the given order
repeat : take a debit state and a credit state , compute one matching , record it , drop whichever state is exhausted
the loop terminates because every iteration either produces a matching that strictly reduces a residual or removes a state from a queue

rounding.what: Nothing at this level; the rounding happens inside the single-pair computation.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the list of matchings and the set of exhausted items
result.stored_or_displayed: Handed back to the node, which creates the Partial Reconciliations in one batch.

edge_cases.case: An item has a positive balance and a negative foreign amount, or the reverse, as an exchange-difference line does.
edge_cases.outcome: It enters both queues; the loop still terminates, because every iteration either strictly reduces a residual or removes a state.

edge_cases.case: The debit queue is empty.
edge_cases.outcome: The loop stops at once and no matching is produced.

edge_cases.case: A pair produces no matching because one side has no entry in the reconciliation currency.
edge_cases.outcome: That side is reported exhausted and the loop moves on to the next state of its queue.

worked_examples.description: Two invoices against one payment, all in the company currency

ordered_states.item: invoice due the tenth of March
invoice due the twentieth of March

debit_queue: invoice due the tenth of March
invoice due the twentieth of March

worked_examples.narrative: The first iteration exhausts the older invoice, the second exhausts the payment, and the credit queue is then empty so the loop stops with one hundred still open on the second invoice.

records.name: The three closing phases of a reconciliation
records.purpose: States what is written once every matching has been computed: the matchings themselves, the exchange entries, the cash-basis entries, the full-reconciliation markers and the paid hooks of the settled documents.

operands.name: the computed matchings, in the order they were produced
operands.source: the pairing loops of the nodes
operands.constraints: created in one batch, in that order

operands.name: the add cash-basis values flag
operands.constraints: when set, the snapshot of the cash-basis values is stored on each new matching

operands.name: the reverse-cancel flag and the no cash basis flag
operands.constraints: either one suppresses the cash-basis entries

operands.name: the prepared exchange-difference entries
operands.constraints: created in one batch and posted when both matched items belong to posted entries

preconditions.condition: At least one matching was computed.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is created and the operation ends.

preconditions.condition: For the cash-basis step, the node's items sit on a receivable or payable account and the company uses cash-basis taxes.
preconditions.otherwise: No cash-basis entry is produced for that node.

procedure: Create every Partial Reconciliation in one batch, in the order they were computed, and attach the created records back to the node that produced them.
When the add cash-basis values flag is set, store on each new matching the snapshot of the cash-basis values that produced it.
Create the exchange-difference entries in one batch and post those whose two matched items both belong to posted entries.

Link each exchange entry to the matching that produced it: for each matching, in order, find the first unused exchange entry that references either of its two items and is not yet linked, and store it on the matching.

When neither the reverse-cancel flag nor the no cash basis flag is set, then for every node whose items sit on a receivable or payable account and whose company uses cash-basis taxes, create the cash-basis tax entries from that node's matchings and store the cash-basis snapshot on them.
Detect the full reconciliations.

Call the post-matching hook: every document that was not paid and is now fully paid or awaiting the clearing of its payment, and every document that was awaiting the clearing of its payment and is now paid, runs its paid hook.
records.formula:
phase three = create the matchings in one batch , in the computed order
phase four  = create and post the exchange entries , link each to its matching ,
              create the cash-basis entries for the qualifying nodes ,
              detect the full reconciliations , run the paid hooks

rounding.what: Nothing; every amount was rounded when the matching was computed.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the created Partial Reconciliations, exchange entries, cash-basis entries and Full Reconciliations
result.stored_or_displayed: All stored; the residuals of the matched items are recomputed from them.

edge_cases.case: An exchange entry references both items of two consecutive matchings.
edge_cases.outcome: The linking walks the matchings in order and takes the first unused entry, so each entry is linked exactly once.

edge_cases.case: The reconciliation runs under the reverse-cancel flag.
edge_cases.outcome: No cash-basis entry is created, because the reconciliation is itself the undoing of an earlier one.

edge_cases.case: One of the two matched items belongs to a draft entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The exchange entry is created but left in draft rather than posted.

worked_examples.description: A single-currency reconciliation of three items
worked_examples.narrative: Only the two matchings are written; with no rate movement and no cash-basis taxes nothing else is produced, and the group is not complete because one invoice keeps a residual.

records.name: The cash-basis quantities a matching contributes
records.purpose: Gives the four numbers this domain hands to the cash-basis tax entries that a matching on a trade account triggers; the content of those entries belongs to the tax domain, these quantities do not.

operands.name: the company-currency amount of the matching
operands.constraints: always positive

operands.name: the foreign amount of the matching on the document's side
operands.constraints: always positive

operands.name: the total balance of the document
operands.constraints: must not be zero for the first branch

operands.name: the total foreign amount of the document
operands.constraints: must not be zero for the second branch

operands.name: the balance and the foreign amount of the other matched item
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of that item
operands.source: the other side of the matching
operands.constraints: used as the rate numerator and denominator when no rate is forced

operands.name: the rate forced by the register-payment flow
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the source currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the register-payment screen, when the difference is pushed onto an exchange account
operands.constraints: when supplied, it wins over every other branch

preconditions.condition: The matching touches a receivable or payable account and the company uses cash-basis taxes.
preconditions.otherwise: No cash-basis entry is produced and the quantities are not computed.

preconditions.condition: The company has a cash-basis journal.
preconditions.otherwise: The creation fails with "There is no tax cash basis journal defined for the '*the company display name*' company." followed by the line "Configure it in Accounting/Configuration/Settings".

procedure: Compute the percentage of the document that this matching settles: the company-currency amount of the matching divided by the total balance of the document when the document is in the company currency, otherwise the foreign amount of the matching divided by the total foreign amount of the document.

Compute the payment rate: the forced rate when the register-payment flow supplied one; otherwise, when the two matched lines carry different currencies, the conversion rate from the company currency to the currency of the source line, for the company of the counterpart line, at the payment date; otherwise the ratio of the rate foreign amount to the rate amount, and zero when the rate amount is zero.

Read the rate amount and the rate foreign amount from the side that is not the document: minus the credit item's balance and minus its foreign amount when the debit item belongs to the document, the debit item's balance and foreign amount when the credit item belongs to the document, and the document's own line's balance and foreign amount when both matched documents are invoice-like, so that each document uses its own rate.
Compute the settlement date: the later of the two matched items' dates when both matched documents are invoice-like, otherwise the date of the counterpart line.
Record whether both matched items belong to posted entries.
Date the cash-basis entry on the later of the settlement date and the day after the company's fiscal lock date for the cash-basis journal.
records.formula:
percentage      = partial_amount ÷ the document's total balance                 when the document is in the company currency
                = partial_amount_currency ÷ the document's total foreign amount   otherwise

payment_rate    = the forced rate supplied by the register-payment flow , when there is one
                = the conversion rate from the company currency to the source line's currency , for the counterpart line's company , at the payment date , when the two matched lines have different currencies
                = rate_amount_currency ÷ rate_amount                              when rate_amount ≠ 0
                = 0                                                               otherwise

settlement_date = the later of the two matched items' dates , when both matched documents are invoice-like
                = the counterpart line's date , otherwise

both_posted     = whether both matched items belong to posted entries

rounding.what: Neither the percentage nor the rate is rounded here; the tax domain rounds the amounts it derives from them.
rounding.precision: The percentage is carried at full precision; the derived tax amounts are rounded to the company currency and to the currency of the document.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied by the tax domain.
rounding.step: After the percentage has been applied to a tax base, never before.

result.name: the percentage settled, the payment rate, the settlement date and the both-posted flag
result.unit_or_currency: a ratio, a rate, a date and a truth value
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as the cash-basis snapshot on the matching when the add cash-basis values flag is set, and read by the tax domain when it builds the entry.

edge_cases.case: The rate amount is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The payment rate is zero and the tax domain treats the settlement as carrying no rate of its own.

edge_cases.case: Both matched documents are invoice-like, as when a credit note settles an invoice.
edge_cases.outcome: Each document uses its own line's balance and foreign amount as the rate pair, so neither document inherits the other's rate.

edge_cases.case: The settlement date falls before the company's fiscal lock date for the cash-basis journal.
edge_cases.outcome: The entry is dated on the day after that lock date instead.

worked_examples.description: A matching of three hundred against a document of one thousand, both in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: Three tenths of the document is settled, and because both sides are in the company currency the payment rate is one.

records.name: The company that carries the derived entries of a matching
records.purpose: Decides in which company the exchange-difference entry and the cash-basis entry of a matching are written, which matters when a branch's invoice is settled by the parent's payment.

operands.name: the company of the debit item
operands.source: the debit side of the matching
operands.constraints: chosen when the entry of the debit item is an invoice-like document

operands.name: the company of the credit item
operands.source: the credit side of the matching
operands.constraints: chosen otherwise

operands.name: the companies of the items of the prepared exchange entry
operands.source: the items collected for the entry
operands.constraints: re-derived independently of the matching

preconditions.condition: A company resolves for the prepared exchange entry.
preconditions.otherwise: No exchange-difference entry is prepared at all.

procedure: Read the company of the matching as the company of the debit item when the entry of that item is an invoice-like document, and as the company of the credit item otherwise.

For the exchange-difference entry, re-derive the company from the entry's own items: the company of the invoice-like entries among them when there are any, otherwise the company of the items, otherwise the company passed explicitly by the caller.
When none of the three resolves, prepare no entry.
records.formula:
company_of_matching = the debit item's company   when the debit item's entry is an invoice-like document
                    = the credit item's company  otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule selects a company.
rounding.step: Before the derived entries are prepared.

result.name: the company of the derived entries
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the exchange-difference entry and on the cash-basis entry.

edge_cases.case: A branch's invoice is settled by the parent's payment.
edge_cases.outcome: The exchange difference and the cash-basis entry are written in the branch that carries the invoice.

edge_cases.case: Neither matched item belongs to an invoice-like entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The company of the credit item is used.

edge_cases.case: No company resolves for the exchange entry.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is prepared, and the drift stays on the item.

worked_examples.description: A branch invoice settled by a parent payment

inputs.debit_item: the receivable item of the branch's invoice
inputs.credit_item: the counterpart item of the parent's payment

worked_examples.narrative: The debit item's entry is an invoice-like document, so the branch carries the exchange difference and the cash-basis entry.

records.name: The accounting rate of a journal item
records.purpose: Reads back, from the item itself, the rate at which it was booked, so that a matching in the currency of the item can be converted to the company currency at exactly the rate the books already carry.

operands.name: foreign amount of the item
operands.constraints: must not be zero in that currency

operands.name: balance of the item
operands.constraints: must not be zero in the company currency

preconditions.condition: The balance is not zero in the company currency and the foreign amount is not zero in the given currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The rate is undefined and the caller falls back to the platform rate or to no rate at all.

procedure: Divide the foreign amount of the item by its balance.
Take the absolute value of the quotient, so the rate is positive whichever side of the entry the item is on.
When either operand is zero at the precision of its currency, report the rate as undefined.
records.formula:
accounting_rate( item , currency ) = | amount_currency ÷ balance |   when balance ≠ 0 in the company currency and amount_currency ≠ 0 in that currency
                                   = undefined                      otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing; the rate is carried at full precision.
rounding.precision: Not applicable; the amounts it is later multiplied by are what get rounded.
rounding.step: Never; rounding a rate would move the matched amounts.

result.name: the accounting rate of the item towards its own currency
result.unit_or_currency: units of the currency of the item per unit of the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; held in the residual map for the duration of the matching.

edge_cases.case: The item has a balance but no foreign amount, as an exchange-difference line in the company currency does.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate is undefined, which is what puts the pair into the exchange-line mode.

edge_cases.case: The item has a foreign amount but a zero balance.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate is undefined for the same reason.

edge_cases.case: The item is in the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The foreign amount equals the balance and the rate is one.

worked_examples.description: An invoice booked at two thousand in the company currency for one thousand five hundred in its own currency
worked_examples.narrative: One unit of the company currency buys three quarters of a unit of the invoice currency, which is the rate of the invoice date.

worked_examples.description: A bank transaction booked at one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five for one thousand five hundred
worked_examples.narrative: The absolute value is taken, so the credit side yields a positive rate of four fifths.

records.name: The platform rate of a journal item towards a counterpart currency
records.purpose: Chooses the rate at which an item kept in the company currency on a trade account is offered in the currency of the item it is about to meet, so that a company-currency invoice can be settled by a foreign-currency payment.

operands.name: the rate forced by the register-payment flow
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the counterpart currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the register-payment screen, when it pushes the whole difference onto an exchange account
operands.constraints: when supplied it wins over every later branch

operands.name: the other item of the pair
operands.constraints: used only when this item is not payment-like and the other one is

operands.name: the invoice date of the entry of the item
operands.source: the Journal Entry, when it is an invoice-like document
operands.constraints: used as the rate date in preference to the item's own date

operands.name: the date of the item
operands.constraints: used as the rate date otherwise

operands.name: the conversion rate table of the company
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the counterpart currency per unit of the company currency
operands.constraints: read at the rate date

preconditions.condition: A counterpart currency different from the company currency is supplied.
preconditions.otherwise: The rate is never asked for, because the mimicking rule does not apply.

procedure: When the register-payment flow supplied a forced rate, return that rate and stop.
When there is an other item, this item is not payment-like and the other item is, return the accounting rate of the other item towards the counterpart currency.
Otherwise take as the rate date the invoice date of the item's entry when that entry is an invoice-like document, and the date of the item otherwise.
Return the conversion rate from the company currency to the counterpart currency, for the company of the item, at that rate date.
Read an item as payment-like exactly when its entry has an originating Payment or an originating Bank Transaction.
records.formula:
platform_rate( item , other_item , currency ) :
    1. if a forced rate was supplied by the register-payment flow , return it
    2. if there is an other item , the item is not payment-like and the other item is , return accounting_rate( other_item , currency )
    3. rate_date = the invoice date of the item's entry when that entry is an invoice-like document , otherwise the item's date
    4. return the conversion rate from the company currency to currency , for the item's company , at rate_date

rounding.what: Nothing; the rate is carried at full precision.
rounding.step: Never; the amount the rate is applied to is what is rounded.

result.name: the rate towards the counterpart currency
result.unit_or_currency: units of the counterpart currency per unit of the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; held in the residual map for the duration of the matching.

edge_cases.case: A company-currency invoice meets a foreign-currency payment.
edge_cases.outcome: The invoice is not payment-like and the payment is, so the payment's own accounting rate is used and the bank's rate prevails over the rate table.

edge_cases.case: Both items are payment-like.
edge_cases.outcome: Neither branch two applies; the rate table is read at the item's own date.

edge_cases.case: The register-payment flow forced a rate.
edge_cases.outcome: That rate is used and the whole difference is pushed into an exchange-difference entry.

edge_cases.case: The entry is an invoice-like document with an invoice date earlier than the item's date.
edge_cases.outcome: The invoice date is the rate date, so the rate of the invoice, not of the accounting date, is used.

worked_examples.description: A company-currency invoice item meeting a foreign-currency payment item
worked_examples.narrative: Branch two applies, so the payment's own accounting rate of four fifths is returned and the invoice is offered at the rate the bank actually used.

records.name: The available residual of one item, per currency
records.purpose: Builds, for one item and one counterpart currency, the map that says in which currencies that item still has something to offer and at which rate, which is what the choice of reconciliation currency reads.

operands.name: running residual in the company currency
operands.source: the item state of the pairing loop
operands.constraints: updated in place after every matching

operands.name: running residual in the currency of the item
operands.source: the item state of the pairing loop
operands.constraints: updated in place after every matching

operands.name: the currency of the item
operands.constraints: equals the company currency when the item carries no foreign amount

operands.name: the counterpart currency
operands.source: the other item of the pair
operands.constraints: drives the mimicking rule

operands.name: the type of the account of the item
operands.constraints: the mimicking rule applies only to a receivable or a payable account

preconditions.condition: The item still has a residual in at least one currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The map is empty and the item is reported exhausted.

procedure: Read the running residual in the company currency, the running residual in the currency of the item, the currency of the item and the account of the item.
When the running residual in the company currency is not zero in that currency, add the entry that maps the company currency to that residual with a rate of one.

When the currency of the item differs from the company currency and the running residual in the currency of the item is not zero in that currency, add the entry that maps the currency of the item to that residual with the accounting rate of the item.

When the currency of the item equals the company currency, and the account is a receivable or a payable account, and the running residual in the company currency is not zero, and the counterpart currency differs from the company currency: take the platform rate towards the counterpart currency, multiply the running company-currency residual by it, round the product to the counterpart currency, and when that is not zero add the entry that maps the counterpart currency to that converted residual with that rate.

Otherwise, when the currency of the item equals the counterpart currency and differs from the company currency and the running residual in the currency of the item is not zero, add the entry that maps the counterpart currency to that residual with the accounting rate of the item; because both keys name the same currency the effect is the same as the earlier entry.

rounding.what: The residual converted into the counterpart currency by the mimicking rule.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the counterpart currency.
rounding.step: Immediately after the multiplication by the rate, before the entry is added and before the zero test.

result.name: the map from currency to the pair of an available residual and its rate
result.unit_or_currency: one residual per currency present, each in that currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the following steps of the same matching.

edge_cases.case: The item is in the company currency on a receivable account and meets a foreign-currency item.
edge_cases.outcome: The mimicking rule adds a foreign entry, so the two items can be matched in the foreign currency at the rate of the day.

edge_cases.case: The item is in the company currency on an account that is neither receivable nor payable.
edge_cases.outcome: No mimicking entry is added and the pair falls back to the company currency.

edge_cases.case: The converted residual rounds to zero in the counterpart currency.
edge_cases.outcome: No entry is added for that currency, and the side may be reported exhausted.

edge_cases.case: The item has a foreign residual but no company-currency residual left.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the foreign entry is present, which is what the exchange-line mode detects.

worked_examples.description: The invoice side of the worked example of section four point six
worked_examples.narrative: The item carries both a company-currency residual and a foreign residual, so both entries are present, the foreign one at the accounting rate of three quarters.

worked_examples.description: The bank transaction side of the same example
worked_examples.narrative: The credit side keeps its negative residuals and its own accounting rate of four fifths.

records.name: Choosing the reconciliation currency of a pair
records.purpose: Decides in which currency a debit and a credit meet, which decides in turn whether an exchange difference can arise at all and which of the two sides carries it.

operands.name: the residual map of the debit item, built with the credit item's currency as counterpart
operands.constraints: may hold the company currency, the debit currency and the credit currency

operands.name: the residual map of the credit item, built with the debit item's currency as counterpart
operands.constraints: the same

operands.name: the currency of the debit item
operands.constraints: considered first

operands.name: the currency of the credit item
operands.constraints: considered second

preconditions.condition: Both maps were built with the other item's currency as the counterpart currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The mimicking entries would be missing and the pair would fall back to the company currency unnecessarily.

procedure: When the currency of the debit item differs from the company currency and is present in both maps, take it as the reconciliation currency.
Otherwise, when the currency of the credit item differs from the company currency and is present in both maps, take it as the reconciliation currency.
Otherwise take the company currency as the reconciliation currency.
records.formula:
reconciliation_currency = debit_currency   when debit_currency ≠ company_currency and debit_currency is a key of both maps
                        = credit_currency  when credit_currency ≠ company_currency and credit_currency is a key of both maps
                        = company_currency otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing; the step selects a currency.
rounding.step: After both maps have been built and before any amount is computed.

result.name: the reconciliation currency of the pair
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides which branch of the amount computation and of the exchange-difference computation runs.

edge_cases.case: Both items are in the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: Neither of the first two tests can pass, so the company currency is chosen.

edge_cases.case: The debit is in a foreign currency and the credit is in the company currency on a trade account.
edge_cases.outcome: The mimicking rule put the debit currency into the credit's map, so the debit currency is chosen and the settlement happens in the foreign currency.

edge_cases.case: The two items are in two different foreign currencies and neither appears in both maps.
edge_cases.outcome: The company currency is chosen and the pair meets through the books.

edge_cases.case: The debit currency is foreign but absent from the credit's map.
edge_cases.outcome: The second test is tried, and the credit currency is chosen when it is present in both maps.

worked_examples.description: A foreign-currency invoice meeting a foreign-currency bank transaction
worked_examples.narrative: The debit currency differs from the company currency and appears in both maps, so it wins on the first test.

worked_examples.description: Two company-currency items
worked_examples.narrative: Neither currency differs from the company currency, so the third branch applies.

records.name: The two amounts to be matched, and the stop when there is nothing left
records.purpose: Reads the two residuals that will actually be compared, in the reconciliation currency, and reports a side exhausted when it has nothing to offer in that currency.

operands.name: the entry of the reconciliation currency in the debit map
operands.source: the residual map of the debit item
operands.constraints: absent when the debit side has nothing left in that currency

operands.name: the entry of the reconciliation currency in the credit map
operands.source: the residual map of the credit item
operands.constraints: absent when the credit side has nothing left in that currency

preconditions.condition: The reconciliation currency has been chosen.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to look up.

procedure: Look up the reconciliation currency in the debit map; when it is absent, report the debit state exhausted.
Look up the reconciliation currency in the credit map; when it is absent, report the credit state exhausted.
When either side was reported exhausted, produce no matching and return.

Otherwise take the debit amount to be matched as the residual of the debit entry, and the credit amount to be matched as minus the residual of the credit entry, so that both are positive for an ordinary debit against credit pair.
records.formula:
recon_debit_amount  =   the debit entry's residual
recon_credit_amount = − the credit entry's residual

rounding.what: Nothing; both residuals were rounded when the maps were built.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Earlier, in the residual map.

result.name: the two positive amounts to be compared
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the comparison and the amount computation.

edge_cases.case: The debit map has no entry for the reconciliation currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The debit state is exhausted, no matching is produced, and the pairing loop takes the next debit state.

edge_cases.case: Both maps lack the entry.
edge_cases.outcome: Both states are exhausted and the loop advances on both queues.

edge_cases.case: The credit residual is positive, as on an exchange-difference line with reversed signs.
edge_cases.outcome: The negation makes the credit amount negative, and the comparison then reports the credit side fully matched at once.

worked_examples.description: An invoice of six hundred against a payment of one thousand, in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: Both amounts come out positive, which is what lets the comparison decide which side is the smaller.

records.name: Detecting the exchange-line mode of a pair
records.purpose: Recognises that one of the two items is an exchange-difference line, so that the matching moves only the company-currency amount and leaves the foreign amounts untouched.

operands.name: the reconciliation currency
operands.constraints: must be the company currency for the mode to be possible

operands.name: the currency of the debit item
operands.constraints: must equal the currency of the credit item

operands.name: the currency of the credit item
operands.constraints: must equal the currency of the debit item

operands.name: whether the debit map holds an entry for the debit currency
operands.source: the residual map of the debit item
operands.constraints: its absence signals an exhausted foreign residual

operands.name: whether the credit map holds an entry for the credit currency
operands.source: the residual map of the credit item
operands.constraints: the same

preconditions.condition: Both maps have already been built with the other item's currency as counterpart.
preconditions.otherwise: The absence of an entry could not be read as an exhausted foreign residual.

procedure: Check that the reconciliation currency is the company currency.
Check that the two items share the same currency.
Check that at least one of the two maps has no entry for that shared currency.
When all three hold, the pair is in the exchange-line mode; no rate is applied on either side.
records.formula:
exchange_line_mode = ( reconciliation currency = company currency )
                 AND ( debit currency = credit currency )
                 AND ( the debit map has no entry for the debit currency OR the credit map has no entry for the credit currency )

rounding.what: Nothing; the mode is a truth value.
rounding.step: After the reconciliation currency is chosen and before the amounts are computed.

result.name: the exchange-line mode flag
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it forces both rates to be undefined in the amount computation.

edge_cases.case: Both items share a foreign currency but one has no foreign amount left.
edge_cases.outcome: The mode is on, so the matching changes only the company-currency amount and the foreign residual of the other side is left alone.

edge_cases.case: The two items share a foreign currency and both still have foreign residuals.
edge_cases.outcome: The mode is off, and the reconciliation currency would in any case have been the shared foreign currency.

edge_cases.case: The two items are in two different currencies.
edge_cases.outcome: The mode is off, whatever the maps hold.

worked_examples.description: An exchange-difference line meeting the drifting item it was created for
worked_examples.narrative: The exchange line has a balance but no foreign residual, so the mode is on and the matching moves one hundred and twenty-five in the company currency and nothing in the foreign currency.

records.name: Deciding which side of a pair is fully matched
records.purpose: Compares the two amounts at the precision of the reconciliation currency and fixes the smaller of the two, which is the amount the matching will carry and the flags the exchange-difference branches read.

operands.name: the debit amount to be matched
operands.constraints: positive for an ordinary pair

operands.name: the credit amount to be matched
operands.constraints: positive for an ordinary pair

preconditions.condition: Both amounts are expressed in the reconciliation currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The comparison would mix currencies.

procedure: Compare the debit amount with the credit amount at the precision of the reconciliation currency.
Take the smaller of the two as the amount that will be matched.
Mark the debit side fully matched when the comparison is less than or equal to zero.
Mark the credit side fully matched when the comparison is greater than or equal to zero, so that both flags are true when the two amounts are equal.
records.formula:
comparison           = compare( reconciliation currency , recon_debit_amount , recon_credit_amount )
min_recon_amount     = min( recon_debit_amount , recon_credit_amount )
debit_fully_matched  = ( comparison ≤ 0 )
credit_fully_matched = ( comparison ≥ 0 )

rounding.what: The difference of the two amounts, inside the comparison.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the reconciliation currency.
rounding.step: Inside the comparison, before the sign is read.

result.name: the comparison, the amount to be matched and the two fully-matched flags
result.unit_or_currency: the reconciliation currency for the amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; they drive the amount computation and the exchange-difference branches.

edge_cases.case: The two amounts are equal at the precision of the reconciliation currency.
edge_cases.outcome: Both flags are true and both sides are exhausted by this matching.

edge_cases.case: The two amounts differ by less than half a rounding step.
edge_cases.outcome: The comparison reports zero and both flags are true, so no residue is left behind.

edge_cases.case: The credit amount is the smaller one.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the credit flag is true; the debit keeps a residual and stays the current debit state of the loop.

worked_examples.description: Six hundred against one thousand
worked_examples.narrative: The invoice is smaller, so it is exhausted and the payment keeps four hundred.

worked_examples.description: Four hundred against four hundred
worked_examples.narrative: Equality sets both flags, and the pairing loop advances on both queues.

records.name: The matched amounts when the reconciliation currency is the company currency
records.purpose: Produces the three amounts of the matching when the two items meet in the books' own currency, converting the matched amount back into each side's own currency at that side's rate.

operands.name: the amount to be matched
operands.constraints: the smaller of the two residuals

operands.name: the rate of the debit currency entry in the debit map
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the debit currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the residual map of the debit item
operands.constraints: undefined when the entry is absent or the pair is in the exchange-line mode

operands.name: the rate of the credit currency entry in the credit map
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the credit currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the residual map of the credit item
operands.constraints: the same

operands.name: the running foreign residual of the debit item
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the debit item
operands.constraints: caps the converted amount

operands.name: the running foreign residual of the credit item
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the credit item
operands.constraints: caps the converted amount, after negation

preconditions.condition: The reconciliation currency is the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The foreign-currency branch applies instead.

procedure: When the pair is in the exchange-line mode, treat both rates as undefined; otherwise read the debit rate from the entry of the debit currency in the debit map and the credit rate from the entry of the credit currency in the credit map, each undefined when its entry is absent.
Set the company-currency amount of the matching to the amount to be matched.

When the debit rate is defined, multiply it by the amount to be matched, round the product to the debit currency, and take the smaller of that and the running foreign residual of the debit item; when the rate is undefined, use zero.

When the credit rate is defined, multiply it by the amount to be matched, round the product to the credit currency, and take the smaller of that and minus the running foreign residual of the credit item; when the rate is undefined, use zero.
records.formula:
partial_amount = min_recon_amount
