partial_debit_amount_currency  = min( round_to( debit_currency  , debit_rate  × min_recon_amount ) ,   remaining_debit_amount_currency  )   when the debit rate is defined , else 0
partial_credit_amount_currency = min( round_to( credit_currency , credit_rate × min_recon_amount ) , − remaining_credit_amount_currency )   when the credit rate is defined , else 0

rounding.what: Each converted foreign amount, after the multiplication by the rate.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the debit currency and of the credit currency respectively.
rounding.step: After the multiplication and before the capping by the running foreign residual.

result.name: the company-currency amount and the two foreign amounts of the matching
result.unit_or_currency: company currency, the currency of the debit item, the currency of the credit item
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Partial Reconciliation as the amount, the debit foreign amount and the credit foreign amount.

edge_cases.case: The pair is in the exchange-line mode.
edge_cases.outcome: Both rates are undefined, both foreign amounts are zero, and only the company-currency amount moves.

edge_cases.case: The converted amount exceeds the running foreign residual.
edge_cases.outcome: The cap takes over, which prevents a foreign residual from going past zero and into the opposite sign.

edge_cases.case: Both items are in the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: Both rates are one, and both foreign amounts equal the company-currency amount.

worked_examples.description: The first iteration of the worked example of section three point eleven
worked_examples.narrative: Both items are in the company currency, so both rates are one; the debit conversion is capped at its own residual of six hundred and the credit conversion at one thousand, leaving six hundred on both sides.

records.name: The interval of an amount after a rate
records.purpose: Gives the lowest, the central and the highest image of an already rounded amount once a rate is applied to it, which is what lets the matching tell a genuine rate difference from a rounding artefact.

operands.name: the amount to convert
operands.constraints: already rounded to the currency converted from, so its true value lies in an interval

operands.name: the rate
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the currency converted to per unit of the currency converted from
operands.constraints: undefined or zero yields three zeros

operands.name: the rounding step of the currency converted from
operands.constraints: halved to give the width of the interval on each side

preconditions.condition: The rate is defined and not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The helper returns zero for all three values.

procedure: When the rate is undefined or zero, return three zeros.
Halve the rounding step of the currency converted from.
Subtract that half-step from the amount, multiply by the rate and round to the currency converted to: that is the low image.
Multiply the amount itself by the rate and round to the currency converted to: that is the middle image.
Add the half-step to the amount, multiply by the rate and round to the currency converted to: that is the high image.
records.formula:
range_after_rate( currency_from , currency_to , amount , rate ) :
    if the rate is undefined or zero : return ( 0 , 0 , 0 )
    half_step = rounding step of currency_from ÷ 2
    low    = round_to( currency_to , ( amount − half_step ) × rate )
    middle = round_to( currency_to ,   amount               × rate )
    high   = round_to( currency_to , ( amount + half_step ) × rate )
    return ( low , middle , high )

rounding.what: Each of the three products.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the currency converted to.
rounding.step: After each multiplication, independently for the three images.

result.name: the low, the middle and the high image of the amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the amount computation and by the rounding-tolerance collapse.

edge_cases.case: The rate is undefined because the pair is in the exchange-line mode.
edge_cases.outcome: The three images are zero and no conversion is attempted.

edge_cases.case: The rate is exactly one.
edge_cases.outcome: The low and the high images may still differ from the middle by one rounding step when the two currencies have different numbers of decimal places.

edge_cases.case: The rate is very large.
edge_cases.outcome: The interval widens accordingly, which is what makes the collapse test tolerant where a large rate genuinely makes one unit of the source currency worth many units of the target.

worked_examples.description: Converting one thousand five hundred at the inverse of three quarters
worked_examples.narrative: The half-step of half a hundredth moves the product by one hundredth in each direction, giving the interval the collapse test compares against.

worked_examples.description: Converting one thousand five hundred at the inverse of four fifths
worked_examples.narrative: The same half-step at the lower rate gives an interval around one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five.

records.name: The matched amounts when the reconciliation currency is a foreign currency
records.purpose: Produces the three amounts of the matching when the two items meet in a foreign currency, converting the matched foreign amount back into the company currency on each side at that side's own rate.

operands.name: the amount to be matched
operands.constraints: the smaller of the two foreign residuals

operands.name: the rate stored in the debit map for the reconciliation currency
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the reconciliation currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the residual map of the debit item
operands.constraints: inverted before it is applied

operands.name: the rate stored in the credit map for the reconciliation currency
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the reconciliation currency per unit of the company currency
operands.source: the residual map of the credit item
operands.constraints: inverted before it is applied

operands.name: the running company-currency residual of the debit item
operands.constraints: caps the converted amount

operands.name: the running company-currency residual of the credit item
operands.constraints: caps the converted amount, after negation

preconditions.condition: The reconciliation currency is not the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The company-currency branch applies instead.

preconditions.condition: Neither rate is zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The interval helper returns zeros and the converted amount is zero.

procedure: When the pair is in the exchange-line mode, treat both rates as undefined; otherwise read each rate from its own map under the reconciliation currency.

Convert the matched foreign amount back into the company currency on the debit side by applying the inverse of the debit rate through the interval helper, and likewise on the credit side with the inverse of the credit rate.
Take the debit company-currency amount as the smaller of the middle image and the running company-currency residual of the debit item.
Take the credit company-currency amount as the smaller of the middle image and minus the running company-currency residual of the credit item.
Take the company-currency amount of the matching as the smaller of those two.
Apply the rounding-tolerance collapse when its four tests all hold.
Set each foreign amount of the matching to the company-currency amount when that side is in the company currency, and to the matched foreign amount otherwise.
records.formula:
debit_range  = range_after_rate( debit_currency  , company_currency , min_recon_amount , 1 ÷ debit_rate  )
credit_range = range_after_rate( credit_currency , company_currency , min_recon_amount , 1 ÷ credit_rate )

partial_debit_amount  = min( debit_range.middle  ,   remaining_debit_amount  )
partial_credit_amount = min( credit_range.middle , − remaining_credit_amount )
partial_amount        = min( partial_debit_amount , partial_credit_amount )

partial_debit_amount_currency  = partial_amount   when debit_currency  = company_currency , else min_recon_amount
partial_credit_amount_currency = partial_amount   when credit_currency = company_currency , else min_recon_amount

rounding.what: Each conversion back into the company currency, inside the interval helper.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: After each multiplication by the inverse rate, before the two minima are taken.

result.name: the company-currency amount and the two foreign amounts of the matching
result.unit_or_currency: company currency and the two item currencies
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Partial Reconciliation.

edge_cases.case: The two sides were booked at different rates.
edge_cases.outcome: The two middle images differ, the smaller is taken, and the difference becomes an exchange-difference line on the side that was booked higher.

edge_cases.case: The pair is in the exchange-line mode.
edge_cases.outcome: Both rates are undefined, both intervals are zero, and the company-currency amount is zero.

edge_cases.case: One side is in the company currency through the mimicking rule.
edge_cases.outcome: Its foreign amount of the matching is the company-currency amount, not the matched foreign amount.

edge_cases.case: The two sides differ only by rounding.
edge_cases.outcome: The collapse rule equalises them and prevents a spurious exchange difference on the second side.

worked_examples.description: The worked example of section four point six: one thousand five hundred matched at two different rates
worked_examples.narrative: The matching carries one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five in the company currency and one thousand five hundred on both foreign sides; the one hundred and twenty-five the invoice was booked above becomes an exchange difference.

records.name: The rounding-tolerance collapse of a foreign-currency matching
records.purpose: Recognises that the two sides of a foreign-currency matching are indistinguishable once rounding is taken into account, and equalises them so that no exchange difference is invented where none exists.

operands.name: the debit company-currency amount
operands.constraints: the middle image capped by the running residual

operands.name: the credit company-currency amount
operands.constraints: the same

operands.name: the low and the high image of the debit conversion
operands.constraints: one rounding step apart from the middle at most

operands.name: the low and the high image of the credit conversion
operands.constraints: the same

operands.name: the running company-currency residuals of both items
operands.constraints: used to rebuild the collapsed amount

preconditions.condition: All four comparisons hold at the precision of the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The two sides are genuinely different and an exchange difference is required.

procedure: Compare the debit company-currency amount with the high image of the credit conversion; the collapse requires that it is not greater.
Compare the debit company-currency amount with the low image of the credit conversion; the collapse requires that it is not smaller.
Compare the credit company-currency amount with the high image of the debit conversion; the collapse requires that it is not greater.
Compare the credit company-currency amount with the low image of the debit conversion; the collapse requires that it is not smaller.

When all four hold, set the company-currency amount of the matching to the smaller of the debit running residual and minus the credit running residual, and set both sides' company-currency amounts to that same value.
records.formula:
collapse holds when all four of
    compare( company , partial_debit_amount  , credit_range.high ) ≤ 0
    compare( company , partial_debit_amount  , credit_range.low  ) ≥ 0
    compare( company , partial_credit_amount , debit_range.high  ) ≤ 0
    compare( company , partial_credit_amount , debit_range.low   ) ≥ 0
then
    partial_amount        = min( remaining_debit_amount , − remaining_credit_amount )
    partial_debit_amount  = partial_amount
    partial_credit_amount = partial_amount

rounding.what: The four differences, inside the comparisons.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Inside each comparison, before its sign is read.

result.name: the equalised company-currency amounts of the matching
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Partial Reconciliation as the amount.

edge_cases.case: The two sides differ by more than the width of the intervals.
edge_cases.outcome: The first failing comparison ends the test and the exchange difference is computed normally.

edge_cases.case: The collapse applies but one side still carries a drift of one rounding step against its own residual.
edge_cases.outcome: A one-unit exchange line is still produced for that side; the collapse only prevents the second, spurious difference.

edge_cases.case: The collapse applies and both residuals are equal.
edge_cases.outcome: Both sides are exhausted and no exchange line at all is recorded.

worked_examples.description: The failing test of the worked example of section four point six
worked_examples.narrative: Two thousand is above the high image of one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five point zero one, so the first clause fails and the exchange difference of one hundred and twenty-five is genuine.

worked_examples.description: The collapse in action, with a transaction-date rate of nought point seven five zero zero zero two five
worked_examples.narrative: All four comparisons pass, so both sides are set to one thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine point nine nine; the debit still drifts by one hundredth against its own residual of two thousand, so a one-cent exchange line is produced, but no second difference appears on the credit side.

records.name: The exchange difference when the reconciliation currency is the company currency
records.purpose: Closes the foreign residual of a side that has just been fully matched in the company currency, so that an item whose company-currency amount is settled does not keep a foreign amount open.

operands.name: the running foreign residual of the debit item
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the debit item
operands.constraints: read only when the debit side is fully matched

operands.name: the debit foreign amount of the matching
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the debit item
operands.constraints: subtracted from the running foreign residual

operands.name: the running foreign residual of the credit item
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the credit item
operands.constraints: read only when the credit side is fully matched

operands.name: the credit foreign amount of the matching
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the credit item
operands.constraints: added to the running foreign residual

preconditions.condition: Neither the no exchange difference flag nor the no recursive exchange difference flag is set on the operation.
preconditions.otherwise: The whole step is skipped and no exchange line is recorded.

preconditions.condition: The side is fully matched.
preconditions.otherwise: That side's branch is not evaluated at all.

procedure: When the debit side is fully matched, subtract the debit foreign amount of the matching from the running foreign residual of the debit item; when the result is not zero in the debit currency, record an exchange line for the debit item fixing its foreign residual by that amount, and reduce the running foreign residual by it.

When the credit side is fully matched, add the credit foreign amount of the matching to the running foreign residual of the credit item; when the result is not zero in the credit currency, record an exchange line for the credit item fixing its foreign residual by that amount, and increase the running foreign residual by it.
When at least one exchange line was recorded, prepare an exchange-difference entry dated on the later of the two items' dates, and mark it to be posted when both items belong to posted entries.

rounding.what: Each difference, inside its zero test.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the debit currency and of the credit currency respectively.
rounding.step: Inside the zero test, before the line is recorded.

result.name: the foreign fixes recorded for the two items
result.stored_or_displayed: Turned into the two lines of an exchange-difference entry, the first of which is reconciled with the drifting item.

edge_cases.case: The side is fully matched and its foreign residual is already exactly consumed.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is zero, nothing is recorded, and no exchange entry is prepared for that side.

edge_cases.case: The side is not fully matched.
edge_cases.outcome: Its branch is not evaluated, so a partially matched item never receives a foreign fix in this branch.

edge_cases.case: The operation carries the no exchange difference flag.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole step is skipped, which is how the reconciliation of an exchange entry avoids producing another one.

worked_examples.description: The first iteration of the worked example of section three point eleven
worked_examples.narrative: The difference is zero, so nothing is recorded; the credit branch is not evaluated because the credit is not fully matched.

records.name: The exchange difference when the reconciliation currency is a foreign currency
records.purpose: Closes the company-currency drift of both sides of a foreign-currency matching, and keeps the ratio between an item's company residual and its foreign residual equal to the ratio it was booked at, even after a partial matching.

operands.name: the running company-currency residual of the debit item
operands.constraints: reduced by the drift when a line is recorded

operands.name: the running company-currency residual of the credit item
operands.constraints: the same

operands.name: the company-currency amount of the matching
operands.constraints: the smaller of the two converted amounts

operands.name: the debit company-currency amount
operands.constraints: used by the partial branch of the debit side

operands.name: the credit company-currency amount
operands.constraints: used by the partial branch of the credit side

preconditions.condition: Neither the no exchange difference flag nor the no recursive exchange difference flag is set on the operation.
preconditions.otherwise: The whole step is skipped.

preconditions.condition: The four branches are evaluated in the order written, the debit pair before the credit pair.
preconditions.otherwise: The running residuals would be read in the wrong state and the fixes would not close.

procedure: When the debit side is fully matched, take the drift as its running company-currency residual minus the company-currency amount of the matching; when that is not zero in the company currency, record an exchange line fixing the company residual of the debit item by it, reduce the running company-currency residual by it, and reduce the running foreign residual by it as well when the debit item is in the company currency.

When the debit side is not fully matched, take the drift as the debit company-currency amount minus the company-currency amount of the matching; when that is strictly positive in the company currency, record the same kind of line and apply the same two reductions.

When the credit side is fully matched, take the drift as its running company-currency residual plus the company-currency amount of the matching; when that is not zero in the company currency, record an exchange line fixing the company residual of the credit item by it, reduce the running company-currency residual by it, and reduce the running foreign residual by it as well when the credit item is in the company currency.

When the credit side is not fully matched, take the drift as the company-currency amount of the matching minus the credit company-currency amount; when that is strictly negative in the company currency, record the same kind of line and apply the same two reductions.
When at least one exchange line was recorded, prepare an exchange-difference entry dated on the later of the two items' dates, and mark it to be posted when both items belong to posted entries.

rounding.what: Each drift, inside its zero test or its comparison with zero.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Inside the test, before the line is recorded.

result.name: the company-currency fixes recorded for the two items
result.stored_or_displayed: Turned into the two lines of an exchange-difference entry, the first of which is reconciled with the drifting item.

edge_cases.case: A foreign invoice is only partially paid.
edge_cases.outcome: The two partial branches run, so the ratio between the company residual and the foreign residual of the invoice stays the ratio it was booked at and the invoice does not drift.

edge_cases.case: The partial drift on the debit side is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is recorded, because the partial branch requires a strictly positive drift.

edge_cases.case: The partial drift on the credit side is positive.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is recorded, because the partial branch requires a strictly negative drift.

edge_cases.case: The item is in the company currency through the mimicking rule.
edge_cases.outcome: The fix is applied to both its running residuals, so the two stay in step.

worked_examples.description: The worked example of section four point six
worked_examples.narrative: The invoice was booked one hundred and twenty-five above what the bank actually converted, so a company-currency fix of one hundred and twenty-five is recorded for the invoice item and nothing for the transaction item.

records.name: Updating the running residuals and producing the matching
records.purpose: Applies the computed amounts to the two running item states and states exactly which values the Partial Reconciliation carries.

operands.name: the company-currency amount of the matching
operands.constraints: always positive

operands.name: the debit foreign amount of the matching
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the debit item
operands.constraints: always positive

operands.name: the credit foreign amount of the matching
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the credit item
operands.constraints: always positive

operands.name: the four running residuals of the pair
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency and the two item currencies
operands.constraints: updated in place

preconditions.condition: The exchange-difference step has already adjusted the running residuals.
preconditions.otherwise: The residuals would be reduced twice for the same drift.

procedure: Subtract the company-currency amount of the matching from the running company-currency residual of the debit item.
Add the company-currency amount of the matching to the running company-currency residual of the credit item.
Subtract the debit foreign amount of the matching from the running foreign residual of the debit item.
Add the credit foreign amount of the matching to the running foreign residual of the credit item.
Record the matching with its company-currency amount, its debit foreign amount, its credit foreign amount, the debit item and the credit item.
records.formula:
remaining_debit_amount           ← remaining_debit_amount           − partial_amount
remaining_credit_amount          ← remaining_credit_amount          + partial_amount
remaining_debit_amount_currency  ← remaining_debit_amount_currency  − partial_debit_amount_currency
remaining_credit_amount_currency ← remaining_credit_amount_currency + partial_credit_amount_currency

the matching carries : amount = partial_amount ; debit foreign amount = partial_debit_amount_currency ; credit foreign amount = partial_credit_amount_currency ; the debit item ; the credit item

rounding.what: Nothing here; all three amounts were rounded when they were computed.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the values of the Partial Reconciliation and the updated running residuals
result.unit_or_currency: company currency and the two item currencies
result.stored_or_displayed: The three amounts and the two item references are stored on the Partial Reconciliation; the running residuals live only for the duration of the operation and are recomputed from the stored matchings afterwards.

edge_cases.case: The three amounts are all zero.
edge_cases.outcome: No matching is recorded at all, because the earlier steps reported the sides exhausted.

edge_cases.case: The debit side is in the company currency and the credit side is not.
edge_cases.outcome: The two foreign amounts of the matching differ, and each side's residual is reduced by its own.

edge_cases.case: The matching is later deleted.
edge_cases.outcome: The residuals are recomputed from the surviving matchings, so the in-place updates of this step are never relied on after the operation.

worked_examples.description: The second iteration of the worked example of section three point eleven
worked_examples.narrative: The payment is exhausted and the second invoice keeps one hundred.

records.name: The exhaustion test of one side of a pair
records.purpose: Tells the pairing loop whether a side has nothing left at all, which is what makes the loop advance to the next item of that queue and what marks the item fully reconciled for the operation.

operands.name: the running company-currency residual of the side
operands.constraints: tested for zero in the company currency

operands.name: the running foreign residual of the side
operands.constraints: tested for zero in that currency

preconditions.condition: The residuals have already been updated by the matching just produced.
preconditions.otherwise: The test would read the state before the matching and never report exhaustion.

procedure: Test the running foreign residual of the side for zero at the precision of the currency of the item.
Test the running company-currency residual of the side for zero at the precision of the company currency.
Report the side exhausted only when both tests answer true.
records.formula:
debit state is exhausted  = is_zero( debit_currency  , remaining_debit_amount_currency  ) AND is_zero( company , remaining_debit_amount  )
credit state is exhausted = is_zero( credit_currency , remaining_credit_amount_currency ) AND is_zero( company , remaining_credit_amount )

rounding.what: Each residual, inside its zero test.
rounding.precision: The currency of the item for one test, the company currency for the other.
rounding.step: Inside each zero test.

result.name: the two exhaustion flags
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; they drive the pairing loop and the set of items marked fully reconciled for the operation.

edge_cases.case: The company-currency residual is zero but a foreign residual remains.
edge_cases.outcome: The side is not exhausted; the loop keeps it as the current state and matches it again.

edge_cases.case: A foreign residual of a fraction of a rounding step remains.
edge_cases.outcome: It rounds to zero and the side counts as exhausted.

edge_cases.case: The exchange-difference step has just closed the drift.
edge_cases.outcome: Both residuals are zero and the side is exhausted in the same iteration.

worked_examples.description: The invoice item after its full matching
worked_examples.narrative: Both residuals are zero, so the item is marked fully reconciled for this operation and the loop takes the next debit state.

worked_examples.description: The second invoice after a partial matching
worked_examples.narrative: One hundred is left in both currencies, so the item stays the current debit state, though the loop stops because the credit queue is empty.

records.name: End-to-end example: a payment of one thousand against invoices of six hundred and five hundred
records.purpose: Carries one single-currency reconciliation through every step of the matching, and shows why the sort order of the plan decides which document is settled in full.

operands.name: the receivable item of the first invoice
operands.source: the first customer invoice, due on the tenth of March
operands.constraints: balance and residual of plus six hundred

operands.name: the receivable item of the second invoice
operands.source: the second customer invoice, due on the twentieth of March
operands.constraints: balance and residual of plus five hundred

operands.name: the counterpart item of the payment
operands.source: the Payment dated the twenty-fifth of March
operands.constraints: balance and residual of minus one thousand

preconditions.condition: The three items sit on the same receivable account, in the same company, in the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The eligibility check refuses the reconciliation.

preconditions.condition: The plan is a single leaf holding the three items, as the register-payment flow builds it.
preconditions.otherwise: The order of settlement changes.

procedure: Sort the leaf by due date, then currency, then foreign amount, then balance, giving the first invoice, the second invoice and then the payment.
Split by currency: only one currency is present, so no sub-node is created.
Build the debit queue from the two invoice items and the credit queue from the payment item.

First iteration: the residual maps hold only the company currency, so the reconciliation currency is the company currency; six hundred against one thousand gives a comparison of minus one, the debit fully matched and a matched amount of six hundred; both rates are one, so both foreign amounts of the matching are six hundred; the exchange difference of the debit side is zero and the credit branch is not evaluated.
Record the first matching, reduce the first invoice to zero and the payment to minus four hundred, and mark the first invoice exhausted.
Second iteration: five hundred against four hundred gives a comparison of plus one, the credit fully matched and a matched amount of four hundred.
Record the second matching, reduce the second invoice to one hundred and the payment to zero, and mark the payment exhausted.
The credit queue is now empty, so the loop stops.
All three items belong to one connected matching group, so they share one partial matching number; no full reconciliation is created because the second invoice still carries one hundred.
records.formula:
iteration one : comparison = compare( company , 600.00 , 1000.00 ) = −1 ; min_recon_amount = 600.00 ; partial_amount = 600.00 ; partial_debit_amount_currency = min( round_to( company , 1 × 600.00 ) , 600.00 ) = 600.00 ; partial_credit_amount_currency = min( round_to( company , 1 × 600.00 ) , 1000.00 ) = 600.00 ; debit_exchange = 600.00 − 600.00 = 0.00
iteration two : comparison = compare( company , 500.00 , 400.00 ) = +1 ; min_recon_amount = 400.00 ; partial_amount = 400.00

rounding.what: Each converted foreign amount and each comparison.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency, one hundredth.
rounding.step: Inside the conversions of step six and inside each comparison; no value in this example is actually moved by rounding.

result.name: two Partial Reconciliations and the residuals of the three items
result.stored_or_displayed: The matchings are stored; the residuals are recomputed onto the three Journal Items and drive the payment states of the two documents.

edge_cases.case: The items are sorted by balance instead of by due date.
edge_cases.outcome: The payment would settle the second invoice first and leave one hundred on the first, which is why the sort key of the plan is part of the specification.

edge_cases.case: The liquidity side of the Payment has not yet met a bank transaction.
edge_cases.outcome: The Payment stays in the state that says it is being processed rather than paid.

worked_examples.description: The full walkthrough as the document states it
worked_examples.narrative: Two matchings of six hundred and four hundred settle the first invoice entirely and the second in part; no exchange entry and no full-reconciliation marker are produced.

records.name: When an exchange-difference entry is prepared
records.purpose: States the input the preparation reads: the list of drifting items and, for each, the amount to remove from one of its two residuals.

operands.name: the pairs of a drifting item and its fix
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency or the currency of the item
operands.source: the exchange-difference step of the single-pair computation
operands.constraints: a fix is either a company-currency amount or a foreign-currency amount, never both

preconditions.condition: At least one pair was collected for the matching.
preconditions.otherwise: No entry is prepared for that matching.

procedure: Collect, for one matching, the list of pairs made of a drifting item and the fix recorded for it.
Read each fix as either a company-currency amount to remove from the item's company residual, or a foreign-currency amount to remove from its foreign residual.
Prepare one entry from that list.
records.formula:
fixes = the list of ( item , fix ) pairs recorded by step 8 for one matching
a fix is a company-currency amount to remove from the item's company residual , or a foreign-currency amount to remove from its foreign residual

rounding.what: Nothing; each fix was rounded when it was recorded.
rounding.precision: The company currency or the currency of the item, according to the kind of fix.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Earlier, inside the exchange-difference step.

result.name: the prepared exchange-difference entry, or nothing
result.stored_or_displayed: Created in the batch of phase four and linked back to the matching that produced it.

edge_cases.case: The list is empty.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is prepared, which is also the guard that stops the matching of an exchange entry from producing another one.

edge_cases.case: Both items of one matching drifted.
edge_cases.outcome: The list holds two pairs and the entry carries four lines, two per item.

worked_examples.description: The single drift of the worked example of section four point six

fixes.item: the receivable item of the invoice

worked_examples.narrative: One drifting item yields one entry of two lines.

records.name: The date and the header of an exchange-difference entry
records.purpose: Fixes the company, the journal, the date and the numbering of the entry that books a rate difference, the date being the only part of the header that is arithmetic.

operands.name: the supplied exchange date
operands.source: the single-pair computation, which passes the later of the two matched items' dates
operands.constraints: the starting point of the date computation

operands.name: the accounting date rule of the exchange journal
operands.constraints: pushes a date forward past any lock date

operands.name: the date of each processed item
operands.constraints: the running date is raised to each of them

operands.name: the company of the invoice-like entries among the items
operands.constraints: chosen first

preconditions.condition: A company resolves, from the invoice-like entries, from the items, or from the caller.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing is prepared at all.

preconditions.condition: The company has an exchange-difference journal.
preconditions.otherwise: The preparation still proceeds and the creation later fails with "You have to configure the 'Exchange Gain or Loss Journal' in your company settings, to manage automatically the booking of accounting entries related to differences between exchange rates."

procedure: Take the company of the invoice-like entries among the items when there are any, otherwise the company of the items, otherwise the company passed explicitly; when none resolves, prepare nothing.
Take the journal as the exchange-difference journal of that company.

Start the date at the accounting date the journal computes for the supplied exchange date, that is the supplied date pushed forward past any lock date; when there is no journal at all, start at the lowest representable date.
Raise the date to the maximum of itself and the date of each processed item.
Set the entry type to a plain entry, force its number so that numbering happens at posting time, and flag it as always tax-exigible.
records.formula:
date = accounting_date_of_the_exchange_journal( supplied exchange date )
for each processed item : date ← max( date , the item's date )

rounding.what: Nothing; the header carries dates and references.
rounding.step: The lock-date correction is applied first, the raising to the item dates after.

result.name: the header of the exchange-difference entry
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Entry.

edge_cases.case: The supplied exchange date falls before a lock date.
edge_cases.outcome: The accounting date rule pushes it past that lock date before the item dates are considered.

edge_cases.case: A processed item is dated after the corrected date.
edge_cases.outcome: The entry takes that later date, so the entry is never dated before the item it corrects.

edge_cases.case: There is no exchange journal at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The date starts at the lowest representable date and the creation later fails with the message about the exchange journal.

worked_examples.description: An invoice dated the first of March and a transaction dated the tenth of March, with no lock date
worked_examples.narrative: The later of the two item dates is already the supplied date, and no lock date moves it.

records.name: The two lines produced for one drifting item
records.purpose: Turns one fix into the pair of journal items that cancels the drift on the item's own account and books the gain or the loss, and states which of the two exchange accounts is chosen.

operands.name: the fix recorded for the item
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency or the currency of the item
operands.constraints: positive for a loss, negative or zero for a gain

operands.name: the currency of the item
operands.constraints: decides whether a company-currency fix also carries a foreign amount

operands.name: the account of the item
operands.constraints: the account of the first line

operands.name: the expense exchange-difference account of the company
operands.constraints: chosen when the fix is strictly positive

operands.name: the income exchange-difference account of the company
operands.constraints: chosen when the fix is zero or negative

operands.name: the running sequence of the lines
operands.constraints: starts at zero and increases by two for each pair

preconditions.condition: A company-currency fix is not zero in the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The pair is skipped and no line is produced for that item.

preconditions.condition: A foreign-currency fix is not zero in the currency of the item.
preconditions.otherwise: The pair is skipped in the same way.

procedure: For a company-currency fix, set the residual amount to the fix and the residual foreign amount to the fix when the item is in the company currency and to zero otherwise; skip the pair when the fix is zero in the company currency.
For a foreign-currency fix, set the residual amount to zero and the residual foreign amount to the fix; skip the pair when the fix is zero in the currency of the item.
Choose the expense exchange-difference account of the company when the fix is strictly positive, and the income exchange-difference account otherwise.

Emit a first line, at the running sequence, on the item's own account, carrying the residual amount as a credit when it is positive and as a debit of its absolute value when it is negative, a foreign amount of minus the residual foreign amount, the item's counterparty, the item's currency, the item's full reconciliation, and the item itself recorded in the reconciled lines relation.

Emit a second line, at the running sequence plus one, on the chosen exchange account, carrying the residual amount as a debit when it is positive and as a credit of its absolute value when it is negative, a foreign amount of the residual foreign amount, the item's counterparty, the item's currency and, when the caller supplied one, the analytic distribution.
Label both lines "Currency exchange rate difference".
Increase the running sequence by two and move on to the next pair.
records.formula:
if the fix is a company-currency amount R :
    amount_residual = R ; amount_residual_currency = R when the item's currency is the company currency , else 0 ; skip when is_zero( company , R )
if the fix is a foreign-currency amount R :
    amount_residual = 0 ; amount_residual_currency = R ; skip when is_zero( item currency , R )

exchange_account = the company's EXPENSE exchange-difference account when R > 0
                 = the company's INCOME  exchange-difference account when R ≤ 0

first line  : the item's own account , credit amount_residual when positive else debit its absolute value , foreign amount = − amount_residual_currency
second line : the exchange account , debit amount_residual when positive else credit its absolute value , foreign amount = amount_residual_currency

rounding.what: Nothing here; the fix was rounded when it was recorded.
rounding.precision: The company currency for a company-currency fix, the currency of the item for a foreign fix.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Earlier, inside the exchange-difference step.

result.name: the two journal items of the fix
result.unit_or_currency: company currency, with a foreign amount in the currency of the item
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the exchange-difference entry; writing the reconciled lines relation of the first line reconciles it with the drifting item at once.

edge_cases.case: The fix is exactly zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The pair is skipped and no lines are produced, which keeps a zero drift from creating an empty entry.

edge_cases.case: The fix is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The income exchange-difference account is used and the two sides swap: the item's own account is debited and the exchange account credited.

edge_cases.case: A company-currency fix on an item that carries a foreign currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The foreign amount of both lines is zero, so only the company-currency drift is corrected.

edge_cases.case: Two drifting items in one entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The second pair starts at sequence two, so the four lines keep the order the fixes were recorded in.

worked_examples.description: A company-currency fix of one hundred and twenty-five on a receivable item held in a foreign currency

first_line.account: the receivable account of the invoice

worked_examples.narrative: The receivable is credited by one hundred and twenty-five, which closes the invoice, and the same amount is debited to the exchange loss account.

records.name: Creating and posting the exchange-difference entries
records.purpose: States the guards that run before the prepared entries are written, the exact refusal of each, and the two flags that keep the creation from cascading.

operands.name: the list of prepared entries
operands.constraints: an empty list stops the whole step

operands.name: the journal of each prepared entry
operands.constraints: must not be empty

operands.name: the expense exchange-difference account of each company used
operands.constraints: must be set

operands.name: the income exchange-difference account of each company used
operands.constraints: must be set

operands.name: whether both matched items belonged to posted entries
operands.constraints: decides whether the new entry is posted

preconditions.condition: The list of prepared entries is not empty.
preconditions.otherwise: The step stops at once, which also prevents the matching of an exchange entry from recursively producing another one.

procedure: When the list of prepared entries is empty, stop.

For each prepared entry with no journal, refuse with "You have to configure the 'Exchange Gain or Loss Journal' in your company settings, to manage automatically the booking of accounting entries related to differences between exchange rates."

For each journal used, when its company has no expense exchange account, refuse with "You should configure the 'Loss Exchange Rate Account' in your company settings, to manage automatically the booking of accounting entries related to differences between exchange rates."

For each journal used, when its company has no income exchange account, refuse with "You should configure the 'Gain Exchange Rate Account' in your company settings, to manage automatically the booking of accounting entries related to differences between exchange rates."
Create all the entries at once, with the no exchange difference flag set so that the reconciliation they trigger does not cascade.
Post the entries whose two matched items both belonged to posted entries, with analytic validation switched off.
records.formula:
if the prepared list is empty : stop
for each entry : journal must not be empty
for each journal used : its company must have both an expense and an income exchange-difference account
create all entries in one batch , with the no exchange difference flag set
post those whose two matched items both belonged to posted entries

rounding.what: Nothing; the amounts are already fixed.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the created and possibly posted exchange-difference entries
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as Journal Entries and linked to the matchings that produced them.

edge_cases.case: One of the two matched items belongs to a draft entry.
edge_cases.outcome: The exchange entry is created but left in draft.

edge_cases.case: The reconciliation triggered by the reconciled lines relation of the first line would itself drift.
edge_cases.outcome: The no exchange difference flag suppresses it, so the creation never cascades.

edge_cases.case: The company has an exchange journal but only one of the two exchange accounts.
edge_cases.outcome: The corresponding message is raised even when the drift would only have used the other account.

worked_examples.description: One prepared entry on a company that is fully configured, both matched items posted
worked_examples.narrative: The entry is created and posted, and the reconciliation it triggers produces no further exchange entry because the flag is set.

records.name: Reversing an exchange-difference entry when a matching is deleted
records.purpose: States what happens to the derived entry when the matching that produced it is removed, and how the reversal is dated so that it never falls in a locked period.

operands.name: the state of the exchange-difference entry
operands.constraints: a draft entry is deleted, a posted entry is reversed

operands.name: the date of the entry
operands.constraints: the preferred date of the reversal

operands.name: the lock dates the entry date would violate
operands.constraints: the latest of them pushes the reversal date

operands.name: the number of the entry
operands.constraints: reproduced inside the reference of the reversal

preconditions.condition: The matching that produced the entry is being deleted.
preconditions.otherwise: Nothing happens to the entry.

procedure: Collect the derived entries of the matchings being deleted and split them into those still in draft and those posted.
Delete the draft entries outright.
For each posted entry, take its own date as the reversal date; when that date violates one or more lock dates, take the day after the latest of them instead.
Reverse each posted entry with the cancel flag, so that the original and the reversal are matched with each other and both are neutralised.
Give each reversal the reference "Reversal of: *the number of the original entry*".
records.formula:
reversal_date = the original entry's own date
              = the day after the latest lock date it violates , when it violates one or more
reference     = "Reversal of: " ‖ the original entry's number

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule moves a date.
rounding.step: Before the reversal is created.

result.name: the deletion or the reversal of the derived entry
result.stored_or_displayed: The reversal is stored as a Journal Entry matched with the original.

edge_cases.case: The entry is still in draft.
edge_cases.outcome: It is deleted and no reversal is written at all.

edge_cases.case: The entry's own date falls inside a locked period.
edge_cases.outcome: The reversal is dated on the day after the latest violated lock date.

edge_cases.case: The matched items themselves.
edge_cases.outcome: They are never touched: deleting a matching changes no debit, no credit and no foreign amount, only the derived residuals.

worked_examples.description: A posted exchange entry dated the tenth of March, with a lock date on the thirty-first of March
worked_examples.narrative: The original date is locked, so the reversal lands on the day after the lock date and carries the reference naming the original entry.

records.name: End-to-end example: a bank transaction of one thousand five hundred matched to a foreign-currency invoice at a different rate
records.purpose: Carries one cross-rate settlement through the transaction's own entry, the matching, the exchange difference and the resulting residuals, and shows the collapse rule deciding whether a second difference appears.

operands.name: the receivable item of the invoice
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency, with a foreign amount in the journal currency
operands.constraints: balance of plus two thousand and foreign amount of plus one thousand five hundred, so an accounting rate of three quarters

operands.name: the counterpart item of the bank transaction
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency, with a foreign amount in the journal currency
operands.constraints: balance of minus one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five and foreign amount of minus one thousand five hundred, so an accounting rate of four fifths

operands.name: the invoice-date rate
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the journal currency per unit of the company currency
operands.constraints: three quarters, so one thousand five hundred of the journal currency is worth two thousand of the company currency

operands.name: the transaction-date rate
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the journal currency per unit of the company currency
operands.constraints: four fifths, so one thousand five hundred of the journal currency is worth one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five of the company currency

preconditions.condition: The counterpart item of the transaction has been moved onto the receivable account of the counterparty by the bank-reconciliation step.
preconditions.otherwise: The two items sit on different accounts and the eligibility check refuses the matching.

preconditions.condition: The company has an exchange journal and both exchange accounts.
preconditions.otherwise: The creation of the exchange entry fails with the corresponding message.

procedure: Build the transaction's own entry: the liquidity line debits one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five of the company currency with a foreign amount of plus one thousand five hundred, and the suspense line credits the same with a foreign amount of minus one thousand five hundred.

Build the two residual maps: the invoice offers two thousand in the company currency at a rate of one and one thousand five hundred in its own currency at three quarters; the transaction offers minus one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five at a rate of one and minus one thousand five hundred at four fifths.
Choose the reconciliation currency: the debit currency differs from the company currency and appears in both maps, so it is the journal currency.
Read the two amounts to match: one thousand five hundred on each side; the pair is not in the exchange-line mode because both maps hold an entry for their own currency.
Compare them: equal, so both sides are fully matched and the matched foreign amount is one thousand five hundred.

Convert back to the company currency through the interval helper on each side, giving a debit interval around two thousand and a credit interval around one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five; take the smaller of the two middles as the company-currency amount of the matching.
Test the collapse: the first clause fails because two thousand is above one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five point zero one, so the difference is genuine.
Compute the exchange differences: the debit drifts by one hundred and twenty-five and the credit by nothing.

Update the residuals, which all reach zero, and write the exchange entry crediting the receivable account by one hundred and twenty-five and debiting the expense exchange-difference account by the same.
records.formula:
debit_range  = range_after_rate( journal currency , company currency , 1500.00 , 1 ÷ 0.75 ) = ( 1999.99 , 2000.00 , 2000.01 )
credit_range = range_after_rate( journal currency , company currency , 1500.00 , 1 ÷ 0.80 ) = ( 1874.99 , 1875.00 , 1875.01 )
partial_debit_amount  = min( 2000.00 , 2000.00 ) = 2000.00
partial_credit_amount = min( 1875.00 , 1875.00 ) = 1875.00
partial_amount        = min( 2000.00 , 1875.00 ) = 1875.00
debit_exchange  = 2000.00 − 1875.00 = 125.00
credit_exchange = −1875.00 + 1875.00 = 0.00

rounding.what: The three images of each interval, and each comparison.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency, one hundredth.
rounding.step: Inside the interval helper, after each multiplication by the inverse rate.

result.name: one Partial Reconciliation, one exchange-difference entry and four zero residuals
result.unit_or_currency: company currency and the journal currency
result.stored_or_displayed: The matching and the entry are stored; the invoice reaches a residual of zero in both currencies and is fully paid.

edge_cases.case: The transaction-date rate is close enough to the invoice-date rate that the two intervals overlap.
edge_cases.outcome: The collapse applies and the second, spurious difference on the credit side is suppressed, although a one-hundredth difference may still be produced on the debit side.

edge_cases.case: The counterpart item is left on the suspense account.
edge_cases.outcome: The two items sit on different accounts and the matching is refused.

worked_examples.description: The settlement as the document states it

exchange_entry.account: the receivable account of the customer

worked_examples.narrative: The invoice was booked at two thousand and the bank converted at one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five, so one hundred and twenty-five lands in the exchange loss account and the invoice closes exactly.

worked_examples.description: The same settlement with a transaction-date rate of nought point seven five zero zero zero two five
worked_examples.narrative: All four collapse comparisons pass, so both sides settle at one thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine point nine nine; the debit still drifts by one hundredth against its own residual, so a one-cent exchange line is produced, but the credit side produces none.

records.name: The connected group of a set of items
records.purpose: Widens a set of matched items to everything that shares their matching numbers, which is the population the completeness test is applied to.

operands.name: the matching numbers of the items of the set
operands.constraints: empty numbers are ignored

operands.name: every journal item in the database carrying one of those numbers
operands.source: the whole ledger, read with elevated privileges
operands.constraints: grouped by number

preconditions.condition: At least one item of the set carries a non-empty matching number.
preconditions.otherwise: The group is the original set alone.

procedure: Collect the distinct non-empty matching numbers of the items of the set.
Read every journal item in the ledger that carries one of those numbers, grouped by number, with elevated privileges so that a number spanning several companies is read in full.
Take the group as the original set plus every item read, ignoring the numbers that begin with the letter that marks an import placeholder, because such a placeholder is not a real matching yet.
records.formula:
numbers = the distinct non-empty matching numbers of the items of the set , excluding those beginning with the letter I
group   = the original set ∪ every journal item of the ledger carrying one of those numbers

rounding.what: Nothing; the step reads texts and item references.
rounding.step: After the matchings have been created and the numbers recomputed.

result.name: the connected group of the set
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the completeness test.

edge_cases.case: An item carries an import placeholder number.
edge_cases.outcome: That number is ignored and pulls no other item into the group.

edge_cases.case: The group spans several companies.
edge_cases.outcome: The elevated read still returns every item, so a group is never closed on a partial view.

edge_cases.case: No item carries a number.
edge_cases.outcome: The group is the set itself, which happens on the very first matching before the numbers are recomputed.

worked_examples.description: The third payment of the chain of section five point four

set: the counterpart item of the third payment

group: the counterpart item of the first payment
the counterpart item of the second payment
the counterpart item of the third payment

worked_examples.narrative: The invoice's partial number pulls the two earlier payments back into the group, which is what lets the completeness test see the whole settlement.

records.name: Whether a connected group is fully settled
records.purpose: Decides whether the group may receive a full-reconciliation marker, using the company-currency residual or the item-currency residual according to whether the group mixes currencies.

operands.name: the items of the connected group
operands.constraints: every one of them must count as settled

operands.name: the currencies of the items of the group
operands.constraints: more than one distinct currency switches the test to the company-currency residual

operands.name: the reconciled flag of each item
operands.constraints: settles the item on its own

operands.name: the number of matchings of each item
operands.constraints: an item with none never counts as settled

operands.name: the two residuals of each item
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the item
operands.constraints: one of the two is tested according to the currency mix

preconditions.condition: The item has not already been assigned to a group by an earlier node of this same operation.
preconditions.otherwise: It is skipped, because its group has already been decided.

procedure: For each node of the plan, and for each of its items not already assigned to a group, compute the connected group of the node's items.
Read whether the group mixes currencies, that is whether its items carry more than one distinct currency.
Count an item of the group as settled when it is flagged reconciled.
Otherwise count it as settled when it has at least one matching and, when the group mixes currencies, its company-currency residual is zero, or, when it does not, its item-currency residual is zero.
Never count an item with no matching at all as settled, even when both its residuals are zero, which is the case of an exchange-difference line that carries a foreign amount but no balance.
Declare the group fully reconciled exactly when every one of its items counts as settled.
records.formula:
has_multiple_currencies = the group's items carry more than one distinct currency
settled( item ) = item is flagged reconciled
              OR ( item has at least one matching AND ( is_zero( company , amount_residual ) when has_multiple_currencies , else is_zero( item currency , amount_residual_currency ) ) )
group is fully reconciled ⟺ every item of the group is settled

rounding.what: Each residual, inside its zero test.
rounding.precision: The company currency or the currency of the item, according to the currency mix.
rounding.step: Inside each zero test.

result.name: whether the group is fully reconciled
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides whether a Full Reconciliation is created.

edge_cases.case: One item of the group still carries a residual.
edge_cases.outcome: The group is not complete and no marker is created.

edge_cases.case: An exchange-difference line of the group has a foreign amount but no matching.
edge_cases.outcome: It never counts as settled, so it cannot close the group by itself.

edge_cases.case: The group mixes currencies.
edge_cases.outcome: The company-currency residual is the one tested, because the item-currency residuals of two different currencies cannot be compared.

edge_cases.case: An item is flagged reconciled but has no matching.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag alone settles it, because the flag is only ever true when both residuals are zero.

worked_examples.description: The group after the third payment of section five point four
worked_examples.narrative: Every item has at least one matching and a zero residual, so the group is complete and one marker is created.

worked_examples.description: The same group after the first payment only
worked_examples.narrative: The invoice still carries seven hundred, so no marker is created.

records.name: Creating the full-reconciliation marker
records.purpose: Records that a group has closed, by linking every matching and every item of the group to one marker and rewriting their matching numbers.

operands.name: the matchings of the items of the group
operands.constraints: all of them are linked

operands.name: the items of the group
operands.constraints: all of them are linked

preconditions.condition: The group is fully reconciled.
preconditions.otherwise: No marker is created.

procedure: Create one Full Reconciliation for the group.
Link to it every matching of the group's items and every item of the group.
Write the marker's identifier onto all of them.
Recompute the matching numbers, which turns the partial number of every item of the group into the decimal text of the marker's identifier.
records.formula:
one Full Reconciliation per fully reconciled group
it links every matching of the group's items and every item of the group
afterwards every item's matching number = the decimal text of the marker's identifier

rounding.what: Nothing; the step writes references and a text.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the Full Reconciliation and the rewritten matching numbers
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the marker, on each matching and on each item.

edge_cases.case: The marker is later deleted.
edge_cases.outcome: The pointer on each item is cleared and the matching numbers are recomputed, becoming empty or a partial number again.

edge_cases.case: One matching of the group is deleted.
edge_cases.outcome: The marker is deleted first, and only then are the numbers recomputed from the surviving matchings.

worked_examples.description: The marker created on the third day of the chain of section five point four
worked_examples.narrative: The four items and the three matchings are linked to marker forty-two, and every item's number becomes the plain text of that identifier.

records.name: End-to-end example: three partial payments reaching full reconciliation
records.purpose: Follows one invoice through three separate reconciliations, showing when the partial number is assigned, when the group closes, and what undoing the last matching restores.

operands.name: the receivable item of the invoice
operands.constraints: balance of plus one thousand

operands.name: the counterpart items of the three payments
operands.source: three Payments registered on three different days
operands.constraints: balances of minus three hundred, minus three hundred and minus four hundred

preconditions.condition: All four items sit on the same receivable account of the same company.
preconditions.otherwise: The eligibility check refuses each reconciliation.

preconditions.condition: The invoice is not reconciled when the second and the third payments arrive.
preconditions.otherwise: The narrowing rule of the eligibility check would refuse the request.

procedure: On the first day, match the invoice against the first payment: the comparison of one thousand with three hundred is plus one, so the credit is fully matched and the matched amount is three hundred; the invoice keeps seven hundred and the payment reaches zero.

Compute the connected group of the two items; the invoice is not settled, so no marker is created, and both items receive the partial number formed of the letter that marks a partial number followed by the identifier of the first matching.

On the second day, match the invoice against the second payment: the invoice carries the partial number but is not reconciled, so the narrowing rule keeps it and the check passes; the matched amount is three hundred and the invoice falls to four hundred.

Compute the connected group: the invoice's number pulls the first payment back in, so the group is the invoice and the two payments; the invoice still carries four hundred, so no marker is created and the number stays the same, because the two matchings land in one component whose number is the smallest matching identifier.

On the third day, match the invoice against the third payment: the comparison of four hundred with four hundred is zero, both sides are fully matched, the matched amount is four hundred and both residuals reach zero.

Compute the connected group: the invoice's number pulls both earlier payments in, so the group is the invoice and the three payments; every one of them has at least one matching and a zero residual, so the group is complete.
Create one Full Reconciliation linking the three matchings and the four items; every item's matching number becomes the decimal text of the marker's identifier and the partial number disappears.

To undo the third day, delete the third matching: the marker is deleted first, then the numbers are recomputed, so the invoice and the first two payments return to the partial number while the third payment, now without any matching, ends with no number at all.
records.formula:
day one   : compare( company , 1000.00 , 300.00 ) = +1 ; partial_amount = 300.00 ; invoice residual 700.00
day two   : partial_amount = 300.00 ; invoice residual 400.00
day three : compare( company , 400.00 , 400.00 ) = 0 ; partial_amount = 400.00 ; invoice residual 0.00
component number = the smallest matching identifier of the component

rounding.what: Each comparison of two residuals.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Inside each comparison; no amount of this example is moved by rounding.

result.name: three matchings, one Full Reconciliation and the payment states of the invoice
result.stored_or_displayed: The matchings and the marker are stored; the invoice's payment state moves from partially paid to paid.

edge_cases.case: The third matching is deleted.
edge_cases.outcome: The marker is deleted, the invoice and the first two payments return to the partial number, the third payment ends with no number and the invoice returns to partially paid with a residual of four hundred.

edge_cases.case: The payments' own liquidity sides are still outstanding.
edge_cases.outcome: The invoice reaches the state that says the payment is still clearing rather than paid.

worked_examples.description: The three days as the document states them, with the first matching identified as seventeen and the marker as forty-two
worked_examples.narrative: The partial number survives the second day because both matchings fall in one component whose number is the smallest matching identifier, and it is replaced by the marker's identifier on the third day.

worked_examples.description: Undoing the third day
worked_examples.narrative: The surviving matchings still form one component whose smallest identifier is seventeen, and the payment that lost its only matching keeps no number.

records.name: Recomputing the matching number of a connected closure
records.purpose: Assigns every item that takes part in a matching a stable number naming the component it belongs to, so that a group can be recognised without walking the matching graph every time.

operands.name: the input set of journal items
operands.source: the creation or the deletion of matchings
operands.constraints: extended to its connected closure before anything else

operands.name: every matching touching an item of the closure
operands.constraints: sorted by ascending identifier

operands.name: the Full Reconciliation of each item, when it has one
operands.constraints: its identifier becomes the number, written as decimal text

preconditions.condition: The closure has been computed through the matching numbers.
preconditions.otherwise: Items linked only through an older matching would be left with a stale number.

procedure: Extend the input set to its connected closure through the matching numbers.
Collect every matching that touches an item of the closure, on either side.
Sort those matchings by ascending identifier.
Maintain two indexes: one from a component number to the list of its item identifiers, and one from an item identifier to its component number.
For each matching in order, look up the numbers currently assigned to its debit item and to its credit item.

When both are known and different, merge the two components: the surviving number is the smaller of the two, every item of the larger-numbered component is re-pointed at the smaller number and its item list is appended to the smaller one's.
When both are known and equal, do nothing.
When only the debit is known, add the credit item to that component; when only the credit is known, add the debit item to that component.
When neither is known, start a new component whose number is this matching's own identifier, containing both items.

Write the result: for an item that has a Full Reconciliation, the matching number is the decimal text of the marker's identifier; otherwise it is the letter that marks a partial number followed by the component number.
Clear the matching number of any item of the closure that received no component at all.
records.formula:
component number = the smallest matching identifier of the component
matching_number( item ) = the decimal text of the Full Reconciliation identifier , when the item has one
                        = "P" ‖ the component number , when the item belongs to a component and has no marker
                        = empty , when the item takes part in no matching

rounding.what: Nothing; the algorithm produces a text.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the matching number of each item of the closure
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on each Journal Item and displayed in the ledger views.

edge_cases.case: Two components are joined by a new matching.
edge_cases.outcome: The smaller number survives, so the number of a group is stable as long as its oldest matching survives.

edge_cases.case: An item of the closure lost its last matching.
edge_cases.outcome: Its number is cleared.

edge_cases.case: The group has a Full Reconciliation.
edge_cases.outcome: Every item carries the decimal text of the marker's identifier and no partial number remains.

worked_examples.description: Two matchings joining one invoice and two payments
worked_examples.narrative: The first matching creates the component numbered seventeen and the second adds the item that was not yet known, so all three items share that number.

records.name: The permitted shapes of a matching number
records.purpose: States the constraint that keeps a matching number consistent with the matchings and the marker of its item, and the exact internal error each violation raises.

operands.name: the matching number of the item
operands.constraints: must be empty, a partial number, a decimal number or an import placeholder

operands.name: the number of matchings of the item
operands.constraints: must agree with the shape

operands.name: the Full Reconciliation of the item
operands.constraints: must agree with the shape

preconditions.condition: The number has just been recomputed or written.
preconditions.otherwise: The constraint is not evaluated.

procedure: When the number is empty, require that the item has no matching; otherwise raise "Should have number".

When the number is the letter that marks a partial number followed by digits, require that the item has at least one matching and no Full Reconciliation; otherwise raise "Should have partials" or "Should not be partial number".

When the number is all digits, require that the item has a Full Reconciliation whose identifier equals that number; otherwise raise "Should not be full number" or "Matching number should be the full reconcile".

When the number begins with the letter that marks an import placeholder followed by at least one character, require that the item has no matching at all; otherwise raise "A temporary number can not be used in a real matching".
For anything else, raise "Invalid matching number format".
records.formula:
empty                        ⟹ the item must have no matching
"P" followed by digits       ⟹ at least one matching AND no Full Reconciliation
all digits                   ⟹ a Full Reconciliation whose identifier equals that number
"I" followed by at least one character ⟹ no matching at all
anything else                ⟹ invalid

rounding.what: Nothing; the constraint reads a text and two counts.
rounding.step: Whenever the number is written.

result.name: the verdict of the constraint
result.unit_or_currency: pass, or an internal error carrying its exact text
result.stored_or_displayed: Raised to the caller; nothing is stored.

edge_cases.case: An imported item carrying a placeholder is drawn into a real matching.
edge_cases.outcome: The constraint raises the message about a temporary number, so the deferred-matching operation must clear the placeholder first.

edge_cases.case: A partial number survives after a marker has been created.
edge_cases.outcome: The message saying the number should not be a partial number is raised.

edge_cases.case: A decimal number does not match the identifier of the marker.
edge_cases.outcome: The message saying the matching number should be the full reconciliation is raised.

worked_examples.description: An item with three matchings and a marker of identifier forty-two
worked_examples.narrative: The number is all digits and equals the identifier of the marker, which is exactly what the third shape requires.

worked_examples.description: An item with no matching but a partial number
worked_examples.narrative: The partial shape requires at least one matching.

records.name: Deferred matching of imported items
records.purpose: Turns the placeholder numbers carried by imported items into real matchings, once every entry of a group has been posted.

operands.name: the placeholder numbers among the items considered
operands.constraints: each begins with the letter that marks an import placeholder

operands.name: every item in the ledger carrying one of those numbers
operands.constraints: grouped by the pair of the number and the account

operands.name: the state of the entry of each item of a group
operands.constraints: every one must be posted before the group is matched

operands.name: the reconcilable flag of the account of a group
operands.constraints: set to true when it was false, and the change is recorded in the log

preconditions.condition: Every entry of the group is posted.
preconditions.otherwise: The group is left alone and matched later.

procedure: Collect the distinct placeholder numbers among the items considered.
Group every item in the ledger carrying one of those numbers by the pair of the number and the account.
For each group, check that every entry of the group is posted; when one is not, skip the group.
When the account of the group does not allow reconciliation, make it reconcilable and record that in the log.
Reconcile the items of the group with the no exchange difference flag and the no cash basis flag set.
records.formula:
groups = the items of the ledger carrying a placeholder number , grouped by ( number , account )
for each group : if every entry of the group is posted , make the account reconcilable when it is not , then reconcile the group with the no exchange difference and no cash basis flags set

rounding.what: Nothing at this level; the matchings themselves round as usual.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the matchings of the imported groups
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as Partial Reconciliations; the placeholder numbers are replaced by real ones.

edge_cases.case: One entry of the group is still in draft.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole group is skipped, so an imported settlement is never matched half way.

edge_cases.case: The account did not allow reconciliation.
edge_cases.outcome: It is made reconcilable and the change is recorded in the log.

edge_cases.case: One placeholder number spans two accounts.
edge_cases.outcome: It yields two groups, each matched on its own account.

worked_examples.description: An imported settlement of one invoice and one payment, both posted
worked_examples.narrative: The account is made reconcilable, the two items are matched, and both derived kinds of entry are suppressed because the import carries its own history.

records.name: The ordering index of a bank transaction
records.purpose: Packs the date, the sequence and the identifier of a transaction into one text, so that asking for the transactions before a given one is a single text comparison rather than a compound condition.

operands.name: the date of the transaction
operands.constraints: written as four digits of year, two of month and two of day, with no separator

operands.name: the sequence of the transaction
operands.constraints: complemented against the largest value the sequence column can hold, which is two thousand one hundred and forty-seven million four hundred and eighty-three thousand six hundred and forty-seven

operands.name: the identifier of the transaction
operands.constraints: padded on the left with zeros to ten characters

preconditions.condition: The transaction already exists in the database.
preconditions.otherwise: The index cannot be computed, because it embeds the identifier.

procedure: Write the date as eight digits: four for the year, two for the month and two for the day, with no separator.

Subtract the sequence from two thousand one hundred and forty-seven million four hundred and eighty-three thousand six hundred and forty-seven and write the result padded on the left with zeros to ten characters.
Write the identifier padded on the left with zeros to ten characters.
Concatenate the three parts in that order.
records.formula: internal_index = date_as_eight_digits( date ) ‖ pad_left_with_zeros_to_ten( 2147483647 − sequence ) ‖ pad_left_with_zeros_to_ten( identifier )

rounding.what: Nothing; the index is a text built from whole numbers.
rounding.precision: Eight characters for the date, ten for each of the two numbers.
rounding.method: Padding with zeros on the left.
rounding.step: Once, when the transaction exists in the database.

result.name: the ordering index of the transaction
