result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Bank Transaction and used as the sort key of every balance computation of the domain.

edge_cases.case: Two transactions share a date and a sequence.
edge_cases.outcome: The identifier breaks the tie ascending, so the older record sorts first.

edge_cases.case: A user gives a transaction a higher sequence.
edge_cases.outcome: Its complement is smaller, so the transaction sorts earlier within its day, which puts it at the top of the day under the default ordering by index descending.

edge_cases.case: The transaction has not been saved yet.
edge_cases.outcome: No index is computed.

worked_examples.description: The example of the document
worked_examples.narrative: The complement of a sequence of one is two thousand one hundred and forty-seven million four hundred and eighty-three thousand six hundred and forty-six, which already fills ten characters.

worked_examples.description: A second transaction the same day with a higher sequence
worked_examples.narrative: The higher sequence gives a smaller complement, so this index is smaller and the transaction sorts earlier.

records.name: The running balance of a bank transaction
records.purpose: Gives the balance of the journal after each displayed transaction, anchored on statements so that the whole history of the journal does not have to be replayed.

operands.name: the ordering indexes of the transactions being displayed
operands.constraints: their smallest and their largest bound the scan

operands.name: the starting balance of the anchoring statement
operands.source: the Bank Statement whose first-line index is strictly smaller than the smallest displayed index
operands.constraints: zero when the statement has none

operands.name: the amount of each transaction in the scan
operands.constraints: added only when the entry is posted

operands.name: whether each transaction is the first of its statement
operands.constraints: re-anchors the running total whatever the state of the entry

operands.name: the state of the entry of each transaction
operands.constraints: only a posted entry contributes its amount

preconditions.condition: The company of a scanned transaction is the journal's company or one of its descendants.
preconditions.otherwise: The transaction is left out of the scan.

procedure: For each journal present among the transactions being displayed, take the smallest and the largest ordering index among them.
Find the most recent statement of that journal whose first-line index is strictly smaller than the smallest index, ordered by first-line index descending.

When such a statement exists, start the running total at its starting balance, or at zero when it has none, and limit the scan to transactions whose index is greater than or equal to that statement's first-line index; when none exists, start at zero and scan everything up to the largest index.

Read, in ascending index order, every transaction of that journal within those bounds whose company is the journal's company or one of its descendants, together with its amount, whether it is the first transaction of its statement, the starting balance of its statement and the state of its entry.

Walk that list in order: when the transaction is the first one of a statement, set the running total to that statement's starting balance, which re-anchors the chain; when the state of its entry is posted, add its amount to the running total; and when the transaction is one of those being displayed, record the running total as its running balance.
Leave untouched the value of a transaction that was deleted from the form and therefore does not appear in the scan.
records.formula:
for each transaction in ascending index order :
    if the transaction is the first one of a statement : running_total ← that statement's starting balance
    if the state of the transaction's entry is posted   : running_total ← running_total + the transaction's amount
    if the transaction is one of those being displayed  : its running balance ← running_total

rounding.what: Nothing is rounded during the walk; each amount is already stored rounded to the journal currency.
rounding.precision: The journal currency, or the company currency when the journal names none.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each amount was written.
rounding.step: Not applied during the walk.

result.name: the running balance of each displayed transaction
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed beside each transaction; not stored.

edge_cases.case: A transaction's entry is in draft or cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: Its amount is not added, but when it is the first of a statement it still re-anchors the running total.

edge_cases.case: There is no statement before the displayed range.
edge_cases.outcome: The running total starts at zero and the scan covers everything up to the largest displayed index.

edge_cases.case: A transaction was deleted from the form.
edge_cases.outcome: It is absent from the scan and keeps whatever running balance it had.

edge_cases.case: The anchoring statement has no starting balance.
edge_cases.outcome: The running total starts at zero.

worked_examples.description: The chain of section seven point seven, displaying all five transactions
worked_examples.narrative: Each first transaction of a statement re-anchors the total on that statement's starting balance, and the fourth transaction, which belongs to no statement, simply carries the total down by one hundred.

records.name: The starting balance of a bank statement
records.purpose: Derives the balance the journal stood at just before a statement opens, chaining onto the reported ending balance of the previous statement and picking up whatever happened in between.

operands.name: the first-line index of the statement
operands.constraints: the ordering index of its earliest transaction

operands.name: the reported ending balance of the anchoring statement
operands.source: the statement of the anchoring transaction
operands.constraints: zero when there is no anchor

operands.name: the amounts of the transactions of the anchoring statement that also belong to this statement
operands.constraints: subtracted, to handle a user moving transactions between statements

operands.name: the amounts of the posted transactions strictly between the anchor and the first transaction
operands.constraints: added

preconditions.condition: The statements are processed in ascending order of first-line index.
preconditions.otherwise: A later statement could be computed from a previous one whose own starting balance is not yet known.

preconditions.condition: The statement names a journal, or its transactions do.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to anchor against.

procedure: Take the statement's first-line index and its journal, falling back to the journal of its transactions when the statement's own field is not yet set.
Find the most recent posted transaction of that journal whose index is smaller than the first-line index and that belongs to some statement; call it the anchor.
Start from the ending balance of the anchor's statement, or from zero when there is no anchor.
Build the set of in-between transactions: the posted transactions of that journal whose index is smaller than the first-line index and, when an anchor exists, greater than the anchor's index.
When an anchor exists, subtract the amounts of the transactions that belong to the anchor's statement and also belong to the statement being computed.
Add the amounts of the in-between transactions.
The result is the starting balance of the statement.
records.formula:
balance_start = ending_balance_of_anchor_statement
              − Σ amount over the transactions of the anchor statement that also belong to this statement
              + Σ amount over the posted transactions strictly between the anchor and the first transaction

rounding.what: Nothing during the accumulation; the comparison against the previous reported ending balance rounds both sides to the journal currency.
rounding.precision: The journal currency, or the company currency when the journal names none.
rounding.step: Only in the validity test, never in the accumulation.

result.name: the starting balance of the statement
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Bank Statement and read by the running-balance computation.

edge_cases.case: The statement is the first of its journal.
edge_cases.outcome: There is no anchor, the starting balance begins at zero and only the in-between transactions are added.

edge_cases.case: A user moved a transaction from the previous statement into this one.
edge_cases.outcome: Its amount is subtracted, because the previous statement's reported ending balance still includes it.

edge_cases.case: A transaction belonging to no statement sits between the anchor and the first transaction.
edge_cases.outcome: Its amount is added, so the chain does not lose it.

edge_cases.case: The anchor's statement has no reported ending balance.
edge_cases.outcome: The accumulation starts at zero.

worked_examples.description: The third statement of the chain of section seven point seven

inputs.first_line_index: the index of the fifth transaction

worked_examples.narrative: The anchor's statement reports one thousand one hundred and fifty and the unassigned transaction of minus one hundred sits in between, so the third statement opens at one thousand and fifty.

worked_examples.description: The second statement of the same chain
worked_examples.narrative: Nothing sits between the two statements, so the starting balance is exactly the reported ending balance of the first.

records.name: The computed ending balance of a bank statement
records.purpose: Gives the balance the statement should close at according to the ledger, which the completeness test compares with what the bank actually reported.

operands.name: the starting balance of the statement
operands.constraints: already chained onto the previous statement

operands.name: the amount of each transaction of the statement
operands.source: the Bank Transactions of the statement
operands.constraints: added only when the state of its entry is posted

preconditions.condition: The starting balance has already been computed.
preconditions.otherwise: The ending balance cannot be chained.

procedure: Take the starting balance of the statement.
Add the amount of each transaction of the statement whose entry is posted.
Leave out the transactions whose entry is in draft or cancelled.
records.formula: balance_end = balance_start + Σ amount over the statement's transactions whose entry state is posted

rounding.what: Nothing during the accumulation; each amount is already stored rounded to the journal currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each amount was written.
rounding.step: Not applied during the accumulation.

result.name: the computed ending balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Bank Statement and shown beside the reported ending balance.

edge_cases.case: Every transaction of the statement is in draft.
edge_cases.outcome: The computed ending balance equals the starting balance.

edge_cases.case: The statement has no transaction at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The computed ending balance equals the starting balance and the statement is valid by definition.

worked_examples.description: The first statement of the chain of section seven point seven
worked_examples.narrative: Zero plus one thousand minus two hundred and fifty gives seven hundred and fifty.

worked_examples.description: The third statement of the same chain
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand and fifty plus fifty gives one thousand one hundred.

records.name: The reported ending balance of a bank statement
records.purpose: Holds what the bank says the account closed at; it starts as a copy of the computed balance so that a freshly created statement is complete by construction.

operands.name: the computed ending balance
operands.constraints: copied on creation and whenever the computation runs

operands.name: the value the user types
operands.source: the user, when the bank says otherwise
operands.constraints: overrides the copy

preconditions.condition: The statement exists.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to store.

procedure: Compute the ending balance from the starting balance and the posted transactions.
Copy it into the reported ending balance, which is a stored editable value.
Leave the user free to overwrite it with what the bank reported.
records.formula: balance_end_real = balance_end , as a stored value that the user may overwrite

rounding.what: Nothing; the value is a copy or a typed amount.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the value is written.
rounding.step: On writing.

result.name: the reported ending balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Bank Statement, editable, and read by the completeness test of this statement and the validity test of the next one.

edge_cases.case: The user never touches the value.
edge_cases.outcome: It equals the computed ending balance and the statement is complete.

edge_cases.case: The user types a different value.
edge_cases.outcome: The statement is no longer complete and the following statement is no longer valid, and both are shown as warnings.

worked_examples.description: A freshly created statement
worked_examples.narrative: The copy makes the statement complete without any user action.

worked_examples.description: The bank reports five less than the ledger
worked_examples.narrative: The statement is flagged incomplete and the following statement is flagged invalid.

records.name: The completeness of a bank statement
records.purpose: Says whether a statement is closed and agrees with the bank, which is what the reconciliation screen and the dashboard show as a warning when it fails.

operands.name: the number of posted transactions of the statement
operands.source: the Bank Transactions of the statement
operands.constraints: must be at least one

operands.name: the computed ending balance
operands.constraints: compared at the precision of the statement currency

operands.name: the reported ending balance
operands.constraints: the same

preconditions.condition: The statement has at least one posted transaction.
preconditions.otherwise: It is not complete, whatever the two balances are.

procedure: Check that the statement has at least one posted transaction.
Compare the computed ending balance with the reported ending balance at the precision of the statement currency.
Answer complete only when both hold.
records.formula: is_complete = ( the statement has at least one posted transaction ) AND compare( statement currency , balance_end , balance_end_real ) = 0

rounding.what: The difference between the two balances, inside the comparison.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the statement currency.
rounding.step: Inside the comparison.

result.name: the completeness flag
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as a warning on the statement and on the dashboard; never a refusal.

edge_cases.case: Every transaction of the statement is in draft.
edge_cases.outcome: The statement is not complete because the first condition fails.

edge_cases.case: The two balances differ by less than one rounding step.
edge_cases.outcome: The comparison reports zero and the statement counts as complete.

worked_examples.description: The first statement of the chain of section seven point seven
worked_examples.narrative: Two posted transactions and two equal balances make the statement complete.

worked_examples.description: The second statement with a bank report of one thousand one hundred and forty-five
worked_examples.narrative: The computed balance is five above the reported one, so the statement is shown as incomplete.

records.name: The validity of a bank statement
records.purpose: Says whether a statement opens exactly where the previous one closed, which is what tells a user that a statement is missing or that a transaction was moved.

operands.name: the first-line index of the statement
operands.constraints: identifies the previous statement

operands.name: the reported ending balance of the previous statement
operands.source: the previous Bank Statement of the same journal
operands.constraints: compared at the precision of the statement currency

operands.name: the starting balance of the statement
operands.constraints: the same

preconditions.condition: A previous statement of the same journal exists and has a first-line index.
preconditions.otherwise: The statement is valid by definition.

preconditions.condition: The statement has transactions.
preconditions.otherwise: It is valid by definition, because it has no first-line index.

procedure: Take the previous statement as the one of the same journal with the greatest first-line index strictly smaller than this statement's first-line index, among those that have one.
When there is no such statement, declare this one valid.

Otherwise round both the previous reported ending balance and this starting balance to the decimal places of the journal's currency, or of the company's currency when the journal has none, and compare them.
Declare the statement invalid when the two rounded values differ.
Flag a journal as having invalid statements when at least one of its statements is invalid.
records.formula:
previous = the statement of the same journal with the greatest first_line_index strictly smaller than this statement's first_line_index , among those that have one
is_valid = ( previous does not exist ) OR compare( statement currency , balance_start , previous.balance_end_real ) = 0

rounding.what: Both balances, before they are compared.
rounding.precision: The decimal places of the journal's currency, or of the company's currency when the journal has none.
rounding.step: Before the comparison, on each of the two values.

result.name: the validity flag of the statement and the invalid-statements flag of the journal
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as a warning on the statement and on the dashboard card of the journal; never a refusal.

edge_cases.case: The statement is the first of its journal.
edge_cases.outcome: It is valid, because no previous statement exists.

edge_cases.case: The statement has no transaction.
edge_cases.outcome: It is valid, because it has no first-line index to compare with.

edge_cases.case: The previous statement's reported ending balance was overridden by the user.
edge_cases.outcome: This statement becomes invalid, which is the signal that the ledger and the bank disagree.

worked_examples.description: The third statement of the chain of section seven point seven, once the bank reports one thousand one hundred and forty-five for the second
worked_examples.narrative: The starting balance of one thousand and fifty was chained onto the computed one thousand one hundred and fifty, while the bank's one thousand one hundred and forty-five less the unassigned one hundred gives one thousand and forty-five, so the statement is invalid and the journal is flagged.

worked_examples.description: The same statement before the override
worked_examples.narrative: The chain is intact and the statement is valid.

records.name: End-to-end example: a chain of three statements
records.purpose: Carries five transactions and three statements through the starting balance, the ending balance, the completeness and the validity, and shows what one wrong bank figure does to the chain.

operands.name: the five transaction amounts, in index order
operands.unit_or_currency: the journal currency, which is the company currency here
operands.constraints: plus one thousand, minus two hundred and fifty, plus four hundred, minus one hundred and plus fifty

operands.name: the assignment of transactions to statements
operands.constraints: the first two on the first statement, the third on the second, the fourth on none, the fifth on the third

preconditions.condition: Every transaction's entry is posted.
preconditions.otherwise: The amounts of the unposted ones are left out of both balances.

preconditions.condition: The journal is held in the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: Every figure would be expressed in the journal currency instead.

procedure: The first statement has no anchor and no in-between transaction, so its starting balance is zero and its computed ending balance is zero plus one thousand minus two hundred and fifty, that is seven hundred and fifty.
The bank reports seven hundred and fifty, so the first statement is complete, and it is valid because it has no previous statement.

The second statement starts at the third transaction; the anchor is the second transaction, whose statement reports seven hundred and fifty; no transaction of the first statement belongs to the second and nothing sits in between, so its starting balance is seven hundred and fifty and its computed ending balance is one thousand one hundred and fifty.

The third statement starts at the fifth transaction; the anchor is the third transaction, whose statement reports one thousand one hundred and fifty; the fourth transaction belongs to no statement, so its minus one hundred is added, giving a starting balance of one thousand and fifty and a computed ending balance of one thousand one hundred.

Now suppose the bank reports one thousand one hundred and forty-five for the second statement: that statement is no longer complete, because the computed one thousand one hundred and fifty differs from it, and the third statement is no longer valid, because its starting balance of one thousand and fifty differs from one thousand one hundred and forty-five less the one hundred of the unassigned transaction, that is one thousand and forty-five.
The journal is then flagged as having invalid statements and the dashboard shows the warning.
records.formula:
first statement  : balance_start = 0.00 ; balance_end = 0 + 1000 − 250 = 750.00
second statement : balance_start = 750.00 ; balance_end = 750 + 400 = 1150.00
third statement  : balance_start = 1150 − 100 = 1050.00 ; balance_end = 1050 + 50 = 1100.00

rounding.what: Only the comparisons of the completeness and the validity tests.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the journal currency.
rounding.step: Inside each comparison; no figure of this example is moved by rounding.

result.name: the six balances and the four flags of the chain
result.stored_or_displayed: The balances are stored on the statements; the flags are displayed as warnings.

edge_cases.case: A transaction belongs to no statement.
edge_cases.outcome: It is picked up as an in-between transaction by the next statement's starting balance.

edge_cases.case: The bank reports a figure different from the ledger.
edge_cases.outcome: The statement becomes incomplete and the following statement becomes invalid, and the journal is flagged.

worked_examples.description: The chain as the document states it, with the bank agreeing
worked_examples.narrative: Each statement chains onto the reported ending balance of the previous one, and the unassigned transaction of minus one hundred is picked up by the third statement's starting balance.

worked_examples.description: The same chain with the bank reporting one thousand one hundred and forty-five for the second statement
worked_examples.narrative: The five-unit disagreement makes the second statement incomplete and the third invalid, and the journal is flagged on the dashboard.

records.name: The three currencies of a bank transaction
records.purpose: Fixes which currency each of the transaction's three amounts is expressed in, which every later formula of the transaction depends on.

operands.name: the currency of the company of the journal
operands.constraints: always present

operands.name: the own currency of the journal
operands.constraints: may be empty

operands.name: the foreign currency of the transaction
operands.constraints: may be empty

preconditions.condition: The journal belongs to a company with a currency.
preconditions.otherwise: No amount of the transaction can be expressed.

procedure: Take the company currency as the currency of the company of the journal.
Take the journal currency as the own currency of the journal, and the company currency when the journal names none.

Take the foreign currency as the foreign currency of the transaction, and when it names none the journal currency, and when that is also absent the company currency; the first non-empty of the three wins.
records.formula:
company_currency = the journal's company currency
journal_currency = the journal's own currency , or the company currency when it has none
foreign_currency = the transaction's foreign currency , or the journal currency , or the company currency , whichever is first non-empty

rounding.what: Nothing; the step selects currencies.
rounding.step: Before any amount of the transaction is computed.

result.name: the company currency, the journal currency and the foreign currency of the transaction
result.stored_or_displayed: Held for the computation of the amounts and of the two journal items.

edge_cases.case: The journal names no currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The journal currency is the company currency and the transaction has only two distinct currencies at most.

edge_cases.case: The transaction names no foreign currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The foreign currency is the journal currency, and the transaction amount equals the journal amount.

edge_cases.case: All three coincide.
edge_cases.outcome: The three amounts of the transaction are the same number.

worked_examples.description: A journal held in a currency other than the company's, with a transaction that names no foreign currency
worked_examples.narrative: The foreign currency falls back to the journal currency, so the counterpart line carries the journal currency.

records.name: The three amounts of a bank transaction
records.purpose: Derives, from the single amount the bank reported, the three figures the transaction's journal entry needs: one in the journal currency, one in the currency of the underlying obligation and one in the books' currency.

operands.name: the amount of the transaction
operands.constraints: signed as the bank reports it, positive for money coming in

operands.name: the foreign amount of the transaction
operands.constraints: read only when the foreign currency differs from the journal currency

operands.name: the conversion rate from the journal currency to the company currency
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the company currency per unit of the journal currency
operands.source: the rate table of the journal's company at the transaction's date
operands.constraints: read only when neither shortcut applies

preconditions.condition: The three currencies have been resolved.
preconditions.otherwise: The branches cannot be chosen.

procedure: Take the journal amount as the amount of the transaction, which is always expressed in the journal currency.
Take the transaction amount as the journal amount when the foreign currency equals the journal currency, and as the foreign amount of the transaction otherwise.

Take the company amount as the journal amount when the journal currency equals the company currency; otherwise as the transaction amount when the foreign currency equals the company currency; otherwise as the journal amount converted from the journal currency to the company currency, for the journal's company, at the transaction's date.
records.formula:
journal_amount     = the transaction's amount
transaction_amount = journal_amount                    when foreign_currency = journal_currency
                   = the transaction's foreign amount  otherwise
company_amount     = journal_amount                    when journal_currency = company_currency
                   = transaction_amount                when foreign_currency = company_currency
                   = convert( journal_amount , from journal_currency to company_currency , for the journal's company , at the transaction's date )   otherwise

rounding.what: The conversion of the third branch.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Inside the conversion, before the amount is written on the liquidity line.

result.name: the journal amount, the transaction amount and the company amount
result.unit_or_currency: the journal currency, the foreign currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written onto the two journal items of the transaction's entry.

edge_cases.case: The journal currency is the company currency and the transaction carries a foreign currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The company amount is the journal amount, so the bank's own conversion is preserved and the foreign amount only appears on the counterpart line.

edge_cases.case: The foreign currency is the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The company amount is the transaction amount, again preserving the bank's conversion.

edge_cases.case: Neither shortcut applies.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate table is read at the transaction's date, which is the only case where the company's rate rather than the bank's decides the company amount.

worked_examples.description: A plain incoming transaction with one currency throughout
worked_examples.narrative: All three amounts coincide and the entry is a plain debit and credit of one thousand five hundred.

worked_examples.description: A journal in the company currency receiving one thousand five hundred of a foreign currency that the bank converted at four fifths
worked_examples.narrative: The journal currency is the company currency, so the company amount is the journal amount and the bank's conversion of one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five stands.

records.name: The two journal items of a bank transaction
records.purpose: States the liquidity line and the counterpart line the transaction's entry always carries when it is created, before any reconciliation rewrites the second one.

operands.name: the journal amount
operands.constraints: the foreign amount of the liquidity line

operands.name: the transaction amount
operands.constraints: negated on the counterpart line

operands.name: the company amount
operands.constraints: decides the side of both lines

operands.name: the default account of the journal
operands.constraints: the account of the liquidity line

operands.name: the explicit counterpart account, or the suspense account of the journal
operands.constraints: the account of the counterpart line

preconditions.condition: A counterpart account resolves, either explicitly or from the journal's suspense account.
preconditions.otherwise: The creation is refused with "You can't create a new statement line without a suspense account set on the *the journal display name* journal."

procedure: Emit the liquidity line on the default account of the journal, in the journal currency, with the journal amount as its foreign amount, debited by the company amount when that is positive and credited by its absolute value when it is negative, carrying the label and the counterparty of the transaction.

Emit the counterpart line on the explicit counterpart account when one was supplied and on the suspense account of the journal otherwise, in the foreign currency, with minus the transaction amount as its foreign amount, credited by the company amount when that is positive and debited by its absolute value when it is negative, carrying the same label and the same counterparty.
records.formula:
liquidity line   : account = the journal's default account ; currency = journal_currency ; foreign amount = journal_amount ; debit = company_amount when positive else 0 ; credit = − company_amount when negative else 0
counterpart line : account = the explicit counterpart account or the journal's suspense account ; currency = foreign_currency ; foreign amount = − transaction_amount ; debit = − company_amount when negative else 0 ; credit = company_amount when positive else 0

rounding.what: Nothing here; the three amounts were rounded when they were computed.
rounding.precision: The journal currency, the foreign currency and the company currency respectively.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Earlier, in the amount calculation.

result.name: the two journal items of the transaction's entry
result.unit_or_currency: company currency, with foreign amounts in the journal currency and the foreign currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Entry, which is created and posted in the same operation.

edge_cases.case: The transaction is money going out.
edge_cases.outcome: The company amount is negative, so the liquidity line is credited and the counterpart line debited.

edge_cases.case: No suspense account is set on the journal and no explicit counterpart account was supplied.
edge_cases.outcome: The creation is refused with the message naming the journal.

edge_cases.case: The foreign currency equals the journal currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The two foreign amounts are the same number with opposite signs.

worked_examples.description: A journal in the company currency receiving one thousand five hundred of a foreign currency converted by the bank at four fifths

liquidity_line.account: the default account of the journal

counterpart_line.account: the suspense account of the journal

worked_examples.narrative: The suspense line is the one that carries the foreign currency, because that is the currency of the underlying obligation, while the bank account itself is in the company currency.

records.name: The amounts and currencies read back from a transaction's entry
records.purpose: Recovers the transaction's three amounts from the entry as it now stands, which is what the reconciliation screen shows once the suspense line has been partly or wholly replaced.

operands.name: the liquidity items of the entry
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency, with foreign amounts in the journal currency
operands.constraints: their foreign amounts and balances are summed

operands.name: the suspense items of the entry
operands.constraints: trusted only when no other item is present

operands.name: the other items of the entry
operands.constraints: their presence means the suspense line can no longer be trusted

operands.name: the foreign amount and the foreign currency of the transaction
operands.constraints: used as the fallback

preconditions.condition: The entry has at least one liquidity item.
preconditions.otherwise: The entry is in an invalid state and the general ledger refuses the write.

procedure: Split the items of the entry into liquidity, suspense and other.
When there is a suspense item and no other item, take the transaction amount as minus the foreign amount of the suspense item and the transaction currency as the currency of that item.

Otherwise, that is when the transaction is partly reconciled or is flagged to be checked so that the suspense item can no longer be trusted, take the transaction amount as the transaction's own foreign amount when it has a foreign currency and as its plain amount otherwise, and the transaction currency as its foreign currency when it has one and as the currency of the liquidity item otherwise.
Take the journal amount as the sum of the foreign amounts of the liquidity items, in the currency of those items.
Take the company amount as the sum of the balances of the liquidity items, in the company currency.
records.formula:
if there is a suspense item and no other item :
    transaction_amount = − the suspense item's foreign amount ; transaction_currency = the suspense item's currency
else :
    transaction_amount = the transaction's own foreign amount when it has a foreign currency , else its plain amount
    transaction_currency = the transaction's foreign currency when it has one , else the liquidity item's currency
journal_amount = Σ foreign amount over the liquidity items
company_amount = Σ balance over the liquidity items

rounding.what: Nothing; the sums are of amounts already rounded when they were written.
rounding.precision: The journal currency for the journal amount, the company currency for the company amount.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Earlier, when the items were written.

result.name: the transaction amount, the transaction currency, the journal amount and the company amount
result.unit_or_currency: the foreign currency, the journal currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the reconciliation screen and used by the rates that convert a counterpart amount.

edge_cases.case: The transaction has been partly reconciled.
edge_cases.outcome: The suspense item no longer represents the whole amount, so the second branch reads the transaction's own values instead.

edge_cases.case: The transaction is flagged to be checked.
edge_cases.outcome: The same second branch applies.

edge_cases.case: The entry has several liquidity items.
edge_cases.outcome: Their foreign amounts and balances are summed, although a structural invariant requires exactly one such item.

worked_examples.description: A freshly created transaction whose entry still holds only the two default lines
worked_examples.narrative: The suspense line is trusted, so the transaction amount is one thousand five hundred of the invoice currency and the liquidity line gives the other two amounts.

records.name: The two rates implied by a bank transaction
records.purpose: Reads back, from the transaction's own three amounts, the two rates the bank actually applied, so that a settlement made from this transaction uses the bank's conversion rather than the company's rate table.

operands.name: the transaction amount
operands.source: the amounts read back from the entry
operands.constraints: its absolute value is the numerator of the first rate

operands.name: the journal amount
operands.source: the amounts read back from the entry
operands.constraints: its absolute value is the denominator of the first rate and the numerator of the second

operands.name: the company amount
operands.source: the amounts read back from the entry
operands.constraints: its absolute value is the denominator of the second rate

preconditions.condition: The journal amount is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The first rate is zero and every conversion through it yields zero.

preconditions.condition: The company amount is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: The second rate is zero and every conversion through it yields zero.

procedure: Divide the absolute value of the transaction amount by the absolute value of the journal amount to obtain the rate from the journal currency to the transaction currency, and use zero when the journal amount is zero.

Divide the absolute value of the journal amount by the absolute value of the company amount to obtain the rate from the company currency to the journal currency, and use zero when the company amount is zero.
records.formula:
rate_journal_to_transaction = | transaction_amount | ÷ | journal_amount |   when journal_amount ≠ 0 , else 0
rate_company_to_journal     = | journal_amount     | ÷ | company_amount |   when company_amount ≠ 0 , else 0

rounding.what: Nothing; both rates are carried at full precision.
rounding.step: Never; the amounts derived from the rates are what get rounded.

result.name: the two rates implied by the transaction
result.unit_or_currency: units of the transaction currency per unit of the journal currency, and units of the journal currency per unit of the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; used by the three conversion cases of the counterpart amount.

edge_cases.case: The journal amount is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The first rate is zero and every conversion through it produces zero.

edge_cases.case: The company amount is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The second rate is zero and every conversion through it produces zero.

edge_cases.case: All three amounts coincide.
edge_cases.outcome: Both rates are one and the conversions are identities.

worked_examples.description: A transaction of one thousand five hundred of a foreign currency credited as one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five in a journal held in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The bank converted at four fifths, and the journal currency is the company currency so the second rate is one.

records.name: Converting a counterpart amount given in the transaction currency
records.purpose: The first of the three conversion cases: the amount to settle is already expressed in the currency of the underlying obligation, so the two other amounts are derived downwards through the bank's own rates.

operands.name: the given amount
operands.source: the residual of the item being settled, or the amount of a model line
operands.constraints: taken as the new transaction amount without change

operands.name: the rate from the journal currency to the transaction currency
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the transaction currency per unit of the journal currency
operands.constraints: zero yields a journal amount of zero

operands.name: the rate from the company currency to the journal currency
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the journal currency per unit of the company currency
operands.constraints: zero yields a balance of zero

preconditions.condition: The currency of the amount is the transaction currency.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other two cases applies.

procedure: Take the new transaction amount as the given amount.
Divide the new transaction amount by the rate from the journal currency to the transaction currency and round the quotient to the journal currency, using zero when that rate is zero.
Divide the new journal amount by the rate from the company currency to the journal currency and round the quotient to the company currency, using zero when that rate is zero.
Return the pair made of the new transaction amount as the foreign amount and the new balance as the balance of the counterpart item.
records.formula:
new_transaction_amount = the given amount
new_journal_amount     = round_to( journal_currency , new_transaction_amount ÷ rate_journal_to_transaction )   or 0 when that rate is 0
new_balance            = round_to( company_currency , new_journal_amount ÷ rate_company_to_journal )           or 0 when that rate is 0

rounding.what: The new journal amount and the new balance.
rounding.precision: The journal currency and the company currency respectively.
rounding.step: After each division, and before the next division uses the result, so the second division reads an already rounded journal amount.

result.name: the foreign amount and the balance of the counterpart journal item
result.unit_or_currency: the transaction currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the counterpart item of the transaction's entry.

edge_cases.case: The rate from the journal currency to the transaction currency is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The journal amount is zero, and the balance is then zero as well.

edge_cases.case: The rate from the company currency to the journal currency is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance is zero although the journal amount is not.

edge_cases.case: The three currencies coincide.
edge_cases.outcome: Both rates are one and all three amounts equal the given amount.

worked_examples.description: Settling one thousand five hundred of the transaction currency at the bank's rate of four fifths, in a journal held in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand five hundred divided by four fifths gives one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five, and the journal currency being the company currency the balance is the same.

records.name: Converting a counterpart amount given in the journal currency
records.purpose: The second of the three conversion cases: the amount to settle is expressed in the currency the journal is held in, so it is pushed upwards into the transaction currency and downwards into the company currency.

operands.name: the given amount
operands.source: the residual of the item being settled, or the amount of a model line
operands.constraints: used directly by both conversions

operands.name: the rate from the journal currency to the transaction currency
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the transaction currency per unit of the journal currency
operands.constraints: multiplied by the given amount

operands.name: the rate from the company currency to the journal currency
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the journal currency per unit of the company currency
operands.constraints: the given amount is divided by it

preconditions.condition: The currency of the amount is the journal currency.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other two cases applies.

procedure: Multiply the given amount by the rate from the journal currency to the transaction currency and round the product to the transaction currency: that is the new transaction amount.
Divide the given amount by the rate from the company currency to the journal currency and round the quotient to the company currency, using zero when that rate is zero: that is the new balance.
Return the pair made of the new transaction amount as the foreign amount and the new balance as the balance of the counterpart item.
records.formula:
new_transaction_amount = round_to( transaction_currency , the given amount × rate_journal_to_transaction )
new_balance            = round_to( company_currency , the given amount ÷ rate_company_to_journal )   or 0 when that rate is 0

rounding.what: The new transaction amount and the new balance.
rounding.precision: The transaction currency and the company currency respectively.
rounding.step: After each operation, independently; neither result feeds the other.

result.name: the foreign amount and the balance of the counterpart journal item
result.unit_or_currency: the transaction currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the counterpart item of the transaction's entry.

edge_cases.case: The rate from the company currency to the journal currency is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance is zero although the transaction amount is not.

edge_cases.case: The transaction currency equals the journal currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The first rate is one and the transaction amount equals the given amount.

worked_examples.description: Settling one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five of the journal currency at a rate of four fifths towards the transaction currency
worked_examples.narrative: One thousand eight hundred and seventy-five multiplied by four fifths gives one thousand five hundred, and the balance is unchanged because the journal currency is the company currency.

records.name: Converting a counterpart amount given in any other currency
records.purpose: The third of the three conversion cases: the amount to settle is in neither the transaction currency nor the journal currency, so the company-currency balance is taken as given and the two other amounts are built up from it.

operands.name: the given balance
operands.source: the residual of the item being settled
operands.constraints: kept unchanged as the new balance

operands.name: the rate from the company currency to the journal currency
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the journal currency per unit of the company currency
operands.constraints: multiplied by the given balance

operands.name: the rate from the journal currency to the transaction currency
operands.unit_or_currency: units of the transaction currency per unit of the journal currency
operands.constraints: multiplied by the new journal amount

preconditions.condition: The currency of the amount is neither the transaction currency nor the journal currency.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other two cases applies.

procedure: Multiply the given balance by the rate from the company currency to the journal currency and round the product to the journal currency: that is the new journal amount.
Multiply the new journal amount by the rate from the journal currency to the transaction currency and round the product to the transaction currency: that is the new transaction amount.
Keep the given balance as the new balance.
Return the pair made of the new transaction amount as the foreign amount and the given balance as the balance of the counterpart item.
records.formula:
new_journal_amount     = round_to( journal_currency , the given balance × rate_company_to_journal )
new_transaction_amount = round_to( transaction_currency , new_journal_amount × rate_journal_to_transaction )
new_balance            = the given balance

rounding.what: The new journal amount and then the new transaction amount.
rounding.precision: The journal currency and the transaction currency respectively.
rounding.step: After the first multiplication, and again after the second, so the second multiplication reads an already rounded journal amount.

result.name: the foreign amount and the balance of the counterpart journal item
result.unit_or_currency: the transaction currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the counterpart item of the transaction's entry.

edge_cases.case: Either rate is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The corresponding amount is zero, and the chain then yields a transaction amount of zero.

edge_cases.case: The item being settled is in a third currency altogether.
edge_cases.outcome: Its own currency plays no part; the company-currency balance is the pivot.

worked_examples.description: Settling an item whose balance is one thousand eight hundred and seventy-five of the company currency, through a journal held in the company currency at a bank rate of four fifths
worked_examples.narrative: The balance is carried straight into the journal currency and then converted to one thousand five hundred of the transaction currency at the bank's own rate.

records.name: The candidate journal items of a bank transaction
records.purpose: Fixes the population a transaction may be matched with, which the reconciliation screen offers and the automatic matching searches.

operands.name: the state of the entry of each candidate
operands.constraints: posted, or draft with a counterparty when the screen allows draft documents

operands.name: the display type of each candidate
operands.constraints: must not be a section, a subsection or a note

operands.name: the company of each candidate
operands.constraints: the transaction's company or one of its descendants

operands.name: the reconciled flag of each candidate
operands.constraints: must be false

operands.name: the account of each candidate
operands.constraints: must be one of the reconcilable accounts of the transaction's root company tree

operands.name: whether the candidate belongs to a Payment
operands.constraints: a Payment's own trade line is excluded

preconditions.condition: Draft documents are allowed by the setting of the reconciliation screen.
preconditions.otherwise: Only items of posted entries are offered; draft documents are never allowed for automatic matching or for reconciliation-model suggestions.

procedure: Keep the items whose entry is posted; when draft documents are allowed, also keep the items of draft entries that have a counterparty.
Drop the items whose display type is a section, a subsection or a note.
Keep the items whose company is the transaction's company or one of its descendants, so that documents of child companies can be matched, consistently with what the screen shows.
Drop the items that are already reconciled.
Keep the items whose account is one of the reconcilable accounts of the transaction's root company tree, which is the phrasing that lets the database use its index on unreconciled items.
Drop the items whose account is a receivable or a payable account and that belong to a Payment, because the money side of a Payment is its outstanding line and not its trade line.
Drop the items that belong to this same transaction.
records.formula:
candidate( item ) = ( the entry is posted OR ( draft documents are allowed AND the entry is draft AND the item has a counterparty ) )
                AND the display type is not a section , a subsection or a note
                AND the item's company is the transaction's company or one of its descendants
                AND the item is not reconciled
                AND the item's account is one of the reconcilable accounts of the transaction's root company tree
                AND NOT ( the account type is receivable or payable AND the item belongs to a Payment )
                AND the item does not belong to this transaction

rounding.what: Nothing; the step filters records.
rounding.step: Before any amount is proposed.

result.name: the set of candidate journal items
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the reconciliation screen and searched by the automatic matching.

edge_cases.case: A Payment's receivable counterpart line would otherwise match the transaction.
edge_cases.outcome: It is excluded, so the transaction settles the Payment's outstanding line instead and the Payment's own allocation to documents is left intact.

edge_cases.case: The transaction belongs to a parent company and a document belongs to a child.
edge_cases.outcome: The document is offered, because descendants are included.

edge_cases.case: Draft documents are allowed but a draft item has no counterparty.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not offered.

edge_cases.case: The account is reconcilable in another company tree.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not offered, because the reconcilable set is taken from the transaction's own root company tree.

worked_examples.description: A transaction of a parent company facing an open invoice of a child company and the receivable line of a Payment

items.name: the receivable counterpart line of a Payment

worked_examples.narrative: The invoice of the child company qualifies, and the Payment's trade line is excluded because the money side of a Payment is its outstanding line.

records.name: Reconciling a bank transaction, step by step
records.purpose: The whole operation a user performs on the reconciliation screen: taking a transaction whose amount sits on the suspense account and explaining it, by matching open items, by allocating through a model, or by recording a Payment.

operands.name: the transaction and its three currencies
operands.unit_or_currency: the journal currency, the transaction currency and the company currency
operands.source: the Bank Transaction and its entry
operands.constraints: read first

operands.name: the open amount of the transaction
operands.constraints: minus the foreign amount when the transaction has a foreign currency and is not checked, otherwise the sum of the suspense items' residuals or foreign amounts

operands.name: the counterparty of the transaction
operands.source: the Bank Transaction, a Bank Account matching the reported account number, or a partner-mapping model
operands.constraints: restricts the proposals when it is known

operands.name: the residual of each matched journal item
operands.constraints: converted through the bank's own rates

operands.name: the amount of each manual or model line
operands.source: the user or the applied model
operands.constraints: converted the same way

preconditions.condition: The transaction's entry holds exactly one liquidity item.
preconditions.otherwise: The general ledger refuses the rewrite with the message about the invalid state of the entry.

preconditions.condition: A partial match is not attempted on a Payment that must be settled in full.
preconditions.otherwise: The match is forbidden, because such a payment is all or nothing.

procedure: Load the transaction: read its journal, its amount, its three currencies, its counterparty and its label, and split its entry into liquidity, suspense and other items.
Determine the open amount: minus the foreign amount when the transaction has a foreign currency and is not checked, otherwise the sum of the residuals or foreign amounts of the suspense items.

Detect the counterparty when the transaction has none: when the bank reported an account number, look for a Bank Account whose account number matches it and take its holder; otherwise evaluate the partner-mapping models in their ordering and take the counterparty of the first whose label condition matches; otherwise, as an industry-standard default, match the reported third-party name against the known counterparties.

Apply the reconciliation models in their ordering: the first model whose every condition holds wins; a partner mapping only sets the counterparty and evaluation continues with the next model, while any other model has its counterpart lines computed and proposed.

Propose matching journal items among the candidates, restricted to the detected counterparty when there is one, preferring an exact amount match on the same counterparty, then a reference match between the transaction label and the document's payment reference or name, then the oldest due date; this preference order is an industry-standard default.
Let the user adjust: add or remove matched items, add manual counterpart lines with an account and an amount, change the counterparty, or choose a different model.
Compute the counterpart amounts: for each matched journal item from its residual through the bank's own rates, and for each manual or model line from the line's own amount through the same rates.

Decide partial or full for each matched item: when the open amount is smaller than the item's residual, only the open amount is taken and the item keeps a residual; a partial match is forbidden when the item belongs to a Payment whose payment method is a transfer-file method or whose Payment has an online transaction.

Rewrite the entry: replace the suspense item by the computed counterpart items, keeping exactly one liquidity item untouched, and give every counterpart item the transaction's counterparty, the label of its source and, when it comes from a model line, that line's account, taxes, analytic distribution and the reference to the model.
Reconcile: for each account present among the new counterpart items, match those items with the matched journal items of the same account through the reconciliation plan.

Mark the transaction: the residual recomputes and the transaction becomes reconciled when it reaches zero; when the applied model is automated the entry is also marked as checked; and when the model names a next activity type, an activity of that type is scheduled on the transaction.

Create a Payment when the user asks for one: a Payment carrying the transaction's counterparty, amount, direction and date, with its outstanding account replaced by the transaction's counterpart account, added to the transaction's automatically generated payments so that undoing the reconciliation deletes it.
records.formula:
open_amount = − the transaction's foreign amount            when the transaction has a foreign currency and is not checked
            = Σ residual or foreign amount over the suspense items   otherwise
for each matched item : ( foreign amount , balance ) = convert_at_the_bank's_own_rate( the item's residual )
match is partial ⟺ open_amount < the item's residual , and partial matching is permitted for that item

rounding.what: Each counterpart amount, inside the conversion at the bank's own rates.
rounding.precision: The transaction currency, the journal currency and the company currency, according to the conversion case.
rounding.step: Inside each conversion, before the item is written.

result.name: the rewritten entry, the matchings and the state of the transaction
result.unit_or_currency: company currency, with foreign amounts in the transaction currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Entry, the Partial Reconciliations and the Bank Transaction.

edge_cases.case: The counterpart lines do not consume the whole amount.
edge_cases.outcome: The remainder stays on the suspense account, the entry keeps a suspense line and the transaction stays unreconciled.

edge_cases.case: The matched item belongs to a Payment settled by a transfer file or carrying an online transaction.
edge_cases.outcome: A partial match is forbidden; the settlement is all or nothing.

edge_cases.case: The applied model is automated.
edge_cases.outcome: The lines are written, the reconciliation is performed and the entry is marked as checked without asking the user.

edge_cases.case: The user records the transaction as a Payment.
edge_cases.outcome: The Payment is created with the transaction's counterpart account as its outstanding account and is deleted again when the reconciliation is undone.

worked_examples.description: A transaction of one thousand five hundred matched in full with one open invoice of the same amount
worked_examples.narrative: The open amount equals the residual, so the suspense line is replaced by one counterpart line on the receivable account and the transaction closes.

worked_examples.description: The same transaction against an invoice of two thousand
worked_examples.narrative: Only the open amount is taken and the invoice keeps five hundred, while the transaction itself is fully explained.

records.name: Undoing the reconciliation of a bank transaction
records.purpose: Returns a transaction to its unexplained state, removing everything the reconciliation wrote and restoring the two default lines.

operands.name: the matchings on the items of the entry
operands.constraints: all removed

operands.name: the automatically generated Payments of the transaction
operands.constraints: deleted

operands.name: whether the current user may review entries
operands.source: the access rights of the user
operands.constraints: becomes the new value of the checked flag

preconditions.condition: The transaction has been reconciled.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to undo.

procedure: Remove every matching on the items of the transaction's entry, which also deletes or reverses the derived exchange and cash-basis entries.
Delete the Payments the reconciliation generated automatically.
Clear the items of the entry and recreate the default liquidity and suspense pair.
Set the checked flag of the entry to whether the current user may review entries.
records.formula:
remove every matching on the entry's items
delete the automatically generated Payments
clear the entry's items and recreate the default liquidity and suspense pair
checked ← whether the current user may review entries

rounding.what: Nothing here; the recreated default lines round as the creation does.
rounding.precision: The journal currency, the foreign currency and the company currency.
rounding.step: When the default pair is rebuilt.

result.name: the transaction restored to its unexplained state
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Entry and the Bank Transaction.

edge_cases.case: A derived exchange entry was posted.
edge_cases.outcome: It is reversed with the cancel flag rather than deleted.

edge_cases.case: The user may not review entries.
edge_cases.outcome: The checked flag becomes false, so the transaction returns to the figure of transactions still to check.

edge_cases.case: The reconciliation created a Payment.
edge_cases.outcome: That Payment is deleted, because it was recorded in the transaction's automatically generated payments.

worked_examples.description: Undoing a reconciliation that had created one Payment and one matching, performed by a user who may review entries
worked_examples.narrative: The entry returns to its two default lines and stays marked as checked because the user has the review right.

records.name: Evaluating the reconciliation models of a transaction
records.purpose: Selects, from the models of the company, at most one that applies to a transaction, plus possibly a counterparty discovered by a mapping, in an order that is entirely determined.

operands.name: the active models whose company is an ancestor of the transaction's company
operands.constraints: ordered by sequence ascending, then by identifier ascending

operands.name: the journal list of each model
operands.constraints: an empty list means every liquidity journal

operands.name: the counterparty list of each model
operands.constraints: an empty list means every counterparty

operands.name: the amount condition of each model
operands.constraints: no condition means the model passes this filter

operands.name: the label condition of each model
operands.constraints: no condition means the model passes this filter

preconditions.condition: The models are walked in their stored order, by sequence ascending then identifier ascending.
preconditions.otherwise: A different model would win and the transaction would be explained differently.

preconditions.condition: The partner mappings are walked before the counterpart models.
preconditions.otherwise: A counterpart model that filters on the counterparty could not see the counterparty a mapping has just discovered.

procedure: Select the candidate models: every Reconciliation Model that is active and whose company is an ancestor of the transaction's company, ordered by sequence ascending then identifier ascending.
Filter on the journal: a model applies only when its journal list is empty or contains the transaction's journal.
Filter on the counterparty: a model applies only when its counterparty list is empty or contains the transaction's counterparty; a transaction with no counterparty passes only when the list is empty.
Filter on the amount, when the model names an amount condition, against the absolute value of the transaction's amount in the transaction currency.
Filter on the label, when the model names a label condition, against the text pool made of the transaction's label, the textual content of its raw transaction details and its note.
Classify each model: one that names a mapped counterparty is a partner mapping, every other one is a counterpart model.

Walk the ordered candidate list once, and for every partner mapping that passes the four filters, set the transaction's counterparty to that mapping's counterparty and stop looking for a counterparty; a partner mapping never produces counterpart lines and never stops the search for a counterpart model.
Walk the ordered candidate list again, now with the counterparty possibly filled in, and take the first counterpart model that passes the four filters as the applicable model.
Never offer spontaneously a counterpart model whose proposable flag is false; such a model can only be chosen explicitly by the user.

Apply the model: compute its counterpart lines, and when its trigger is the automatic one write them, reconcile and mark the transaction's entry as checked without asking the user, while a manual trigger presents them for confirmation.
Schedule the follow-up when the model names a next activity type, by creating an activity of that type on the transaction.
Record the origin: every journal item created by a model line stores a reference to the model, so the model can later count and list what it produced.
records.formula:
candidates = active models whose company is an ancestor of the transaction's company , ordered by sequence ascending then identifier ascending
applies( model ) = ( journal list is empty OR contains the transaction's journal )
              AND ( counterparty list is empty OR contains the transaction's counterparty )
              AND the amount condition passes
              AND the label condition passes
pass one : the first partner mapping that applies sets the counterparty
pass two : the first counterpart model that applies is the applicable model

rounding.what: Nothing; the evaluation compares an amount against bounds and a text against a pattern.
rounding.precision: The transaction currency for the amount filter.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: at most one applicable counterpart model, and possibly a detected counterparty
result.stored_or_displayed: The counterparty is written on the transaction; the model drives the counterpart lines and the reference stored on each created item.

edge_cases.case: A partner mapping matches.
edge_cases.outcome: It sets the counterparty and the search continues, so a counterpart model filtering on that counterparty can now pass.

edge_cases.case: Two counterpart models both pass.
edge_cases.outcome: The one with the smaller sequence wins, and the identifier breaks a tie.

edge_cases.case: A model has no condition at all and no automation.
edge_cases.outcome: Its proposable flag is false, so it is never offered spontaneously and can only be chosen by hand.

edge_cases.case: The transaction has no counterparty and a model names a counterparty list.
edge_cases.outcome: That model does not apply.

worked_examples.description: One partner mapping and one counterpart model filtering on that counterparty

expected_outputs.applicable_model: the counterpart model of sequence twenty

worked_examples.narrative: The mapping fills in the counterparty on the first pass, which is exactly what lets the counterpart model pass its counterparty filter on the second.

records.name: The amount condition of a reconciliation model: an upper bound
records.purpose: The first of the three amount conditions: the model applies only to transactions no larger than a stated maximum.

operands.name: the absolute value of the transaction's amount
operands.constraints: the sign is discarded, so an outgoing transaction is tested on its magnitude

operands.name: the maximum of the model
operands.constraints: the only bound the form asks for under this condition

preconditions.condition: The model names this amount condition.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other two conditions applies, or the model has none and passes the filter.

procedure: Take the absolute value of the transaction's amount, in the transaction currency.
Compare it with the maximum of the model.
The model passes the amount filter when the absolute amount is not greater than the maximum.
records.formula:
a = | the transaction's amount |   in the transaction currency
passes ⟺ a ≤ match_amount_max

rounding.what: Nothing; both values are already expressed in the transaction currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the amount was written.
rounding.step: Not applied during the comparison.

result.name: whether the amount filter passes
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides whether the model applies.

edge_cases.case: The transaction is money going out.
edge_cases.outcome: The absolute value is tested, so the sign never decides the outcome.

edge_cases.case: The amount equals the maximum exactly.
edge_cases.outcome: The model passes, because the bound is inclusive.

worked_examples.description: A model with a maximum of fifty against an outgoing transaction of forty-five
worked_examples.narrative: Forty-five is not greater than fifty, so the model applies.

worked_examples.description: The same model against a transaction of sixty
worked_examples.narrative: Sixty is above the maximum, so the model does not apply.

records.name: The amount condition of a reconciliation model: a lower bound
records.purpose: The second of the three amount conditions: the model applies only to transactions no smaller than a stated minimum.

operands.name: the absolute value of the transaction's amount
operands.constraints: the sign is discarded

operands.name: the minimum of the model
operands.constraints: the only bound the form asks for under this condition

preconditions.condition: The model names this amount condition.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other two conditions applies, or the model has none and passes the filter.

procedure: Take the absolute value of the transaction's amount, in the transaction currency.
Compare it with the minimum of the model.
The model passes the amount filter when the absolute amount is not smaller than the minimum.
records.formula:
a = | the transaction's amount |   in the transaction currency
passes ⟺ a ≥ match_amount_min

rounding.what: Nothing; both values are already expressed in the transaction currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the amount was written.
rounding.step: Not applied during the comparison.

result.name: whether the amount filter passes
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides whether the model applies.

edge_cases.case: The amount equals the minimum exactly.
edge_cases.outcome: The model passes, because the bound is inclusive.

edge_cases.case: The transaction amount is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The model passes only when the minimum is zero as well.

worked_examples.description: A model with a minimum of one thousand against a transaction of three thousand three hundred and fifty
worked_examples.narrative: Three thousand three hundred and fifty is above the minimum, so the model applies.

records.name: The amount condition of a reconciliation model: between two bounds
records.purpose: The third of the three amount conditions: the model applies only to transactions inside a stated band, both bounds being required.

operands.name: the absolute value of the transaction's amount
operands.constraints: the sign is discarded

operands.name: the minimum of the model
operands.constraints: required under this condition

operands.name: the maximum of the model
operands.constraints: required under this condition

preconditions.condition: The model names this amount condition and both bounds are filled in.
preconditions.otherwise: The form refuses to save the model, because both bounds are required.

procedure: Take the absolute value of the transaction's amount, in the transaction currency.
Check that it is not smaller than the minimum.
Check that it is not greater than the maximum.
The model passes the amount filter when both hold.
records.formula:
a = | the transaction's amount |   in the transaction currency
passes ⟺ match_amount_min ≤ a ≤ match_amount_max

rounding.what: Nothing; all three values are already expressed in the transaction currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the amounts were written.
rounding.step: Not applied during the comparisons.

result.name: whether the amount filter passes
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides whether the model applies.

edge_cases.case: The amount equals one of the two bounds.
edge_cases.outcome: The model passes, because both bounds are inclusive.

edge_cases.case: The minimum is above the maximum.
edge_cases.outcome: No amount can pass and the model never applies.

worked_examples.description: A model banded between ten and one hundred against a transaction of forty-five
worked_examples.narrative: Forty-five lies inside the band, so the model applies.

worked_examples.description: The same model against a transaction of one hundred and five
worked_examples.narrative: One hundred and five is above the upper bound.

records.name: The label condition of a reconciliation model
records.purpose: Tests the text a bank sent with the transaction against the pattern of a model, in one of three modes, over a pool that includes the raw details as well as the label.

operands.name: the label of the transaction
operands.constraints: part of the text pool

operands.name: the textual content of the raw transaction details
operands.constraints: part of the text pool

operands.name: the note of the transaction
operands.constraints: part of the text pool

operands.name: the parameter of the model
operands.constraints: read as a plain text in the first two modes and as a pattern in the third

preconditions.condition: The model names a label condition.
preconditions.otherwise: The model passes this filter without any test.

procedure: Build the text pool from the transaction's label, the textual content of its raw transaction details and its note.
Under the containment mode, the model passes when the parameter appears somewhere in the pool, ignoring letter case.
Under the negated containment mode, the model passes when the parameter does not appear in the pool, ignoring letter case.
Under the pattern mode, the model passes when the parameter, read as a pattern, matches somewhere in the pool.
records.formula:
pool = the transaction's label ‖ the textual content of its raw transaction details ‖ its note
contains     : passes ⟺ the parameter appears in pool , ignoring letter case
not contains : passes ⟺ the parameter does not appear in pool , ignoring letter case
pattern      : passes ⟺ the parameter , read as a pattern , matches somewhere in pool

rounding.what: Nothing; the test is on text.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: whether the label filter passes
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides whether the model applies.

edge_cases.case: The parameter appears only in the raw details and not in the label.
edge_cases.outcome: The model still passes, because the pool covers all three texts.

edge_cases.case: The parameter differs from the text only by letter case.
edge_cases.outcome: The two containment modes ignore case, so it still matches.

edge_cases.case: The pattern does not match anywhere.
edge_cases.outcome: The model does not apply, and a model line that reads the same pattern would in any case produce nothing.

worked_examples.description: A model whose condition is containment of a three-letter marker, against a bank label carrying that marker
worked_examples.narrative: The marker appears in the label, so the model applies and its lines are computed.

records.name: Whether a reconciliation model may be proposed
records.purpose: Keeps a model with no condition at all from being offered against every transaction, by requiring at least one restriction or an automatic trigger.

operands.name: whether the model is a partner mapping
operands.constraints: a mapping is never proposable

operands.name: whether the model has a label condition
operands.constraints: any one of the four qualifies the model

operands.name: whether the model has an amount condition
operands.constraints: the same

operands.name: whether the model has a counterparty list
operands.constraints: the same

operands.name: whether the trigger of the model is the automatic one
operands.constraints: the same

preconditions.condition: The model is not a partner mapping.
preconditions.otherwise: The flag is false, because a mapping never writes anything.

procedure: Answer false at once when the model is a partner mapping.
Otherwise answer true when the model has a label condition, or an amount condition, or a counterparty list, or an automatic trigger.
Otherwise answer false, so that a model with no condition at all and no automation is never offered spontaneously and can only be chosen explicitly by the user.
records.formula:
can_be_proposed = NOT a partner mapping
              AND ( it has a label condition OR it has an amount condition OR it has a counterparty list OR its trigger is the automatic one )

rounding.what: Nothing; the flag is a truth value.
rounding.step: Whenever the model's conditions change.

result.name: the proposable flag of the model
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Reconciliation Model and read by the reconciliation screen.

edge_cases.case: A model with no condition but an automatic trigger.
edge_cases.outcome: It is proposable, because the automation is itself a deliberate choice by the configurer.

edge_cases.case: A partner mapping with a label condition.
edge_cases.outcome: It is still not proposable, because a mapping only names a counterparty.

edge_cases.case: A model with a journal list but nothing else.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not proposable: the journal list alone does not qualify.

worked_examples.description: A model whose only restriction is a label condition
