worked_examples.narrative: The label condition alone makes the model specific enough to be offered.

worked_examples.description: A model with a journal list only
worked_examples.narrative: Nothing restricts the model, so it would match every transaction and is not offered.

records.name: The ordering of reconciliation models and of their lines
records.purpose: States the three orderings the evaluation and the amount computation depend on, because each of them changes the result.

operands.name: the sequence of each model
operands.constraints: the first ordering key, ascending

operands.name: the identifier of each model
operands.constraints: the tie-break, ascending

operands.name: the sequence of each line of a model
operands.constraints: the first ordering key, ascending

operands.name: the identifier of each line
operands.constraints: the tie-break, ascending

preconditions.condition: The models and the lines carry sequences.
preconditions.otherwise: The identifiers alone order them.

procedure: Order the models by sequence ascending, then by identifier ascending.
Within one model, order the lines by sequence ascending, then by identifier ascending, because a line whose amount is a percentage of the open balance consumes what the lines before it left.
Evaluate the partner mappings before the counterpart models, so that a counterpart model that filters on the counterparty can see the counterparty a mapping has just discovered.
records.formula:
models : sequence ascending , then identifier ascending
lines within one model : sequence ascending , then identifier ascending
partner mappings are evaluated before counterpart models

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule orders records.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the evaluation order of the models and the computation order of the lines
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides which model wins and how the open balance is consumed.

edge_cases.case: Two models share a sequence.
edge_cases.outcome: The smaller identifier is evaluated first.

edge_cases.case: The lines of a model are reordered.
edge_cases.outcome: The amounts change: a percentage line evaluated first consumes the whole open balance and leaves nothing for the lines after it.

worked_examples.description: A model whose second line takes the whole remaining open balance

line_order: the line reading the amount out of the label
the line taking one hundred percent of the open balance

worked_examples.narrative: In this order the second line absorbs the eight point zero seven the first left, and the transaction closes.

worked_examples.description: The same two lines in the other order

line_order: the line taking one hundred percent of the open balance
the line reading the amount out of the label

worked_examples.narrative: The percentage line consumes the whole amount first, and the transaction is left unexplained by three thousand three hundred and fifty-eight point zero seven.

records.name: Recognising a partner-mapping model
records.purpose: States the four conditions that make a model a pure counterparty mapping, which writes nothing and only says whom a transaction belongs to.

operands.name: whether the model has a label condition
operands.constraints: required

operands.name: the number of lines of the model
operands.constraints: exactly one

operands.name: whether that line names a counterparty
operands.constraints: required

operands.name: whether that line names an account
operands.constraints: must be false

preconditions.condition: All four conditions hold.
preconditions.otherwise: The model is a counterpart model and produces journal items.

procedure: Check that the model has a label condition.
Check that it has exactly one line.
Check that this line names a counterparty.
Check that this line names no account.

When all four hold, treat the model as a partner mapping: its proposable flag is false, it never writes anything, and it only says that a transaction whose label looks like this belongs to that counterparty.
records.formula:
is_partner_mapping ⟺ the model has a label condition
                 AND it has exactly one line
                 AND that line names a counterparty
                 AND that line names no account

rounding.what: Nothing; the classification reads four flags.
rounding.step: Before the two evaluation passes.

result.name: whether the model is a partner mapping
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Reconciliation Model as the mapped counterparty, and read by the two evaluation passes.

edge_cases.case: The single line names both a counterparty and an account.
edge_cases.outcome: The model is a counterpart model and does write a journal item.

edge_cases.case: The model has two lines, one of which names only a counterparty.
edge_cases.outcome: The model is not a mapping, because a mapping has exactly one line.

edge_cases.case: The model has no label condition.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not a mapping, because a mapping exists precisely to key on the label.

worked_examples.description: A model with one line naming a counterparty and no account, keyed on a label
worked_examples.narrative: The model only fills in the counterparty on the first evaluation pass and writes nothing.

records.name: The transaction amount and the open balance of a model application
records.purpose: Defines the two quantities every counterpart line of a model reads: the amount the bank reported and what is still unexplained at the moment the line is evaluated.

operands.name: the amount of the transaction
operands.constraints: signed as the bank reports it

operands.name: the amounts of the lines already written
operands.source: the lines of the model evaluated before this one
operands.constraints: each reduces the open balance

preconditions.condition: The lines are evaluated in their stored order.
preconditions.otherwise: The open balance a line reads is not the one the model intends.

procedure: Read the transaction amount as the amount of the transaction in the transaction currency, signed as the bank reports it.
Start the open balance at minus the transaction amount, so that a negative open balance means an amount still to be credited somewhere.
Reduce the open balance by the amount of each line as it is written.
When every line has been evaluated and the open balance is still not zero, leave the remainder on the suspense account, so that the transaction is only partly reconciled.
records.formula:
transaction_amount = the transaction's amount in the transaction currency , signed as the bank reports it
open_balance       = − transaction_amount , at the start
after each line    : open_balance ← open_balance − the line amount

rounding.what: Nothing here; each line amount is rounded when it is computed.
rounding.step: Inside each line's own computation.

result.name: the transaction amount and the running open balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; the remainder, when there is one, stays visible as the suspense line of the entry.

edge_cases.case: The lines over-explain the transaction.
edge_cases.outcome: The open balance changes sign and the remainder stays on the suspense account with the opposite sign.

edge_cases.case: The model has no line at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The open balance stays at minus the transaction amount and nothing is explained.

edge_cases.case: A line produces nothing, because its pattern did not match.
edge_cases.outcome: The open balance is unchanged by that line.

worked_examples.description: A transaction of plus three thousand three hundred and fifty
worked_examples.narrative: A negative open balance of three thousand three hundred and fifty means that amount still has to be credited somewhere.

records.name: The counterpart line amount in the fixed mode
records.purpose: The first of the four amount modes: the line carries a constant, whose sign decides the side of the journal item.

operands.name: the amount text of the line
operands.constraints: read as a number

preconditions.condition: The amount text reads as a number.
preconditions.otherwise: The line produces nothing.

procedure: Read the amount text of the line as a number.
Take that number as the line amount.
Produce a debit when the value is negative and a credit when it is positive.
Reduce the open balance by the line amount.
records.formula:
line_amount = the numeric value of amount_string
a negative value produces a debit ; a positive value produces a credit

rounding.what: Nothing; the constant is used as written.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the journal item is written.
rounding.step: When the item is written.

result.name: the amount of the counterpart line
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the counterpart journal item of the transaction's entry.

edge_cases.case: The value is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: No journal item is produced for that line and the open balance is unchanged.

edge_cases.case: The value is larger than the transaction.
edge_cases.outcome: The open balance changes sign and the remainder stays on the suspense account.

worked_examples.description: A line carrying a fixed charge of fifteen
worked_examples.narrative: The constant of fifteen is credited and the open balance moves by the same amount.

records.name: The counterpart line amount as a percentage of the open balance
records.purpose: The second of the four amount modes: the line takes a share of what is still unexplained at the moment it is evaluated, which is what makes the line order part of the model's definition.

operands.name: the open balance
operands.source: the running state of the model application
operands.constraints: already reduced by the lines before this one

operands.name: the percentage of the line
operands.source: the amount text of the Reconciliation Model Line
operands.constraints: read as a number

preconditions.condition: The amount text reads as a number.
preconditions.otherwise: The line produces nothing.

procedure: Multiply the open balance by the percentage of the line.
Divide the product by one hundred.
Round the result to the transaction currency: that is the line amount.
Reduce the open balance by the line amount.
records.formula: line_amount = round_to( transaction currency , open_balance × amount_string_value ÷ 100 )

rounding.what: The product of the open balance and the percentage, divided by one hundred.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the transaction currency.
rounding.step: After the multiplication and the division, before the open balance is reduced.

result.name: the amount of the counterpart line
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the counterpart journal item of the transaction's entry.

edge_cases.case: The percentage is one hundred.
edge_cases.outcome: The line takes the whole open balance and the transaction closes, provided no later line adds anything.

edge_cases.case: The line is evaluated first.
edge_cases.outcome: The open balance is still the whole transaction amount, so the line consumes everything and the lines after it re-open the balance.

edge_cases.case: The open balance is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The line amount is zero and no journal item is produced.

worked_examples.description: The bank-fee line of the worked example, taking one hundred percent of what is left
worked_examples.narrative: Eight point zero seven multiplied by one hundred and divided by one hundred is eight point zero seven, which closes the transaction.

records.name: The counterpart line amount as a percentage of the transaction
records.purpose: The third of the four amount modes: the line takes a share of the amount the bank reported, whatever the earlier lines consumed, so that two such lines of half each always split the original amount.

operands.name: the transaction amount
operands.constraints: read directly, not through the open balance

operands.name: the percentage of the line
operands.source: the amount text of the Reconciliation Model Line
operands.constraints: read as a number

preconditions.condition: The amount text reads as a number.
preconditions.otherwise: The line produces nothing.

procedure: Multiply the transaction amount by the percentage of the line.
Divide the product by one hundred.
Round the result to the transaction currency: that is the line amount.
Reduce the open balance by the line amount, even though the amount itself did not read the open balance.
records.formula: line_amount = round_to( transaction currency , transaction_amount × amount_string_value ÷ 100 )

rounding.what: The product of the transaction amount and the percentage, divided by one hundred.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the transaction currency.
rounding.step: After the multiplication and the division, before the open balance is reduced.

result.name: the amount of the counterpart line
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the counterpart journal item of the transaction's entry.

edge_cases.case: Two lines of fifty percent each.
edge_cases.outcome: They always split the original transaction amount exactly, whatever the other lines did.

edge_cases.case: The mode is used where the other percentage mode was intended.
edge_cases.outcome: The open balance does not close: in the worked example a line of one hundred percent of the transaction would take three thousand three hundred and fifty rather than the eight point zero seven that was left.

worked_examples.description: The variant reading of the worked example, with the second line taking one hundred percent of the transaction
worked_examples.narrative: The line reads the transaction amount rather than the open balance, so three thousand three hundred and fifty is taken and the transaction is left unexplained by three thousand three hundred and forty-one point nine three.

records.name: The counterpart line amount read out of the label
records.purpose: The fourth of the four amount modes: the line reads the amount out of the text the bank sent, which is how a gross amount stated in a remittance can be booked exactly.

operands.name: the label of the transaction
operands.constraints: the text the pattern is applied to

operands.name: the pattern of the line
operands.source: the amount text of the Reconciliation Model Line
operands.constraints: read as a pattern with capture groups

preconditions.condition: The pattern matches the label.
preconditions.otherwise: The line produces nothing at all and the open balance is unchanged.

procedure: Apply the pattern of the line to the label of the transaction.
When it does not match, produce nothing.
Otherwise concatenate the capture groups in order.
Replace a comma by a decimal point in the concatenated text.
Read the result as a number: that is the line amount.
Reduce the open balance by the line amount.
records.formula:
if the pattern does not match the label : the line produces nothing
otherwise : line_amount = the number read from ( the capture groups concatenated in order , with a comma replaced by a decimal point )

rounding.what: Nothing; the number is taken as it is written in the label.
rounding.precision: The transaction currency, applied when the journal item is written.
rounding.step: When the item is written.

result.name: the amount of the counterpart line
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the counterpart journal item of the transaction's entry.

edge_cases.case: The pattern does not match.
edge_cases.outcome: The line produces nothing and the remaining amount stays on the suspense account.

edge_cases.case: The captured text uses a comma as the decimal separator.
edge_cases.outcome: The comma is replaced by a decimal point before the text is read as a number.

edge_cases.case: The pattern captures several groups.
edge_cases.outcome: They are concatenated in order before the substitution and the reading.

worked_examples.description: The gross-amount line of the worked example
worked_examples.narrative: The gross income of three thousand three hundred and fifty-eight point zero seven is credited, which turns the open balance positive by eight point zero seven, the amount the bank kept as a fee.

records.name: Reducing the open balance after each model line
records.purpose: States what happens between two lines and at the end of the model: the open balance falls by each line amount, and any remainder stays on the suspense account.

operands.name: the open balance before the line
operands.constraints: starts at minus the transaction amount

operands.name: the amount of the line
operands.constraints: zero when the line produced nothing

operands.name: the counterparty of the line
operands.constraints: the transaction's counterparty is used when the line names none

operands.name: the taxes of the line
operands.constraints: computed on the line amount by the tax engine

operands.name: the analytic distribution of the line
operands.constraints: copied onto the journal item

preconditions.condition: The lines are evaluated in their stored order.
preconditions.otherwise: A line reading the open balance would read a different value.

procedure: After each line, reduce the open balance by that line's amount.
Write on the line's journal item the counterparty of the line when it names one, and the transaction's counterparty otherwise.

When the line names taxes, compute them on the line amount through the tax engine, treating the line amount as tax-included or tax-excluded according to each tax's own setting, and produce the tax journal items alongside the base one.
When the line names an analytic distribution, copy it onto the journal item.
When every line has been evaluated and the open balance is still not zero, leave the remainder on the suspense account, so that the transaction is only partly reconciled.
records.formula:
after each line : open_balance ← open_balance − line_amount
at the end : if open_balance ≠ 0 , the remainder stays on the suspense account and the transaction is only partly reconciled

rounding.what: Nothing here; each line amount was rounded in its own mode.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Earlier, inside each mode.

result.name: the running open balance and the counterpart journal items
result.stored_or_displayed: The items are stored on the transaction's entry; the remainder, when there is one, is the suspense line.

edge_cases.case: A line produced nothing.
edge_cases.outcome: The open balance is unchanged and no item is written for that line.

edge_cases.case: A line carries taxes.
edge_cases.outcome: The tax engine produces the tax items alongside the base one, on the tax accounts, with the tax grids of the repartition lines.

edge_cases.case: The open balance ends non-zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The transaction keeps a suspense line for the remainder and stays unreconciled.

worked_examples.description: The two lines of the worked example
worked_examples.narrative: The two lines together bring the open balance to zero, so the suspense line disappears and the transaction is reconciled.

records.name: End-to-end example: a reconciliation model with a percentage counterpart
records.purpose: Carries one model application through the matching, the two line amounts and the rewritten entry, and shows how the line order and the choice between the two percentage modes change the outcome.

operands.name: the label condition of the model
operands.constraints: containment of a three-letter marker

operands.name: the first line of the model
operands.constraints: an income account, the amount read out of the label

operands.name: the second line of the model
operands.constraints: a finance-expense account, one hundred percent of the open balance

operands.name: the transaction
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency, which is also the journal currency
operands.constraints: an amount of plus three thousand three hundred and fifty and a label carrying the gross amount

preconditions.condition: The label contains the marker the model keys on.
preconditions.otherwise: The model does not apply and the transaction stays on the suspense account.

preconditions.condition: The lines are evaluated in their stored order.
preconditions.otherwise: The percentage line consumes the whole amount first and the transaction is left unexplained.

procedure: Match the model: the label contains the marker, so the model applies.
Read the entry as it stands: the liquidity line debits three thousand three hundred and fifty and the suspense line credits the same.
Start the open balance at minus three thousand three hundred and fifty, meaning that amount still has to be credited somewhere.

Evaluate the first line: the pattern captures the gross amount written with a comma, which becomes three thousand three hundred and fifty-eight point zero seven; the line credits that amount and the open balance becomes plus eight point zero seven.

Evaluate the second line: one hundred percent of the open balance of eight point zero seven, rounded to the company currency, is eight point zero seven; the line debits it and the open balance reaches zero.
Rewrite the entry: the liquidity line is untouched, the suspense line is gone, and two counterpart lines carry the gross income and the bank fee.
The transaction is reconciled, and the difference between what was invoiced and what the bank credited is booked as a bank fee.
records.formula:
open_balance = −3350.00 at the start
line_1_amount = 3358.07  (credit) , read out of the label ; open_balance ← −3350.00 + 3358.07 = +8.07
line_2_amount = round_to( company currency , 8.07 × 100 ÷ 100 ) = 8.07  (debit) ; open_balance ← 8.07 − 8.07 = 0.00

rounding.what: The percentage line's product.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency, one hundredth.
rounding.step: After the multiplication and the division of the percentage line; the value is not moved by the rounding in this example.

result.name: the rewritten entry of three lines and the reconciled transaction
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Journal Entry; the transaction is marked reconciled.

edge_cases.case: The two lines are given in the other order.
edge_cases.outcome: The percentage line consumes the whole three thousand three hundred and fifty first, the other line then adds three thousand three hundred and fifty-eight point zero seven on top, and the open balance ends at minus three thousand three hundred and fifty-eight point zero seven.

edge_cases.case: The second line uses the percentage of the transaction rather than of the open balance.
edge_cases.outcome: Its amount is three thousand three hundred and fifty whatever the first line did, the open balance ends at minus three thousand three hundred and forty-one point nine three, and the transaction is left unreconciled.

worked_examples.description: The model as shipped in the demonstration data

line_two.mode: a percentage of the open balance

worked_examples.narrative: The gross income is credited in full and the eight point zero seven the bank kept is booked as a fee, so the entry balances and the transaction closes.

worked_examples.description: The same model with the lines in the other order

line_order: the line read out of the label

worked_examples.narrative: The line ordering is part of the model's definition, and reversing it leaves the whole gross amount unexplained.

worked_examples.description: The same model with the second line reading the percentage of the transaction
worked_examples.narrative: The two percentage modes are not interchangeable.

records.name: The grouping key of a journal item on the register-payment screen
records.purpose: Decides which selected items belong to the same future payment, by naming the five properties two items must share.

operands.name: the counterparty of the item
operands.constraints: the first part of the key

operands.name: the account of the item
operands.constraints: the second part

operands.name: the currency of the item
operands.constraints: the third part

operands.name: the recipient bank account named on the entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry, when it is an invoice-like document
operands.constraints: empty for any other kind of entry

operands.name: the kind of counterparty
operands.constraints: customer for a receivable account, supplier otherwise

preconditions.condition: The item sits on a receivable or a payable account.
preconditions.otherwise: The screen refuses to open with "You can't open the register payment wizard without at least one receivable/payable line."

procedure: Read the counterparty of the item.
Read the account of the item.
Read the currency of the item.
Read the recipient bank account named on the item's entry when that entry is an invoice-like document, and take it as empty otherwise.
Read the kind of counterparty as customer when the account type is receivable and as supplier otherwise.
Two items belong to the same batch exactly when their five-part keys are equal.
records.formula:
batch_key( item ) = ( counterparty , account , currency , the recipient bank account of the entry when it is an invoice-like document else empty , the counterparty kind )
counterparty kind = customer when the account type is receivable , else supplier

rounding.what: Nothing; the key is made of references and one selection value.
rounding.step: Before the batches are built.

result.name: the five-part grouping key
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides the grouping of the selected items into batches.

edge_cases.case: The entry is not an invoice-like document.
edge_cases.outcome: The recipient bank account part of the key is empty, so plain entries of the same counterparty and account group together.

edge_cases.case: Two documents of one counterparty name different recipient accounts.
edge_cases.outcome: They start in different batches, which the merging step may later join.

edge_cases.case: One counterparty has both a receivable and a payable item.
edge_cases.outcome: Both the account and the kind differ, so the two never share a key.

worked_examples.description: Two customer invoices of one counterparty, in one currency, naming the same recipient account
worked_examples.narrative: The five parts agree, so the two invoices are paid by one payment.

records.name: Building and merging the batches of the register-payment screen
records.purpose: Turns the selected items into the batches that will become payments, joining the two directions of one counterparty when each direction resolves to a single recipient account, so that an invoice and a credit note yield one net payment.

operands.name: the selected journal items
operands.constraints: must belong to one root company and must not be empty

operands.name: the grouping key of each item
operands.constraints: preserved in the order the keys first appear

operands.name: the recipient accounts seen on the inbound side of each counterparty
operands.source: the items whose balance is positive
operands.constraints: recorded as an ordered set

operands.name: the recipient accounts seen on the outbound side of each counterparty
operands.source: the items whose balance is negative
operands.constraints: recorded as an ordered set

operands.name: the balance of each item
operands.constraints: summed to give the direction of the batch

preconditions.condition: The root companies of the selected items are not more than one.
preconditions.otherwise: The screen refuses with "You can't create payments for entries belonging to different companies."

preconditions.condition: At least one receivable or payable item is selected.
preconditions.otherwise: The screen refuses with "You can't open the register payment wizard without at least one receivable/payable line."

procedure: Take the selected journal items and refuse the two conditions above.
Group the items by their grouping key, preserving the order in which the keys first appear.

While grouping, record for each counterparty the ordered set of recipient accounts seen on the inbound side, that is on the items whose balance is positive, and the ordered set seen on the outbound side.
Let the counterparties with exactly one distinct inbound recipient account be the inbound-unique ones, and likewise for the outbound side.
Walk the keys in their order of first appearance, skipping a key already absorbed by an earlier merge.
For the current batch, decide to merge when its counterparty is both inbound-unique and outbound-unique.

When merging, look at every later, not yet absorbed batch and absorb it when its key agrees with the current key on every part except the recipient bank account, appending its items to the current batch and marking its key as seen; the direction is not part of the key at this stage.
Sum the balances of the batch's items and set the direction to inbound when the sum is greater than zero and to outbound otherwise.
When merging, set the batch's recipient bank account to the single account recorded for that counterparty in the resulting direction, and replace the batch's item list with the merged one.
Append the batch to the result.
records.formula:
unique_inbound  = the counterparties with exactly one distinct inbound recipient account
unique_outbound = the counterparties with exactly one distinct outbound recipient account
merge = counterparty ∈ unique_inbound AND counterparty ∈ unique_outbound
balance = Σ balance over the batch's items
direction = inbound when balance > 0 , else outbound

rounding.what: Nothing; the sum of balances is read only for its sign.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each balance was written.
rounding.step: Not applied during the summation.

result.name: the ordered list of batches, each with its items, its direction and its recipient bank account
result.stored_or_displayed: Held by the screen; one payment is created per batch when grouping is on.

edge_cases.case: A counterparty has one open invoice and one open credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: The two batches are merged and one net payment is created, whose direction follows the sign of the total balance.

edge_cases.case: A counterparty has two distinct inbound recipient accounts.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not inbound-unique, so no merge happens and each recipient account keeps its own batch.

edge_cases.case: The total balance of a merged batch is exactly zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction is outbound, because only a strictly positive balance is inbound.

edge_cases.case: The selection spans a parent company and its branch.
edge_cases.outcome: The root companies agree, so the screen opens and the batches are built as usual.

worked_examples.description: One counterparty with an invoice of one thousand and a credit note of three hundred, each naming its own recipient account

expected_outputs.recipient_bank_account: the single inbound account of that counterparty

worked_examples.narrative: The merge yields one payment of seven hundred rather than two payments facing each other.

records.name: The company and the source amounts of a batch
records.purpose: Reads from a batch the company that will carry the payment and the two totals the screen shows as the amount the documents are asking for.

operands.name: the companies of the batch's items
operands.constraints: the one with the fewest ancestors is taken, and the root company when the items come from sibling companies

operands.name: the company-currency residual of each item
operands.constraints: summed, then taken in absolute value

operands.name: the item-currency residual of each item
operands.constraints: summed and taken in absolute value when the batch currency is not the company currency

operands.name: the currency of the batch
operands.constraints: decides which of the two sums is the source amount in currency

preconditions.condition: The batch holds at least one item.
preconditions.otherwise: No amount can be read.

procedure: Take the company of the batch as the company of its items with the fewest ancestors, and as the root company when the items come from sibling companies, that is when they span more than one company and none of those companies is the ancestor of the others.
Sum the company-currency residuals of the batch's items and take the absolute value: that is the source amount.
When the currency of the batch is the company currency, take the source amount in currency as the source amount.
Otherwise sum the item-currency residuals of the batch's items and take the absolute value: that is the source amount in currency.
Read from the batch also the counterparty, the kind of counterparty, the direction and the source currency.
records.formula:
company = the batch item company with the fewest ancestors , or the root company when the items come from sibling companies
source_amount          = | Σ amount_residual over the batch's items |            in the company currency
source_amount_currency = source_amount                                            when the batch currency = the company currency
                       = | Σ amount_residual_currency over the batch's items |    otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing during the summation; the residuals are already rounded.
rounding.precision: The company currency and the batch currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the residuals were computed.
rounding.step: Not applied during the summation.

result.name: the company, the source amount and the source amount in currency of the batch
result.unit_or_currency: company currency and the batch currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the register-payment screen and carried onto the created Payment.

edge_cases.case: The items come from sibling companies.
edge_cases.outcome: The root company is taken, because no sibling is the ancestor of the others.

edge_cases.case: The batch mixes a positive and a negative residual after a merge.
edge_cases.outcome: The sum is netted first and the absolute value is taken afterwards, so the source amount is the net.

edge_cases.case: The batch currency is the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The two source amounts coincide by construction.

worked_examples.description: A merged batch of an invoice of one thousand and a credit note of three hundred, in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The net of seven hundred is what the documents are asking for, and the two figures coincide because the batch is in the company currency.

records.name: The installment reading of a document
records.purpose: Turns the payment-term items of one document into the ordered installments the register-payment screen reasons about, each with its four amounts, its due date and its type.

operands.name: the payment-term journal items of the document
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency, with foreign amounts in the currency of the document
operands.constraints: sorted by due date with the items that have none last, then by date

operands.name: the direction sign of the document
operands.constraints: plus one for a plain entry or an outbound document, minus one otherwise

operands.name: the payment currency
operands.constraints: used by the discount eligibility test

operands.name: the payment date
operands.constraints: separates overdue installments from the ones still to come

operands.name: the next payment date
operands.constraints: when supplied, installments due on or before it are classified as before that date

preconditions.condition: The document has payment-term items.
preconditions.otherwise: The reading produces no installment.

procedure: Take the payment-term journal items of the document, sorted by due date with the items that have none last, then by date.
Read the direction sign as plus one for a plain entry or an outbound document, and minus one otherwise.

Walk the items, numbering them from one, and for each build an installment record holding the number, the item, the due date or the item's date when it has none, the company-currency residual, the item-currency residual, the two unsigned variants obtained by multiplying each residual by minus the direction sign, the type, which starts as the neutral one, and whether the item is reconciled.
When the item is reconciled, leave the type at the neutral one and move on.

When the document is eligible for an early payment discount for the payment currency at the payment date, overwrite the installment's four amounts with the discounted ones, record the discount as the difference between the item's foreign amount and its discount foreign amount and between its balance and its discount balance, set the type to the early-discount one and move on.
Otherwise, when the item is a payment-term item, classify it as an installment.
Return the list of installments.

rounding.what: Nothing; the residuals and the discount amounts are already rounded.
rounding.precision: The company currency and the currency of the document.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the amounts were written.
rounding.step: Not applied during the reading.

result.name: the ordered list of installments of the document
result.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the document
result.stored_or_displayed: Held by the screen; the installments are dispatched into the four buckets that give the totals.

edge_cases.case: A payment-term item has no due date.
edge_cases.outcome: It sorts last and its own date is used as the due date of the installment.

edge_cases.case: The item is already reconciled.
edge_cases.outcome: Its type stays the neutral one and it lands in the common bucket.

edge_cases.case: The document is eligible for a discount.
edge_cases.outcome: The four amounts are replaced by the discounted ones and the discount itself is recorded on the installment.

edge_cases.case: The document is an outbound document.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction sign is plus one, so the unsigned variants are the residuals with their signs flipped.

worked_examples.description: A customer invoice of one thousand with a single payment-term item and a two percent discount within seven days
worked_examples.narrative: The single installment carries the discounted nine hundred and eighty and records the twenty the discount grants.

records.name: Eligibility of a document for an early payment discount
records.purpose: States the five conditions a document must satisfy before its installment is read at the discounted amount.

operands.name: the currency of the document
operands.constraints: must equal the payment currency

operands.name: the kind of the document
operands.constraints: must be an invoice or a receipt, of either direction

operands.name: the payment term of the document
operands.constraints: must declare an early discount

operands.name: the discount date of the first payment-term item
operands.constraints: must not be before the reference date

operands.name: whether any payment-term item of the document is already matched
operands.constraints: must be false

preconditions.condition: A reference date is supplied, or the document has an invoice date.
preconditions.otherwise: The date condition passes on its own.

procedure: Check that the currency of the document equals the payment currency.
Check that the document type is an invoice or a receipt, of either direction.
Check that the payment term of the document declares an early discount.

Check the date: the condition passes when there is no reference date, or when the document has no invoice date, or when the discount date of the first payment-term item is not before the reference date.
Check that no payment-term item of the document is already matched with anything.
The document is eligible exactly when all five hold.
records.formula:
eligible ⟺ the document's currency = the payment currency
       AND the document type is an invoice or a receipt , of either direction
       AND the document's payment term declares an early discount
       AND ( there is no reference date OR the document has no invoice date OR the discount date of the first payment-term item is not before the reference date )
       AND no payment-term item of the document is already matched with anything

rounding.what: Nothing; the test reads a currency, a kind, a term, a date and a count.
rounding.precision: Whole days for the date condition.
rounding.step: Before the installment amounts are overwritten.

result.name: whether the document is eligible for the discount
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides whether the installment carries the discounted amounts and whether the screen enters discount mode.

edge_cases.case: The document is already partly paid.
edge_cases.outcome: A payment-term item is matched, so the document is not eligible and the discount is no longer offered.

edge_cases.case: The payment is made in a currency other than the document's.
edge_cases.outcome: The document is not eligible, because the first condition fails.

edge_cases.case: The payment date is after the discount date.
edge_cases.outcome: The date condition fails and the full amount is read instead.

edge_cases.case: The document has no invoice date.
edge_cases.outcome: The date condition passes, whatever the reference date is.

worked_examples.description: A customer invoice paid three days after its date, under a two percent discount within seven days

inputs.discount_date: the invoice date plus seven days
inputs.reference_date: the invoice date plus three days

worked_examples.narrative: All five conditions hold, so the installment is read at nine hundred and eighty and the discount of twenty is recorded.

records.name: Classifying a payment-term installment
records.purpose: Gives each installment of a document one of three types, and latches the first mode of the document, which decides what the screen proposes and what the switch under the amount offers.

operands.name: the due date of the installment
operands.constraints: the item's own date when it has no due date

operands.name: the payment date
operands.constraints: an installment due strictly before it is overdue

operands.name: the next payment date
operands.constraints: an installment due on or before it is classified as before that date

operands.name: the first mode already latched for the document
operands.unit_or_currency: a stored selection value, or nothing
operands.constraints: latched by the first classified installment

preconditions.condition: The item is a payment-term item and is not reconciled and not eligible for the discount.
preconditions.otherwise: Its type stays the neutral one.

procedure: Classify the installment as before the next payment date when a next payment date was supplied and the installment's due date is not after it.
Otherwise classify it as overdue when its due date is strictly before the payment date, which also latches the first mode of the document to overdue.
Otherwise classify it as the next one when no first mode has been latched yet, which latches the first mode to that.
Otherwise classify it as the next one when the current mode is overdue, so that after a run of overdue installments the following one is offered as the next.
Take the type of the installment as the mode so determined.
records.formula:
before_date : a next payment date was supplied AND the due date is not after it
overdue     : otherwise , the due date is strictly before the payment date ; this latches the document's first mode to overdue
next        : otherwise , when no first mode has been latched yet ; this latches the first mode to next
next        : otherwise , when the current mode is overdue

rounding.what: Nothing; the classification compares dates.
rounding.step: Before the installments are dispatched into the buckets.

result.name: the type of the installment and the first mode of the document
result.stored_or_displayed: Held by the screen and read by the bucket dispatch and by the switch under the amount.

edge_cases.case: An installment is due exactly on the payment date.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not overdue, because the test is strict.

edge_cases.case: A run of overdue installments is followed by one that is not.
edge_cases.outcome: That one is classified as the next, so the screen can offer the overdue total and the following installment separately.

edge_cases.case: A next payment date is supplied.
edge_cases.outcome: Installments due on or before it are classified as before that date and the screen latches that mode.

edge_cases.case: The second installment after one already classified as the next.
edge_cases.outcome: None of the four branches applies, so it keeps the neutral type and lands in the bucket reserved for the full amount only.

worked_examples.description: A document with one installment due before the payment date and one due after
worked_examples.narrative: The first installment is overdue and latches the mode, and the one after a run of overdue installments is offered as the next.

records.name: Converting a list of installments into the screen currency
records.purpose: Totals a bucket of installments in the currency the payment will be made in, going through the company currency whenever neither shortcut applies.

operands.name: the company-currency residual of each installment
operands.constraints: the pivot of the third branch

operands.name: the item-currency residual of each installment
operands.constraints: used directly in the first two branches

operands.name: the currency of the screen
operands.constraints: the target of every conversion

operands.name: the payment date
operands.constraints: the date at which every rate is read

preconditions.condition: A payment date is set.
preconditions.otherwise: No rate can be read and the totals are not recomputed.

procedure: Group the installments by the currency of their item.
For each currency, sum the company-currency residuals and sum the item-currency residuals.
When the currency equals the screen currency, take the sum of item-currency residuals as the contribution.

Otherwise, when the currency is not the company currency and the screen currency is the company currency, convert the sum of item-currency residuals from that currency to the company currency, for the company, at the payment date.

Otherwise convert the sum of company-currency residuals from the company currency to the screen currency, for the company, at the payment date; this third branch covers both an item kept in the company currency paid in another one, and two different foreign currencies meeting, and in both the company-currency residual is the pivot.
Add the contributions of every currency.

rounding.what: Each conversion.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the target currency of that conversion.
rounding.step: Inside each conversion, after the residuals of that currency have been summed.

result.name: the total of the bucket in the screen currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Held by the screen as one of the four totals.

edge_cases.case: Every installment is already in the screen currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The first branch applies and no conversion is made at all.

edge_cases.case: The installments are in two different foreign currencies and the screen is in a third.
edge_cases.outcome: Each group goes through the company currency, so the two are commensurable.

edge_cases.case: The bucket is empty.
edge_cases.outcome: The total is zero.

worked_examples.description: A bucket of two installments in the company currency, with the screen in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The first branch applies to the single group and no conversion is needed.

records.name: Dispatching the installments into the four buckets
records.purpose: Sorts the installments of every document into the four groups whose totals the screen proposes, and latches the first mode that decides the wording of the switch under the amount.

operands.name: the installments of each document
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the document
operands.constraints: walked in order within each document

operands.name: the next payment date read from the calling screen
operands.source: the active domain of the calling screen, when it carries a condition on the next payment date whose value is a text
operands.constraints: read as a date

operands.name: the undiscounted residuals of an eligible installment
operands.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currency of the document
operands.constraints: used to build the copy that goes into the bucket for the difference

operands.name: the type of the previous installment of the same document
operands.constraints: decides where a later installment of the next type lands

preconditions.condition: The union of the batches' items is sorted by document, then by due date with the items that have none last.
preconditions.otherwise: The dispatch would not see the installments of a document in order.

procedure: Read the next payment date from the calling screen: when its active domain carries a condition on the next payment date whose value is a text, read that text as a date; otherwise take none.
Build the union of every batch's items and sort it by document, then by due date with the items that have none last.
Group by document and read the installments of each document.

Send an installment of the early-discount type to the bucket used by default, and a copy of it with the residuals restored to the item's undiscounted values to the bucket used for the difference, and latch the flag saying a discount applies.
Send a payment-term installment of the overdue type to the common bucket.
Send a payment-term installment of the type meaning before the next payment date to the common bucket, and latch the screen's first mode to that type.

Send a payment-term installment of the next type to the bucket reserved for the full amount only when the previous installment of the same document was of the next, the overdue or the before-date type, and to the common bucket when no previous installment was classified, latching the screen's first mode to the next type.
Send anything else to the common bucket.

Let the first classified mode of a document become the screen's first mode when none has been latched yet, so that when several documents are paid together and any one of them offers a next installment, the whole screen is in that mode.
Record also the set of journal items behind the common and the by-default buckets: those are the items that will actually be paid.
records.formula:
early payment discount → the by-default bucket , and an undiscounted copy → the for-difference bucket ; discount_applied ← true
overdue                → the common bucket
before the next payment date → the common bucket ; the screen's first mode ← before_date
next                   → the full-amount-only bucket when the previous installment of the same document was next , overdue or before_date
                       → the common bucket when no previous installment was classified ; the screen's first mode ← next
anything else          → the common bucket

rounding.what: Nothing here; the conversion of each bucket rounds.
rounding.step: In the conversion of each bucket, not in the dispatch.

result.name: the four buckets, the discount-applied flag, the screen's first mode and the items that will be paid
result.unit_or_currency: company currency and the currencies of the documents
result.stored_or_displayed: Held by the screen; the four totals and the proposed amount follow from them.

edge_cases.case: A document offers a next installment while another is overdue.
edge_cases.outcome: The whole screen is put in the mode of the next installment, which is deliberate when several documents are paid together.

edge_cases.case: An installment is reconciled.
edge_cases.outcome: Its type is the neutral one and it lands in the common bucket.

edge_cases.case: A document has several installments of the next type.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the first lands in the common bucket; the later ones land in the bucket reserved for the full amount.

edge_cases.case: A discount applies.
edge_cases.outcome: The same installment is present twice, discounted in one bucket and undiscounted in the other, which is exactly what makes the difference equal the discount.

worked_examples.description: A single customer invoice eligible for a two percent discount
worked_examples.narrative: The discounted installment goes to the by-default bucket and its undiscounted copy to the bucket used for the difference.

records.name: The four totals of the register-payment screen
records.purpose: Produces the four amounts the screen reasons about: what it proposes by default, what the whole selection comes to, and the two undiscounted counterparts used to compute the difference.

operands.name: the total of the common bucket
operands.constraints: present in all four totals

operands.name: the total of the by-default bucket
operands.constraints: the discounted amounts

operands.name: the total of the for-difference bucket
operands.constraints: the undiscounted counterparts

operands.name: the total of the full-amount-only bucket
operands.constraints: added only to the two full totals

preconditions.condition: Each bucket has been converted into the screen currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The four sums would mix currencies.

procedure: Convert each of the four buckets into the screen currency.
Add the common total and the by-default total and take the absolute value: that is the amount proposed by default.
Add the common total, the by-default total and the full-amount-only total and take the absolute value: that is the full amount.
Add the common total and the for-difference total and take the absolute value: that is the amount used for the difference.
Add the common total, the for-difference total and the full-amount-only total and take the absolute value: that is the full amount used for the difference.
records.formula:
amount_by_default          = | common + by_default |
full_amount                = | common + by_default + full_only |
amount_for_difference      = | common + for_difference |
full_amount_for_difference = | common + for_difference + full_only |

rounding.what: Each bucket total, inside its own conversion.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the screen currency.
rounding.step: Inside the conversion of each bucket, before the four sums are taken.

result.name: the four totals
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the register-payment screen and read by the proposed amount, the installment mode, the switch and the payment difference.

edge_cases.case: No discount applies.
edge_cases.outcome: The by-default and the for-difference buckets hold the same amounts, so the four totals collapse into two.

edge_cases.case: The full-amount-only bucket is empty.
edge_cases.outcome: The full amount equals the amount proposed by default and the switch offers nothing.

edge_cases.case: The buckets net to a negative figure.
edge_cases.outcome: The absolute value is taken, so the totals are always positive and the direction carries the sign.

worked_examples.description: A single invoice of one thousand with a two percent discount
worked_examples.narrative: The default and the full amount are both the discounted nine hundred and eighty, while the two difference totals carry the undiscounted one thousand.

records.name: The proposed amount of the register-payment screen
records.purpose: Decides what figure the amount field holds, and when the automatic computation stops overwriting what the user typed.

operands.name: the amount proposed by default
operands.constraints: the value written when the computation runs

operands.name: the previous amount
operands.constraints: kept when the computation cannot run or the user typed a custom amount

operands.name: whether a journal, a currency and a payment date are set
operands.constraints: all three are needed

operands.name: whether the user typed a custom amount
operands.constraints: true when the typed value differs from all four totals

preconditions.condition: A journal, a currency and a payment date are all set and the user has not typed a custom amount.
preconditions.otherwise: The previous amount is kept unchanged.

procedure: When there is no journal, no currency or no payment date, or the user has typed a custom amount, keep the previous amount.
Otherwise write the amount proposed by default into the amount field.
records.formula:
amount = the previous amount   when there is no journal , no currency , no payment date , or the user has typed a custom amount
       = amount_by_default     otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing here; the default total was rounded when its buckets were converted.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Earlier, in the conversion of the buckets.

result.name: the amount of the payment to be created
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed and editable on the register-payment screen, and carried onto every created Payment.

edge_cases.case: The user types a figure equal to one of the four totals.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not a custom amount and the automatic computation may overwrite it again.

edge_cases.case: The user types a figure equal to none of the four totals.
edge_cases.outcome: It is remembered as a custom amount and the computation stops overwriting it.

edge_cases.case: The payment date is cleared.
edge_cases.outcome: The previous amount is kept, because no rate can be read.

worked_examples.description: A discounted invoice with everything set and no custom amount
worked_examples.narrative: The screen proposes the discounted amount.

worked_examples.description: The user overwrites one hundred by ninety-nine point nine seven
worked_examples.narrative: The typed value differs from all four totals, so it is remembered and the computation no longer overwrites it.

records.name: The installment mode of the register-payment screen
records.purpose: Names which of the proposed readings the current amount corresponds to, which the switch under the amount and the payment difference both read.

operands.name: the amount currently in the field
operands.constraints: compared at the precision of the screen currency

operands.name: the full amount
operands.constraints: tested first

operands.name: the amount proposed by default
operands.constraints: tested second

operands.name: the first mode latched by the dispatch
operands.constraints: returned when the amount equals the default

preconditions.condition: The four totals have been computed.
preconditions.otherwise: No comparison can be made.

procedure: Compare the amount with the full amount at the precision of the screen currency; when they are equal, the mode is the full one.
Otherwise compare the amount with the amount proposed by default; when they are equal, the mode is the first mode latched by the dispatch.
Otherwise the mode is the full one.
records.formula:
installments_mode = full                      when compare( currency , amount , full_amount ) = 0
                  = the screen's first mode  when compare( currency , amount , amount_by_default ) = 0
                  = full                      otherwise

rounding.what: Each difference, inside its comparison.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the screen currency.
rounding.step: Inside each comparison.

result.name: the installment mode
result.stored_or_displayed: Held by the screen and read by the switch, by the payment difference and by the memo rule.

edge_cases.case: The full amount equals the amount proposed by default.
edge_cases.outcome: The first test already passes and the mode is the full one, even when the dispatch latched another mode.

edge_cases.case: The user typed a custom amount.
edge_cases.outcome: It matches neither total, so the mode is the full one and the difference is computed against the full undiscounted total.

edge_cases.case: The amount equals the default while the dispatch latched the overdue mode.
edge_cases.outcome: The mode is the overdue one and the switch offers the full amount.

worked_examples.description: A discounted invoice where the default and the full amount coincide
worked_examples.narrative: The first test passes at once.

worked_examples.description: A write-off of three hundredths
worked_examples.narrative: The typed amount equals neither total, so the third branch applies.

records.name: The switch offered under the amount
records.purpose: States, for each installment mode, which amount the clickable switch would write and which text is shown beside it.

operands.name: the installment mode
operands.constraints: selects the row

operands.name: the full amount
operands.constraints: the switch amount of three of the five rows

operands.name: the amount proposed by default
operands.constraints: the switch amount of the full mode

operands.name: whether a discount applies
operands.constraints: chooses between the two texts of the full mode

operands.name: the next payment date, or today
operands.constraints: named in the text of the before-date mode

preconditions.condition: The user has not typed a custom amount.
preconditions.otherwise: No switch text is shown at all.

procedure: When the mode is the full one and the full amount already equals both the amount proposed by default and the typed amount, offer a switch amount of zero and show nothing.

When the mode is the full one otherwise and the amount is not zero, offer the amount proposed by default, and show "This is the full amount." followed by "Consider paying the amount with early payment discount instead." when a discount applies and by "Consider paying in installments instead." otherwise, the last words of each being the clickable part.
When the mode is the overdue one, offer the full amount and show "This is the overdue amount." followed by "Consider paying the full amount."

When the mode is the one meaning before the next payment date, offer the full amount and show "Total for the installments before *the next payment date, or today*." followed by "Consider paying the full amount."
When the mode is the next one, offer the full amount and show "This is the next unreconciled installment." followed by "Consider paying the full amount."
Show no switch text at all when the user has typed a custom amount.
records.formula:
full , and full_amount = amount_by_default = the typed amount : switch amount = 0.00 , nothing shown
full , otherwise , with a non-zero amount          : switch amount = amount_by_default
overdue                                            : switch amount = full_amount
before the next payment date                       : switch amount = full_amount
next                                               : switch amount = full_amount

rounding.what: Nothing; the switch writes one of the totals unchanged.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Earlier, in the conversion of the buckets.

result.name: the switch amount and the text beside it
result.unit_or_currency: the screen currency for the amount
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed under the amount field; clicking the bold fragment writes the switch amount into the field.

edge_cases.case: The three amounts already coincide.
edge_cases.outcome: The switch amount is zero and nothing is shown, because there is no other reading to offer.

edge_cases.case: The user typed a custom amount.
edge_cases.outcome: No switch text is shown at all.

edge_cases.case: A discount applies and the mode is the full one.
edge_cases.outcome: The text offers the discounted reading rather than the installment reading.

worked_examples.description: A document with one overdue installment of four hundred out of a full amount of one thousand
worked_examples.narrative: The switch would write the full one thousand into the amount field.

worked_examples.description: A discounted invoice where the three amounts coincide
worked_examples.narrative: There is no other reading to offer, so nothing is displayed.

records.name: The early-discount mode of the register-payment screen
records.purpose: Says when the screen is granting a discount rather than writing off a difference, which forces the difference handling and hides the write-off section.

operands.name: the discount-applied flag
operands.constraints: latched when at least one installment was read at the discounted amount

operands.name: the amount currently in the field
operands.constraints: compared with two of the four totals

operands.name: the amount proposed by default
operands.constraints: either comparison qualifies

operands.name: the full amount
operands.constraints: either comparison qualifies

preconditions.condition: At least one document was read at its discounted amount.
preconditions.otherwise: The mode is off and any difference is a write-off.

procedure: Check the discount-applied flag.
Compare the amount with the amount proposed by default and with the full amount, at the precision of the screen currency.
The mode is on when the flag is set and at least one of the two comparisons reports equality.
When the mode is on, force the difference handling to the reconciling one and hide the write-off section, because the difference is not a write-off but the discount itself.
records.formula: early_payment_discount_mode = discount_applied AND ( compare( currency , amount , amount_by_default ) = 0 OR compare( currency , amount , full_amount ) = 0 )

rounding.what: Each difference, inside its comparison.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the screen currency.
rounding.step: Inside each comparison.

result.name: the early-discount mode of the screen
result.stored_or_displayed: Held by the screen; it forces the difference handling and hides the write-off section.

edge_cases.case: A discount applies but the user typed a different amount.
edge_cases.outcome: Neither comparison reports equality, so the mode is off and the difference becomes an ordinary write-off or is kept open.

edge_cases.case: No document was eligible.
edge_cases.outcome: The flag is false and the mode is off whatever the amount is.

edge_cases.case: The mode is on.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference handling is forced to the reconciling one and the discount counterpart lines are produced instead of a write-off line.

worked_examples.description: A discounted invoice paid at the proposed amount
worked_examples.narrative: The screen is in discount mode, so the twenty of difference is booked by the discount rule rather than as a write-off.

records.name: The payment difference of the register-payment screen
records.purpose: Gives the gap between what the documents ask for, undiscounted, and what is actually being paid; in discount mode that gap is exactly the discount granted.

operands.name: the amount used for the difference
operands.constraints: the undiscounted counterpart of the amount proposed by default

operands.name: the full amount used for the difference
operands.constraints: the undiscounted counterpart of the full amount

operands.name: the amount currently in the field
operands.constraints: subtracted from the chosen total

operands.name: the installment mode
operands.constraints: selects which of the two totals is used

operands.name: whether a payment date is set
operands.constraints: when it is not, the difference is zero

preconditions.condition: A payment date is set.
preconditions.otherwise: The difference is zero.

procedure: When there is no payment date, take the difference as zero.
When the mode is the overdue one, the next one or the one meaning before the next payment date, subtract the amount from the amount used for the difference.
When the mode is the full one, subtract the amount from the full amount used for the difference.
Otherwise subtract the amount from the amount used for the difference.

Show the difference section when the difference is not zero, the screen is not in discount mode, the screen is editable, grouping is either unavailable or switched on, and the chosen payment method line has an outstanding account.
records.formula:
payment_difference = amount_for_difference      − amount   when the mode is overdue , next or before the next payment date
                   = full_amount_for_difference − amount   when the mode is full
                   = amount_for_difference      − amount   otherwise
                   = 0.00                                  when there is no payment date

rounding.what: Nothing here; both totals were rounded when their buckets were converted.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Earlier, in the conversion of the buckets.

result.name: the payment difference
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the register-payment screen and turned into a write-off line or into discount counterpart lines.

edge_cases.case: The screen is in discount mode.
edge_cases.outcome: The totals used for the difference are the undiscounted ones, so the difference equals the discount granted exactly.

edge_cases.case: There is no payment date.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference is zero and no write-off is proposed.

edge_cases.case: The chosen payment method line has no outstanding account.
edge_cases.outcome: The difference section is not shown, because no write-off line could be booked.

worked_examples.description: A discounted invoice of one thousand paid at nine hundred and eighty
worked_examples.narrative: The difference equals the discount, because the total used for the difference is the undiscounted one.

worked_examples.description: An invoice of one hundred paid at ninety-nine point nine seven
worked_examples.narrative: The three hundredths are the amount the user will write off.

records.name: The difference kept open
records.purpose: The first of the three ways a difference is handled: nothing is booked for it and the document keeps a residual.

operands.name: the difference handling chosen on the screen
operands.constraints: the one meaning the difference is left open

operands.name: the payment difference
operands.constraints: not booked at all

preconditions.condition: The chosen handling is the one that leaves the difference open.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other two cases applies.

procedure: Produce no write-off line at all.
Let the reconciliation match as much as it can.
Leave the document with a residual equal to the difference.
records.formula: no write-off line is produced ; the reconciliation matches as much as it can and the document keeps a residual

rounding.what: Nothing; no amount is booked for the difference.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the residual left on the document
result.stored_or_displayed: Recomputed onto the document's payment-term item, whose payment state becomes the partially paid one.

edge_cases.case: The difference is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The handling makes no difference, because nothing would have been booked in any case.

edge_cases.case: The payment exceeds the documents.
edge_cases.outcome: The surplus stays on the payment's own counterpart line as a residual.

worked_examples.description: An invoice of one hundred paid at ninety-nine point nine seven with the difference left open
worked_examples.narrative: The entry has only two lines and the invoice keeps three hundredths open.

records.name: The difference in discount mode: the open amount and the open balance
records.purpose: The second of the three ways a difference is handled: it is the discount granted, and this calculation gives the two amounts the discount counterpart lines must together consume.

operands.name: the payment difference
operands.constraints: equal to the discount granted

operands.name: the direction of the payment
operands.constraints: gives the sign of the open amount

operands.name: the payment date
operands.constraints: the date at which the conversion is made

operands.name: the foreign residual of each eligible payment-term item
operands.constraints: negated to give the matched foreign amount

preconditions.condition: The screen is in discount mode.
preconditions.otherwise: The difference is handled as a write-off or left open.

preconditions.condition: At least one document of the batch is eligible for the discount at the payment date.
preconditions.otherwise: No pair is recorded and no discount line is produced.

procedure: For every journal item of the batch whose document is eligible for the discount at the payment date, record the pair made of the item, the matched foreign amount taken as minus the item's foreign residual, and the matched balance taken as that amount converted to the company currency at the payment date.
Take the open amount in the payment currency as the payment difference multiplied by plus one when the direction is inbound and by minus one when it is outbound.
Convert the open amount from the payment currency to the company currency, for the company, at the payment date: that is the open balance.
Produce the discount counterpart lines from those pairs and that open balance; all of them become write-off lines of the Payment.

rounding.what: The conversion of the open amount and of each matched balance.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Inside each conversion, at the payment date.

result.name: the recorded pairs, the open amount and the open balance
result.unit_or_currency: the payment currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Held for the production of the discount counterpart lines, which become write-off lines of the Payment.

edge_cases.case: The payment is outbound.
edge_cases.outcome: The open amount carries the opposite sign, so the discount is a gain rather than a loss.

edge_cases.case: The payment currency is the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion is an identity and the open balance equals the open amount.

edge_cases.case: The discount lines do not exactly consume the open balance.
edge_cases.outcome: The leftover becomes one further line on an exchange-difference account.

worked_examples.description: An inbound payment taking a discount of twenty on an invoice of one thousand, everything in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The whole one thousand of the payment-term item is matched, and twenty is the open balance the discount lines must consume.

records.name: The difference pushed onto an exchange account, with a foreign payment currency: the forced balance
records.purpose: The first variant of the third way a difference is handled: when the chosen account is an exchange-difference account and the payment is not in the company currency, the payment's company-currency amount is forced onto the documents' figure so that the whole difference lands on the exchange side.

operands.name: the company-currency residual of each item of the batch
operands.constraints: summed to give the forced balance

operands.name: the chosen difference account
operands.constraints: must be one of the company's two exchange-difference accounts

operands.name: the payment currency
operands.constraints: must differ from the company currency for this variant

preconditions.condition: The chosen difference account is one of the company's two exchange-difference accounts.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary write-off variant applies.

preconditions.condition: The payment currency differs from the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The forced-rate variant applies instead.

procedure: Produce no write-off line.
Sum the company-currency residuals of the batch's items.
Create the Payment with that sum as its forced balance, so that its liquidity side is booked at exactly the company-currency amount the documents carry.
The whole difference then lands on the exchange side when the reconciliation runs.
records.formula:
forced balance = Σ amount_residual over the batch's items
no write-off line is produced ; the Payment's liquidity side is booked at the forced balance

rounding.what: Nothing during the summation; each residual is already rounded.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the residuals were computed.
rounding.step: Not applied during the summation.

result.name: the forced balance of the Payment
result.stored_or_displayed: Passed to the creation of the Payment and used by the liquidity balance of its entry.

edge_cases.case: Write-off lines were also supplied.
edge_cases.outcome: The forced balance is ignored by the liquidity balance, which falls back to the conversion at the payment date.

edge_cases.case: The sum of residuals is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The forced balance is zero and the liquidity balance is zero as well.

worked_examples.description: A payment in a foreign currency settling documents worth one thousand two hundred of the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The payment's liquidity side is booked at exactly one thousand two hundred, and the gap between that and the converted foreign amount becomes an exchange difference.

records.name: The difference pushed onto an exchange account, with the company currency: the forced rate
records.purpose: The second variant of the third way a difference is handled: when the chosen account is an exchange-difference account and the payment is in the company currency, a rate is forced onto the reconciliation so that the whole difference becomes an exchange-difference entry.

operands.name: the item-currency residual of each item of the batch
operands.constraints: summed to give the numerator

operands.name: the amount of the payment
operands.unit_or_currency: the company currency, which is here the payment currency
operands.constraints: the denominator; a zero amount yields a rate of zero

preconditions.condition: The chosen difference account is one of the company's two exchange-difference accounts.
preconditions.otherwise: The ordinary write-off variant applies.

preconditions.condition: The payment currency is the company currency.
preconditions.otherwise: The forced-balance variant applies instead.

procedure: Produce no write-off line.
Sum the item-currency residuals of the batch's items.
Divide the absolute value of that sum by the amount of the payment, and take zero when the amount is zero: that is the forced rate.

Pass the forced rate to the reconciliation, which uses it in place of the rate table when it builds the residual map of an item kept in the company currency, pushing the whole difference into an exchange-difference entry.
records.formula:
forced_rate = | ( Σ amount_residual_currency over the batch's items ) ÷ amount |   when amount ≠ 0
            = 0                                                                     otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing; the rate is carried at full precision.
rounding.step: Never; the amounts the rate is later applied to are what get rounded.

result.name: the forced rate
result.unit_or_currency: units of the item currency per unit of the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Passed to the reconciliation and used in place of the rate table.

edge_cases.case: The amount of the payment is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The forced rate is zero, and every conversion through it yields zero.

edge_cases.case: The items are in the company currency as well.
edge_cases.outcome: The rate is the ratio of the residual sum to the amount, which is one when they agree.

worked_examples.description: Documents totalling one thousand two hundred of a foreign currency settled by a payment of one thousand of the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The reconciliation offers the company-currency items at one point two units of the foreign currency each, so the whole gap becomes an exchange difference.

records.name: The difference written off to an ordinary account
records.purpose: The third variant of the third way a difference is handled: one write-off line is produced on the chosen account, with the sign that makes the counterpart settle the documents exactly.
