operands.name: the payment difference
operands.constraints: not zero

operands.name: the direction of the payment
operands.constraints: gives the sign of the write-off amount

operands.name: the payment date
operands.constraints: the date at which the conversion is made

operands.name: the chosen difference account
operands.constraints: not an exchange-difference account

operands.name: the write-off label
operands.constraints: the default is the text "Write-Off"

preconditions.condition: The difference handling is the reconciling one, the screen is not in discount mode and the difference is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the other cases applies.

preconditions.condition: The chosen account is not one of the company's two exchange-difference accounts.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the two forced variants applies.

procedure: Take the write-off amount in the payment currency as the payment difference when the direction is inbound, and as minus the payment difference when it is outbound.
Convert that amount from the payment currency to the company currency, for the company, at the payment date: that is the write-off balance.
Produce one write-off line carrying the write-off label, the chosen difference account, the counterparty of the screen and the payment currency.
records.formula:
write_off_amount_currency =   payment_difference   when the direction is inbound
                          = − payment_difference   when the direction is outbound
write_off_balance = convert( write_off_amount_currency , from the payment currency to the company currency , for the company , at the payment date )

rounding.what: The conversion of the write-off amount.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Inside the conversion, at the payment date.

result.name: the single write-off line of the Payment
result.unit_or_currency: the payment currency, with a balance in the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored as a write-off value of the Payment and written as a journal item of its entry.

edge_cases.case: The payment is outbound.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign flips, so the difference account is credited rather than debited and the counterpart is a debit on the payable account.

edge_cases.case: The payment currency is the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion is an identity and the two write-off amounts coincide.

edge_cases.case: The difference is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: This case does not apply at all and no write-off line is produced.

worked_examples.description: An inbound payment of ninety-nine point nine seven against an invoice of one hundred
worked_examples.narrative: The write-off is a debit of three hundredths, so the counterpart credits exactly one hundred and the invoice closes.

worked_examples.description: An outbound payment of ninety-nine point nine seven against a bill of one hundred
worked_examples.narrative: The sign flips and the counterpart is a debit of one hundred on the payable account.

records.name: Choosing the cash-discount account of a document
records.purpose: Decides on which of the company's two cash-discount accounts the discount of a document is booked, by the direction of the document rather than of the payment.

operands.name: the kind of the document
operands.constraints: inbound for a customer invoice, a customer receipt or a vendor credit note; outbound for a vendor bill, a vendor receipt or a customer credit note

operands.name: the cash-discount loss account of the company
operands.constraints: chosen for an inbound document

operands.name: the cash-discount gain account of the company
operands.constraints: chosen otherwise

operands.name: the discount percentage of the payment term
operands.source: the payment term of the document
operands.constraints: when it is zero, nothing at all is produced

preconditions.condition: The discount percentage of the payment term is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: No discount counterpart line is produced for the document.

procedure: Read the discount percentage of the payment term; when it is zero, produce nothing.

Classify the document: an inbound document is one the company expects money for, that is a customer invoice, a customer receipt or a vendor credit note; an outbound document is one the company expects to pay, that is a vendor bill, a vendor receipt or a customer credit note.
Choose the cash-discount loss account of the company for an inbound document, because granting a discount on money owed to the company is a loss.
Choose the cash-discount gain account of the company otherwise, because obtaining a discount on money the company owes is a gain.

Determine an analytic distribution for the discount from the analytic distribution models, keyed on the code of the discount account, the company, the commercial counterparty and the tags of the counterparty.
records.formula:
discount_account = the company's cash-discount LOSS account   when the document is an INBOUND document
                 = the company's cash-discount GAIN account   otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule selects an account.
rounding.step: Before the discount lines are built.

result.name: the discount account and its analytic distribution
result.stored_or_displayed: Carried on every discount counterpart line of that document.

edge_cases.case: A discount is taken on a vendor bill.
edge_cases.outcome: The gain account is used and the entry mirrors the customer case: the liquidity and the discount line are both credits and the counterpart is a debit.

edge_cases.case: The payment term declares no discount percentage.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is produced for that document.

edge_cases.case: A vendor credit note.
edge_cases.outcome: It counts as an inbound document, because the company expects money for it, so the loss account is used.

worked_examples.description: A customer invoice with a two percent discount

expected_outputs.discount_account: the cash-discount loss account of the company

worked_examples.narrative: Granting the discount costs the company, so the loss account is used.

records.name: The base delta of a rebuilt product line
records.purpose: Computes, line by line, how much of a document's untaxed base the discount removes, by rebuilding the line at the discounted unit price and comparing it with the original.

operands.name: the unit price of the original product line
operands.constraints: multiplied by the discounted fraction

operands.name: the discount percentage of the payment term
operands.constraints: one hundred minus it, divided by one hundred, is the factor

operands.name: the direction sign of the document
operands.constraints: applied to the discounted totals before the subtraction

operands.name: the foreign amount and the balance of the original line
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the document and the company currency
operands.constraints: subtracted from the signed discounted totals

preconditions.condition: The document has product lines.
preconditions.otherwise: No base delta is produced.

preconditions.condition: Fixed-amount taxes are excluded from the recomputation.
preconditions.otherwise: A fixed tax would be scaled down with the base, which it is not.

procedure: Rebuild the product lines of the document with their unit price multiplied by one hundred minus the discount percentage, divided by one hundred, treating them as refund lines, and recompute their taxes, excluding fixed-amount taxes from the recomputation.

For each rebuilt line, multiply the discounted untaxed total in the currency of the document by the direction sign and subtract the foreign amount of the original line, then round the result to the currency of the document: that is the base delta in the currency.
Do the same with the discounted untaxed total in the company currency and the balance of the original line, rounding to the company currency: that is the base delta in the company currency.

Accumulate both deltas under a grouping key made of the counterparty, the currency, the discount account and the analytic distribution, and, when the discount computation mode of the payment term includes the taxes and the product lines carry taxes, also of the taxes of the line and of its tax grids.
records.formula:
discounted unit price = the original unit price × ( 100 − discount_percentage ) ÷ 100
base_delta_amount_currency = round_to( document currency , direction_sign × discounted_total_excluded_in_currency − the original line's foreign amount )
base_delta_balance         = round_to( company currency  , direction_sign × discounted_total_excluded            − the original line's balance )

rounding.what: Each of the two deltas, after the subtraction.
rounding.precision: The currency of the document and the company currency respectively.
rounding.step: After the subtraction, before the delta is accumulated under its grouping key.

result.name: the two base deltas of the line
result.unit_or_currency: the currency of the document and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Accumulated per grouping key and turned into the base counterpart lines of the discount.

edge_cases.case: The document carries a fixed-amount tax.
edge_cases.outcome: That tax is excluded from the recomputation, so it is not scaled down with the base.

edge_cases.case: The discount computation mode includes the taxes and the lines carry taxes.
edge_cases.outcome: The taxes and the tax grids of the line join the grouping key, so the discount line can carry them and correct the tax report.

edge_cases.case: The document is an outbound document.
edge_cases.outcome: The direction sign is plus one and the deltas come out with the opposite sign, which is what makes the discount a gain.

worked_examples.description: A customer invoice with a single product line of one thousand and a two percent discount
worked_examples.narrative: Minus one times nine hundred and eighty, less minus one thousand, is twenty: exactly the base the discount removes.

records.name: The fraction of the document being settled
records.purpose: Scales the discount lines down to the share of the document the payment actually settles, so that a partial settlement grants only its share of the discount.

operands.name: the foreign residual of the payment-term item
operands.constraints: the numerator

operands.name: the total of the document
operands.constraints: the denominator

preconditions.condition: The total of the document is not zero.
preconditions.otherwise: No fraction can be computed.

procedure: Divide the foreign residual of the payment-term item by the total of the document.
Take the absolute value, so the fraction is positive whichever direction the document has.
records.formula: percentage_paid = | the payment-term item's foreign residual ÷ the document total |

rounding.what: Nothing; the fraction is carried at full precision.
rounding.step: Never; the amounts it multiplies are what get rounded.

result.name: the fraction of the document being settled
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it scales every discount counterpart line.

edge_cases.case: The whole document is being settled.
edge_cases.outcome: The fraction is one and the discount lines carry the whole delta.

edge_cases.case: The document has several payment-term items and only one is settled.
edge_cases.outcome: The fraction is that item's share and the discount lines are scaled accordingly.

worked_examples.description: A single payment-term item covering a whole invoice of one thousand
worked_examples.narrative: The whole document is settled, so the discount lines carry the full delta.

records.name: The tax counterpart lines of an early payment discount
records.purpose: Produces the lines that correct the tax when the payment term computes the discount on the taxed amount, so that the tax report reflects the discount granted.

operands.name: the tax lines of the rebuilt base lines
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the document and the company currency
operands.source: the recomputation at the discounted unit price
operands.constraints: computed only when the discount computation mode includes the taxes and the product lines carry taxes

operands.name: the tax amount the document already carries for the mirrored repartition line
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the document and the company currency
operands.source: the Journal Items of the document
operands.constraints: subtracted from each rebuilt tax line

operands.name: the fraction of the document being settled
operands.constraints: multiplies both amounts of each delta

operands.name: the name of the tax
operands.constraints: reproduced inside the label of the line

preconditions.condition: The discount computation mode of the payment term includes the taxes and the product lines carry taxes.
preconditions.otherwise: No tax line is produced and the whole discount sits on the discount account without affecting the tax report.

procedure: Compute the tax lines of the rebuilt base lines.
Subtract from each the tax amount the document already carries for the mirrored repartition line, keeping the delta.
Multiply the delta in the currency of the document by the fraction of the document being settled and round the product to the currency of the document.
Multiply the delta in the company currency by the same fraction and round the product to the company currency.
Make each such delta a counterpart line labelled "Early Payment Discount (*the name of the tax*)" on the tax account.
records.formula:
for each tax delta :
    amount_currency = round_to( document currency , delta_amount_currency × percentage_paid )
    balance         = round_to( company currency  , delta_balance         × percentage_paid )
label = "Early Payment Discount (" ‖ the name of the tax ‖ ")"

rounding.what: Each of the two amounts of the tax line.
rounding.precision: The currency of the document and the company currency respectively.
rounding.step: After the multiplication by the fraction, before the line is emitted.

result.name: the tax counterpart lines of the discount
result.unit_or_currency: the currency of the document and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written as write-off lines of the Payment, on the tax accounts.

edge_cases.case: The discount computation mode excludes the taxes.
edge_cases.outcome: No tax line is produced and the whole discount sits on the discount account, leaving the tax report untouched.

edge_cases.case: Only part of the document is being settled.
edge_cases.outcome: The tax deltas are scaled by the fraction, so the tax correction matches the share settled.

worked_examples.description: An invoice of one thousand net plus twenty-one percent tax, with a two percent discount computed on the taxed amount, settled in full

expected_outputs.label: Early Payment Discount (the name of the tax)

worked_examples.narrative: Two percent of the two hundred and ten of tax is four point two, which is booked on the tax account so that the tax report carries the discount.

records.name: The base counterpart lines of an early payment discount
records.purpose: Turns each accumulated base delta into a counterpart line on the cash-discount account, scaled to the share of the document being settled.

operands.name: the accumulated base delta of a grouping key
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the document and the company currency
operands.constraints: summed across the lines sharing the key

operands.name: the fraction of the document being settled
operands.constraints: multiplies both amounts

operands.name: the discount account and the analytic distribution of the grouping key
operands.constraints: carried on the line

preconditions.condition: At least one base delta was accumulated.
preconditions.otherwise: No base line is produced.

procedure: Take the accumulated base delta of the grouping key.
Multiply the delta in the currency of the document by the fraction of the document being settled and round the product to the currency of the document.
Multiply the delta in the company currency by the same fraction and round the product to the company currency.

Emit one counterpart line labelled "Early Payment Discount", carrying the discount account, the counterparty, the currency and the analytic distribution of the grouping key, and, when the mode includes the taxes, the taxes and the tax grids of the key.
Sum across documents the lines that share a grouping key.
records.formula:
for each accumulated base delta :
    amount_currency = round_to( document currency , base_delta_amount_currency × percentage_paid )
    balance         = round_to( company currency  , base_delta_balance         × percentage_paid )
label = "Early Payment Discount"

rounding.what: Each of the two amounts of the base line.
rounding.precision: The currency of the document and the company currency respectively.
rounding.step: After the multiplication by the fraction, before the line is emitted.

result.name: the base counterpart lines of the discount
result.unit_or_currency: the currency of the document and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written as write-off lines of the Payment, on the cash-discount account.

edge_cases.case: Several documents share a grouping key.
edge_cases.outcome: Their lines are summed, so one line is written per key rather than one per document.

edge_cases.case: The mode includes the taxes.
edge_cases.outcome: The line carries the taxes and the tax grids of the original product lines, so that the tax report is corrected.

edge_cases.case: Only part of the document is settled.
edge_cases.outcome: The line carries that share of the delta.

worked_examples.description: A single product line of one thousand at a two percent discount, settled in full
worked_examples.narrative: The whole twenty of base delta becomes one discount line.

records.name: The rounding fix of the discount counterpart lines
records.purpose: Guarantees that the discount counterpart lines sum exactly to the discount the payment-term item records, by pushing any residue onto the largest base line.

operands.name: the foreign amount and the discount foreign amount of the payment-term item
operands.constraints: their difference is the discount in the currency

operands.name: the balance and the discount balance of the payment-term item
operands.constraints: their difference is the discount in the company currency

operands.name: the amounts of the base lines already produced
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the document and the company currency
operands.constraints: subtracted from the two discounts

operands.name: the amounts of the tax lines already produced
operands.unit_or_currency: the currency of the document and the company currency
operands.constraints: subtracted as well

preconditions.condition: At least one base line was produced.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nowhere to add the residue.

procedure: Take the discount in the currency as the foreign amount of the payment-term item minus its discount foreign amount.
Take the discount in the company currency as the balance of the payment-term item minus its discount balance.
Subtract from each the sum of the base line amounts and the sum of the tax line amounts, giving the two residues.
Add both residues to the base line with the largest foreign amount.
records.formula:
term_amount_currency = payment_term_item.amount_currency − payment_term_item.discount_amount_currency
term_balance         = payment_term_item.balance         − payment_term_item.discount_balance
delta_amount_currency = term_amount_currency − Σ base line amounts − Σ tax line amounts
delta_balance         = term_balance         − Σ base line balances − Σ tax line balances
both deltas are added to the base line with the largest foreign amount

rounding.what: Nothing here; the fix corrects the residue that the earlier roundings left.
rounding.precision: The currency of the document and the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the lines were produced.
rounding.step: After all the lines have been produced, as the last step before the leftover exchange line.

result.name: the corrected base line amounts
result.unit_or_currency: the currency of the document and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the write-off line of the Payment.

edge_cases.case: The lines already sum to the discount exactly.
edge_cases.outcome: Both residues are zero and nothing is added.

edge_cases.case: Several base lines exist.
edge_cases.outcome: The residue lands on the one with the largest foreign amount, where it is proportionally smallest.

edge_cases.case: The tax lines absorbed part of the discount.
edge_cases.outcome: Their sum is subtracted as well, so the residue covers the whole set of lines.

worked_examples.description: A single base line of twenty against a payment-term item recording a discount of twenty
worked_examples.narrative: The lines already sum exactly to the discount, so nothing is added.

records.name: The leftover exchange line of an early payment discount
records.purpose: Books whatever the discount lines did not consume of the open balance, on one of the company's two exchange-difference accounts, so that the payment entry balances.

operands.name: the open balance
operands.constraints: reduced by the balance of every discount line

operands.name: the balance of each discount line
operands.source: the base and tax counterpart lines
operands.constraints: reduces the running open balance

operands.name: the expense exchange-difference account of the company
operands.constraints: chosen when the remaining open balance is positive

operands.name: the income exchange-difference account of the company
operands.constraints: chosen when it is negative

preconditions.condition: The running open balance is not zero once every discount line has been subtracted.
preconditions.otherwise: No further line is produced.

procedure: Start the running open balance at the open balance of the discount-mode calculation.
Reduce it by the balance of every discount line, across documents, after the lines sharing a grouping key have been summed.
Compare what is left with zero at the precision of the company currency.
When it is positive, take the expense exchange-difference account of the company; when it is negative, take the income exchange-difference account.
Produce one further counterpart line on that account, labelled "Early Payment Discount (Exchange Difference)", with a foreign amount of zero and a balance equal to the remaining open balance.
records.formula:
exchange_sign = compare( company currency , the remaining open balance , 0 )
if exchange_sign > 0 : account = the company's EXPENSE exchange-difference account
if exchange_sign < 0 : account = the company's INCOME  exchange-difference account
the line carries a foreign amount of 0 and a balance equal to the remaining open balance

rounding.what: The remaining open balance, inside the comparison with zero.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Inside the comparison, before the account is chosen.

result.name: the leftover exchange line of the discount
result.stored_or_displayed: Written as a write-off line of the Payment.

edge_cases.case: The discount lines consume the open balance exactly.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is left and no exchange line is produced.

edge_cases.case: A rate movement between the document and the payment left a residue.
edge_cases.outcome: That residue is booked on the exchange account rather than distorting the discount.

edge_cases.case: The residue is negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The income exchange-difference account is used.

worked_examples.description: A discount of twenty fully consumed by one base line of twenty
worked_examples.narrative: Nothing is left, so no exchange line appears in the payment entry.

records.name: End-to-end example: a payment taking a two percent early discount
records.purpose: Carries one discounted settlement through the installment reading, the four totals, the mode, the difference, the discount lines and the resulting payment entry, and states the taxed variant.

operands.name: the invoice total
operands.constraints: one thousand, with no tax

operands.name: the payment term
operands.source: the payment term of the invoice
operands.constraints: two percent within seven days, otherwise thirty days

operands.name: the payment-term item
operands.constraints: a balance and a foreign amount of plus one thousand, a discount balance and a discount foreign amount of nine hundred and eighty

operands.name: the payment date
operands.constraints: three days after the invoice date, so within the discount window

preconditions.condition: The invoice is eligible for the discount at the payment date.
preconditions.otherwise: The installment would carry the full one thousand and no discount mode would apply.

preconditions.condition: The company has a cash-discount loss account.
preconditions.otherwise: The discount line could not be booked.

procedure: Read the installments: the document is eligible, so the single installment is of the early-discount type with amounts of nine hundred and eighty and a recorded discount of twenty.
Dispatch it: the discounted installment goes to the by-default bucket and an undiscounted copy of one thousand to the bucket used for the difference, and the discount-applied flag is latched.
Compute the four totals: nine hundred and eighty for both the default and the full amount, one thousand for both difference totals.
Propose nine hundred and eighty as the amount.
Read the mode: the amount equals the full amount, so the mode is the full one.

Read the discount mode: the flag is set and the amount equals the default, so the screen is in discount mode, the difference handling is forced to the reconciling one and the write-off section is hidden.
Compute the difference: the mode is the full one, so the full difference total of one thousand less nine hundred and eighty gives twenty.
Record the eligible pair: the matched foreign amount is minus one thousand and the matched balance minus one thousand; the open amount is twenty inbound and the open balance is twenty.

Build the discount lines: the account is the cash-discount loss account because the invoice is an inbound document; the single product line of one thousand is rebuilt at nine hundred and eighty; the base delta in the company currency is twenty; the fraction settled is one; so the base line carries twenty.
Apply the rounding fix: the payment-term item records a discount of twenty and the lines sum to twenty, so nothing is added; the remaining open balance is zero, so no exchange line is produced.

Create the Payment of nine hundred and eighty with one write-off line of twenty on the cash-discount loss account, whose entry debits the outstanding receipts account by nine hundred and eighty, debits the cash-discount loss account by twenty and credits the receivable account by one thousand.
records.formula:
common = 0.00 ; by_default = 980.00 ; for_difference = 1000.00 ; full_only = 0.00
amount_by_default = 980.00 ; full_amount = 980.00 ; amount_for_difference = 1000.00 ; full_amount_for_difference = 1000.00
payment_difference = 1000.00 − 980.00 = 20.00
discounted unit price = 1000.00 × ( 100 − 2 ) ÷ 100 = 980.00
base_delta_balance = round_to( company , ( −1 ) × 980.00 − ( −1000.00 ) ) = 20.00
percentage_paid = | 1000.00 ÷ 1000.00 | = 1.00
base line amount = round_to( company , 20.00 × 1.00 ) = 20.00
term_balance = 1000.00 − 980.00 = 20.00 ; delta_balance = 20.00 − 20.00 = 0.00

rounding.what: The base delta, the base line amount and the residue of the rounding fix.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency, one hundredth.
rounding.step: After each subtraction and after the multiplication by the fraction; no value of this example is moved by the rounding.

result.name: a Payment of nine hundred and eighty with one discount line of twenty, and an invoice fully paid
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Payment and its Journal Entry; the counterpart of one thousand matches the invoice exactly.

edge_cases.case: The invoice carries twenty-one percent tax and the discount computation mode includes the taxes.
edge_cases.outcome: The two percent applies to the base and to the tax: twenty on the base and four point two on the tax, that is twenty-four point two in total; the proposed amount is one thousand one hundred and eighty-five point eight, and the counterpart lines are one base line of twenty carrying the tax grids of the original line plus one tax line of four point two on the tax account.

edge_cases.case: The same taxed invoice with a discount computation mode that excludes the taxes.
edge_cases.outcome: No tax line is produced and the whole twenty-four point two sits on the discount account without affecting the tax report.

worked_examples.description: The untaxed settlement as the document states it

inputs.payment_date: the invoice date plus three days

worked_examples.narrative: Only nine hundred and eighty of money moves, yet the counterpart of one thousand settles the invoice exactly and the twenty sits in the cash-discount loss account.

worked_examples.description: The taxed variant with a discount computed on the taxed amount

counterpart_lines.label: Early Payment Discount (the name of the tax)

worked_examples.narrative: Two percent of the one thousand of base and of the two hundred and ten of tax gives twenty-four point two, and the tax part is booked on the tax account so the tax report carries the discount.

worked_examples.description: The same taxed invoice with a discount computed on the untaxed amount
worked_examples.narrative: No tax line is produced and the tax report is untouched.

records.name: End-to-end example: a write-off of three hundredths
records.purpose: Carries one short payment through the custom-amount detector, the mode, the difference and the write-off, in both directions, and states what the alternative handling would have produced.

operands.name: the invoice total
operands.constraints: one hundred

operands.name: the amount the customer transferred
operands.source: the user, typing over the proposal
operands.constraints: ninety-nine point nine seven

operands.name: the chosen difference account
operands.constraints: a rounding-difference expense account, not an exchange account

operands.name: the write-off label
operands.constraints: the default text "Write-Off"

preconditions.condition: The typed amount differs from all four totals.
preconditions.otherwise: It would not be remembered as a custom amount and the automatic computation would overwrite it.

preconditions.condition: The chosen account is not one of the company's two exchange-difference accounts.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the two forced variants would apply instead.

procedure: Read the totals: both the amount proposed by default and the full amount are one hundred.
The user overwrites the amount with ninety-nine point nine seven; since that differs from all four totals, it is remembered as a custom amount and the automatic computation stops overwriting it.
Read the mode: ninety-nine point nine seven equals neither the full amount nor the default amount, so the mode is the full one.
Compute the difference: the full difference total of one hundred less ninety-nine point nine seven gives three hundredths.
The user sets the handling to the reconciling one, chooses a rounding-difference expense account and keeps the default label.

The chosen account is not an exchange account, so the ordinary write-off variant applies: the write-off amount is plus three hundredths because the direction is inbound, and the balance is the same because the payment is in the company currency.

Create the Payment of ninety-nine point nine seven with one write-off line, whose entry debits the outstanding receipts account by ninety-nine point nine seven, debits the rounding-difference account by three hundredths and credits the receivable account by one hundred.
records.formula:
payment_difference = full_amount_for_difference − amount = 100.00 − 99.97 = 0.03
write_off_amount_currency = + 0.03   (inbound)
write_off_balance         = + 0.03

rounding.what: The conversion of the write-off amount into the company currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency, one hundredth.
rounding.step: Inside the conversion; here the conversion is an identity because the payment is in the company currency.

result.name: a Payment of ninety-nine point nine seven with one write-off line of three hundredths
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Payment and its Journal Entry; the counterpart of one hundred settles the invoice exactly.

edge_cases.case: The difference handling is the one that leaves the difference open.
edge_cases.outcome: The entry would have been two lines of ninety-nine point nine seven and the invoice would have kept a residual of three hundredths with the partially paid state.

edge_cases.case: The payment is outbound, that is a bill of one hundred paid at ninety-nine point nine seven.
edge_cases.outcome: The write-off amount is minus three hundredths, so the difference account is credited by three hundredths and the counterpart is a debit of one hundred on the payable account.

worked_examples.description: The inbound settlement as the document states it
worked_examples.narrative: The counterpart of one hundred settles the invoice exactly, although only ninety-nine point nine seven of money moved.

worked_examples.description: The same settlement with the difference left open
worked_examples.narrative: The entry has two lines and the invoice keeps three hundredths.

worked_examples.description: The outbound mirror: a bill of one hundred paid at ninety-nine point nine seven
worked_examples.narrative: The sign flips throughout.

records.name: Correcting the balance when the payment currency differs from the documents'
records.purpose: Adds the small amount that makes a payment made in another currency settle its documents exactly in the company currency, so that no unmatched remainder is left behind.

operands.name: the company-currency residuals of the items to reconcile
operands.constraints: summed and taken in absolute value

operands.name: the foreign amount and the balance of the liquidity item of the Payment
operands.unit_or_currency: the payment currency and the company currency
operands.source: the Journal Entry of the Payment
operands.constraints: their ratio is the payment rate; a zero balance yields a rate of zero

operands.name: the foreign amounts of the counterpart items
operands.source: the Journal Entry of the Payment
operands.constraints: summed and taken in absolute value

operands.name: the balances of the counterpart items
operands.source: the Journal Entry of the Payment
operands.constraints: summed and taken in absolute value

preconditions.condition: The Payments have been created but not yet posted, and the screen is editable.
preconditions.otherwise: The correction is not attempted.

preconditions.condition: The currency of the Payment differs from the currency of the items it will settle.
preconditions.otherwise: No correction is needed.

procedure: Split the entry of the Payment into liquidity, counterpart and write-off items.
Sum the company-currency residuals of the items to reconcile and take the absolute value: that is the source balance.
Divide the foreign amount of the liquidity item by its balance to obtain the payment rate, taking zero when that balance is zero.
Multiply the absolute source balance by the payment rate: that is the source converted into the payment currency.
Sum the foreign amounts of the counterpart items and take the absolute value: that is the payment amount in currency.
When the source converted and the payment amount in currency differ by more than zero in the payment currency, the user is not trying to settle the items in full, so leave the Payment alone.
Otherwise subtract from the source balance the absolute sum of the balances of the counterpart items, giving the delta; when that delta is zero in the company currency, leave the Payment alone.

Otherwise add the delta to the debit of the first debit item among the liquidity and counterpart items, and the same delta to the credit of the first credit item, so that the company-currency amount of the Payment matches the documents exactly.
records.formula:
source_balance          = | Σ amount_residual over the items to reconcile |
payment_rate            = the liquidity item's foreign amount ÷ the liquidity item's balance   when that balance ≠ 0 , else 0
source_converted        = | source_balance | × payment_rate
payment_amount_currency = | Σ amount_currency over the counterpart items |
if compare( payment currency , source_converted , payment_amount_currency ) ≠ 0 : leave the Payment alone
delta = source_balance − | Σ balance over the counterpart items |
if is_zero( company currency , delta ) : leave the Payment alone
else : add delta to the debit of the first debit item and to the credit of the first credit item

rounding.what: The two comparisons, one in the payment currency and one in the company currency.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the payment currency and of the company currency respectively.
rounding.step: Inside each comparison, before the correction is applied.

result.name: the corrected debit and credit of the payment entry
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the Journal Entry of the Payment before it is posted.

edge_cases.case: The user is paying only part of the documents.
edge_cases.outcome: The source converted differs from the payment amount in currency and the Payment is left alone.

edge_cases.case: The delta is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The Payment is left alone, because the two sides already agree.

edge_cases.case: The Payment is already posted, or the screen is not editable.
edge_cases.outcome: The correction is not attempted at all.

worked_examples.description: The illustration of the document: a currency whose rate against the company currency is one hundred to one
worked_examples.narrative: Paying twelve point one five of the company currency with zero point one two of the other gives a computed balance of twelve, and the fifteen hundredths would never be matched; the correction adds them to both sides.

records.name: Splitting an existing payment entry into its three groups
records.purpose: Classifies the items of a Payment's entry into liquidity, counterpart and write-off, which every later rule about a Payment reads, and repairs a Payment whose outstanding account has since been changed.

operands.name: the default account of the journal
operands.constraints: one of the valid liquidity accounts

operands.name: the payment account of the Payment's own method line
operands.constraints: one of the valid liquidity accounts

operands.name: the payment accounts of every inbound and outbound method line of the journal
operands.source: the payment method lines of the journal
operands.constraints: all of them count as valid liquidity accounts

operands.name: the outstanding account of the Payment
operands.constraints: also a valid liquidity account

operands.name: the type of the account of each item
operands.constraints: a receivable or a payable account makes the item a counterpart

operands.name: the inter-bank transfer account of the company
operands.constraints: also makes an item a counterpart, which is what splits an internal transfer correctly

preconditions.condition: The Payment has an entry.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to split.

procedure: Build the set of valid liquidity accounts: the default account of the journal, the payment account of the Payment's own method line, the payment accounts of every inbound method line of the journal, the payment accounts of every outbound method line of the journal, and the outstanding account of the Payment.
Classify an item whose account is one of those as a liquidity item.
Otherwise classify an item whose account type is receivable or payable, or whose account is the inter-bank transfer account of the company, as a counterpart item.
Classify every other item as a write-off item.

Apply the repair rule: when exactly one write-off item was found and either group is empty, move that single item into the empty group, first into liquidity when liquidity is empty and then into counterpart when counterpart is empty.
records.formula:
valid liquidity accounts = { the journal's default account } ∪ { the payment account of the Payment's own method line } ∪ { the payment accounts of the journal's inbound method lines } ∪ { the payment accounts of the journal's outbound method lines } ∪ { the Payment's outstanding account }
liquidity  : the item's account is one of those
counterpart: otherwise , the account type is receivable or payable , or the account is the company's inter-bank transfer account
write-off  : every other item
repair     : exactly one write-off item and an empty group ⟹ move it into that group , liquidity first , then counterpart

rounding.what: Nothing; the split classifies items.
rounding.step: Whenever the entry is read or rewritten.

result.name: the three groups of items of the payment entry
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; read by the synchronisation, by the balance correction and by the rules about the Payment's state.

edge_cases.case: The journal's outstanding account was changed after the Payment was created.
edge_cases.outcome: The repair rule moves the single unclassified item into the empty group, which keeps the Payment usable.

edge_cases.case: The entry is that of an internal transfer.
edge_cases.outcome: The inter-bank transfer account counts as a counterpart account, so the entry splits into liquidity and counterpart rather than into liquidity and write-off.

edge_cases.case: Two or more items fall outside both groups.
edge_cases.outcome: The repair rule does not apply, because it requires exactly one write-off item.

worked_examples.description: A payment entry with one outstanding-receipts line, one receivable line and one rounding-difference line
worked_examples.narrative: All three groups are populated, so the repair rule does not fire.

records.name: The write-off and withholding totals of a new payment entry
records.purpose: Totals the supplied write-off lines and the withholding lines, and states the rule that drops the write-off lines when both kinds are present.

operands.name: the foreign amount of each supplied write-off line
operands.source: the caller, usually the register-payment screen
operands.constraints: summed

operands.name: the balance of each supplied write-off line
operands.constraints: summed

operands.name: the foreign amount of each withholding line
operands.source: the withholding hook, which is empty in the core capability
operands.constraints: summed

operands.name: the balance of each withholding line
operands.constraints: summed

preconditions.condition: The two kinds of line are not both present.
preconditions.otherwise: The write-off lines are dropped and their totals reset to zero, because the withholding capability already passes its lines as write-off lines through the synchronisation path.

procedure: Build the default label by concatenating the name of the payment method line, or the text "No Payment Method" when there is none, and then, when the Payment has a memo, the separator made of a colon and a space followed by the memo.
Collect the supplied write-off lines and sum their foreign amounts and their balances.
Collect the withholding lines from the withholding hook and sum them the same way.
When both kinds of line are present, drop the write-off lines and reset their two totals to zero.
records.formula:
write_off_amount_currency = Σ amount_currency over the supplied write-off lines
write_off_balance         = Σ balance         over the supplied write-off lines
withholding_amount_currency = Σ amount_currency over the withholding lines
withholding_balance         = Σ balance         over the withholding lines
if both kinds are present : the write-off lines are dropped and their two totals become 0

rounding.what: Nothing during the summation; each line amount is already rounded.
rounding.precision: The payment currency and the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the lines were built.
rounding.step: Not applied during the summation.

result.name: the four totals and the default label
result.unit_or_currency: the payment currency and the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Held for the preparation of the items; the label is written on the liquidity and counterpart lines.

edge_cases.case: No write-off line and no withholding line is supplied.
edge_cases.outcome: All four totals are zero and the counterpart simply mirrors the liquidity.

edge_cases.case: Both kinds are supplied.
edge_cases.outcome: The write-off lines are dropped, because the two mechanisms are not combined.

edge_cases.case: The Payment has no payment method line.
edge_cases.outcome: The label begins with the text "No Payment Method".

worked_examples.description: One write-off line of twenty on a discounted payment
worked_examples.narrative: Only the write-off side is populated, so nothing is dropped.

records.name: The liquidity amount of a payment entry in the payment currency
records.purpose: Turns the always positive amount of a Payment into the signed foreign amount of its liquidity line, by the direction alone.

operands.name: the amount of the Payment
operands.constraints: never negative, because the direction carries the sign

operands.name: the direction of the Payment
operands.constraints: inbound, outbound, or neither

preconditions.condition: An outstanding account resolves for the Payment.
preconditions.otherwise: The preparation fails with "You can't create a new payment without an outstanding payments/receipts account set either on the company or the *the payment method name* payment method in the *the journal display name* journal."

procedure: When the direction is inbound, take the amount of the Payment.
When the direction is outbound, take minus the amount of the Payment.
Otherwise take zero.
records.formula:
liquidity_amount_currency =   amount   when the direction is inbound
                          = − amount   when the direction is outbound
                          =   0        otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing; the amount is already rounded to the payment currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the amount was written.
rounding.step: Not applied here.

result.name: the foreign amount of the liquidity line, before the withholding subtraction
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the liquidity item of the Payment's entry.

edge_cases.case: The Payment has no direction.
edge_cases.outcome: The liquidity amount is zero and the entry carries no movement.

edge_cases.case: The amount is zero.
edge_cases.outcome: The liquidity amount is zero whatever the direction is.

worked_examples.description: An inbound customer payment of one thousand
worked_examples.narrative: The liquidity line carries plus one thousand and is therefore a debit.

worked_examples.description: An outbound vendor payment of one thousand
worked_examples.narrative: The liquidity line carries minus one thousand and is therefore a credit.

records.name: The liquidity balance of a payment entry from a forced balance
records.purpose: The first of the two ways the company-currency amount of the liquidity line is obtained: the caller states it outright, so that the payment is booked at exactly the figure the documents carry.

operands.name: the forced balance supplied by the caller
operands.source: the register-payment screen, when the difference is pushed onto an exchange account
operands.constraints: its absolute value is taken and the sign of the liquidity amount is applied

operands.name: the liquidity amount in the payment currency
operands.constraints: only its sign is used

operands.name: whether write-off lines were supplied
operands.constraints: when any were, this branch does not apply

preconditions.condition: No write-off line was supplied and a forced balance was.
preconditions.otherwise: The conversion branch applies instead.

procedure: Take the sign as plus one when the liquidity amount in the payment currency is greater than zero, and minus one otherwise.
Multiply that sign by the absolute value of the forced balance: that is the liquidity balance.
records.formula:
sign              = +1 when liquidity_amount_currency > 0 , else −1
liquidity_balance = sign × | forced balance |

rounding.what: Nothing; the forced balance is supplied already rounded to the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied by the caller.
rounding.step: Not applied here.

result.name: the balance of the liquidity line, before the withholding subtraction
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the liquidity item of the Payment's entry.

edge_cases.case: The liquidity amount is zero or negative.
edge_cases.outcome: The sign is minus one, so a forced balance always follows the direction of the payment rather than its own sign.

edge_cases.case: Write-off lines were supplied as well.
edge_cases.outcome: The forced balance is ignored and the conversion branch applies.

worked_examples.description: An inbound payment in a foreign currency whose documents carry one thousand two hundred of the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The liquidity line is booked at exactly one thousand two hundred, and the gap against the converted foreign amount becomes an exchange difference.

records.name: The liquidity balance of a payment entry by conversion
records.purpose: The second of the two ways the company-currency amount of the liquidity line is obtained: the signed foreign amount is converted at the date of the Payment.

operands.name: the liquidity amount in the payment currency
operands.constraints: signed by the direction

operands.name: the payment currency
operands.constraints: the source of the conversion

operands.name: the company currency
operands.constraints: the target of the conversion

operands.name: the date of the Payment
operands.constraints: the date at which the rate is read

preconditions.condition: Either a write-off line was supplied, or no forced balance was.
preconditions.otherwise: The forced-balance branch applies instead.

procedure: Convert the liquidity amount in the payment currency from the payment currency to the company currency, for the company, at the date of the Payment.
Round the result to the company currency: that is the liquidity balance.
records.formula: liquidity_balance = convert( liquidity_amount_currency , from the payment currency to the company currency , for the company , at the payment date )

rounding.what: The conversion.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Inside the conversion, before the withholding subtraction.

result.name: the balance of the liquidity line, before the withholding subtraction
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the liquidity item of the Payment's entry.

edge_cases.case: The payment currency is the company currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion is an identity and the balance equals the foreign amount.

edge_cases.case: The conversion leaves the entry a little short of the documents.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance correction of the register-payment screen may add the small difference to one debit line and one credit line.

worked_examples.description: An inbound payment of nine hundred and eighty in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The conversion is an identity, so the liquidity line debits nine hundred and eighty.

records.name: Subtracting the withholding totals from the liquidity side
records.purpose: Reduces the liquidity line by whatever is withheld, so that the liquidity carries the net while the counterpart still carries the gross.

operands.name: the liquidity amount in the payment currency
operands.constraints: reduced in place

operands.name: the liquidity balance
operands.constraints: reduced in place

operands.name: the withholding total in the payment currency
operands.constraints: zero in the core capability

operands.name: the withholding total in the company currency
operands.constraints: zero in the core capability

preconditions.condition: The withholding totals have been computed.
preconditions.otherwise: The subtraction has nothing to remove.

procedure: Subtract the withholding total in the payment currency from the liquidity amount in the payment currency.
Subtract the withholding total in the company currency from the liquidity balance.
records.formula:
liquidity_amount_currency ← liquidity_amount_currency − withholding_amount_currency
liquidity_balance         ← liquidity_balance         − withholding_balance

rounding.what: Nothing; both operands are already rounded.
rounding.precision: The payment currency and the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Earlier, when each value was produced.

result.name: the net liquidity amount and balance
result.unit_or_currency: the payment currency and company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the liquidity item of the Payment's entry.

edge_cases.case: No withholding line exists, as in the core capability.
edge_cases.outcome: Both subtractions remove zero and the liquidity carries the gross.

edge_cases.case: Withholding lines exist.
edge_cases.outcome: The liquidity carries the net, while the counterpart amounts subtract the withholding a second time, which is what makes the counterpart carry the gross.

worked_examples.description: A payment with no withholding
worked_examples.narrative: Nothing is withheld, so the liquidity line is unchanged.

records.name: The counterpart amounts of a payment entry
records.purpose: Gives the amounts of the counterpart line, which absorb the liquidity, the write-off and the withholding so that the entry balances and the counterpart matches the documents exactly.

operands.name: the net liquidity amount in the payment currency
operands.constraints: negated

operands.name: the net liquidity balance
operands.constraints: negated

operands.name: the write-off totals
operands.unit_or_currency: the payment currency and company currency
operands.constraints: subtracted

operands.name: the withholding totals
operands.unit_or_currency: the payment currency and company currency
operands.constraints: subtracted again, which is what makes the counterpart carry the gross

preconditions.condition: The liquidity amounts have already had the withholding subtracted.
preconditions.otherwise: The counterpart would carry the net rather than the gross.

procedure: Take minus the net liquidity amount in the payment currency, subtract the write-off total in the payment currency and subtract the withholding total in the payment currency: that is the counterpart amount in the payment currency.
Take minus the net liquidity balance, subtract the write-off total in the company currency and subtract the withholding total in the company currency: that is the counterpart balance.
Emit the items in this order: liquidity, counterpart, write-off, withholding.

Note that the withholding total is in effect subtracted twice, once from the liquidity side and once here, which is what makes the counterpart carry the gross amount while the liquidity carries the net.
records.formula:
counterpart_amount_currency = − liquidity_amount_currency − write_off_amount_currency − withholding_amount_currency
counterpart_balance         = − liquidity_balance         − write_off_balance         − withholding_balance
items are emitted in the order : liquidity , counterpart , write-off , withholding

rounding.what: Nothing; every operand is already rounded.
rounding.precision: The payment currency and the company currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Earlier, when each value was produced.

result.name: the foreign amount and the balance of the counterpart line
result.unit_or_currency: the payment currency and company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the counterpart item of the Payment's entry, which is the item reconciled with the settled documents.

edge_cases.case: A write-off line was prepared before the counterpart.
edge_cases.outcome: The counterpart absorbs it, so the counterpart settles the document at its full amount while the liquidity carries only what moved.

edge_cases.case: Both write-off and withholding lines exist.
edge_cases.outcome: The write-off lines were dropped earlier, so only the withholding is subtracted.

edge_cases.case: No write-off and no withholding.
edge_cases.outcome: The counterpart is the exact negation of the liquidity.

worked_examples.description: An inbound payment of ninety-nine point nine seven with a write-off of three hundredths
worked_examples.narrative: Minus ninety-nine point nine seven less three hundredths is minus one hundred, which matches the invoice's receivable item exactly.

worked_examples.description: An inbound payment of nine hundred and eighty with a discount line of twenty
worked_examples.narrative: The counterpart carries the full one thousand, so the invoice closes although only nine hundred and eighty moved.

records.name: The signed amount of a Payment in the company currency
records.purpose: Gives the figure the dashboard and the reports use for a Payment, read from its entry when it has one and derived by conversion when it does not.

operands.name: the balances of the liquidity items of the entry
operands.source: the Journal Entry of the Payment
operands.constraints: summed when an entry exists

operands.name: the signed amount of the Payment
operands.constraints: used only when there is no entry

operands.name: the date of the Payment
operands.constraints: the date at which the rate is read

preconditions.condition: The Payment has an entry.
preconditions.otherwise: The conversion branch applies.

procedure: When the Payment has an entry, sum the balances of its liquidity items.
Otherwise convert the signed amount of the Payment from the payment currency to the company currency, for the company, at the date of the Payment.
records.formula:
amount_company_currency_signed = Σ balance over the liquidity items                             when an entry exists
                               = convert( amount_signed , from the payment currency to the company currency , for the company , at the payment date )   otherwise

rounding.what: The conversion of the second branch; the first branch sums amounts already rounded.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the company currency.
rounding.step: Inside the conversion.

result.name: the signed amount of the Payment in the company currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the Payment and used by the dashboard figures of the liquidity journal.

edge_cases.case: The Payment produces no entry because its method has no payment account.
edge_cases.outcome: The conversion branch applies.

edge_cases.case: The entry has several liquidity items.
edge_cases.outcome: Their balances are summed, so a split liquidity side still gives one figure.

edge_cases.case: The liquidity balance was forced.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure is the forced one, not the conversion at the payment date.

worked_examples.description: An inbound payment of one thousand whose entry debits the outstanding receipts account by one thousand
worked_examples.narrative: The sum of the liquidity balances is the signed amount.

worked_examples.description: An outbound payment of one thousand with no entry, in the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The conversion is an identity and the sign follows the direction.

records.name: Normalising and sanitizing a bank account number
records.purpose: Reduces an account number as typed to the canonical form every check and every stored value uses.

operands.name: the account number as typed
operands.constraints: may carry spaces, hyphens and lower-case letters

preconditions.condition: An account number was supplied.
preconditions.otherwise: The validation refuses at once with "There is no IBAN code."

procedure: Remove from the account number every character that is neither a letter nor a digit: that is the normalised form.
Convert the normalised form to upper case: that is the sanitized form.
Store the sanitized number by the same rule: every non-alphanumeric character removed and the rest upper-cased.
records.formula:
normalised = the account number with every character that is neither a letter nor a digit removed
sanitised  = normalised , upper-cased

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule rewrites a text.
rounding.step: Before every check and before storing.

result.name: the sanitized account number
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Bank Account beside the number as typed, and read by every check.

edge_cases.case: The number is typed in groups separated by spaces.
edge_cases.outcome: The spaces are removed and the checks see one continuous text.

edge_cases.case: The number carries lower-case letters.
edge_cases.outcome: They are upper-cased, so the country code and the base-thirty-six expansion read correctly.

edge_cases.case: The number carries punctuation such as hyphens or points.
edge_cases.outcome: Every such character is removed.

worked_examples.description: A number typed in groups of four
worked_examples.narrative: The three spaces are removed and the letters are already upper case.

records.name: The account-number template of a country and its length
records.purpose: Gives, per country, the shape a valid international account number has, which fixes its length and says which position belongs to which part.

operands.name: the two-letter country code
operands.source: the first two characters of the sanitized number, lower-cased
operands.constraints: must be a key of the table

operands.name: the template of that country
operands.constraints: written in groups of four separated by spaces for readability

preconditions.condition: The country code is a key of the table.
preconditions.otherwise: The validation refuses with "The IBAN is invalid, it should begin with the country code"

procedure: Read the template of the country from the shipped table.

Read each position of the template: the two literal country letters occupy the first two positions; the lower-case letter marking a check digit marks a check digit of the international number itself; the capital letter marking the bank code marks a position of the national bank code; the one marking the branch marks a position of the branch code; the one marking the account marks a position of the account number; the capital letter marking a national check digit marks such a digit; the one marking the account type marks a position of an account-type code, used by two countries; the one marking the balance account marks a position of a balance-account number, used by one country; the one marking the fiscal identification marks a position of a fiscal identification number, used by one country; the one marking a reserved zero is used by one country; and the two remaining capital letters mark further country-specific positions.
Remove the spaces from the template: its length is then the length a valid number of that country must have.
records.formula:
template_length( country code ) = the length of the country's template once its spaces are removed
the sanitized number must have exactly that length

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule reads a table and counts characters.
rounding.step: Before the length check.

result.name: the template of the country and its length
result.unit_or_currency: a text and a count of characters
result.stored_or_displayed: Read by the length check, by the part extraction and by the message that shows the expected shape.

edge_cases.case: The country code is not a key of the table.
edge_cases.outcome: The validation refuses with the message about the country code, and every part extraction yields nothing.

edge_cases.case: The template carries a symbol used by only one or two countries.
edge_cases.outcome: The corresponding part is extractable only for those countries.

worked_examples.description: The complete shipped table, as the length a valid number must have for each country code
worked_examples.narrative: Seventy countries are supported; the shortest valid number has fifteen characters and the longest thirty-one.

worked_examples.description: One template read position by position
worked_examples.narrative: The sixteen positions divide into the country code, two check digits, a three-position bank code, a seven-position account number and two national check digits.

records.name: The emptiness check of an account number
records.purpose: The first step of the validation: an empty number is refused before anything else is attempted.

operands.name: the sanitized account number
operands.constraints: must not be empty

preconditions.condition: The number has been sanitized.
preconditions.otherwise: A number made only of punctuation would not be recognised as empty.

procedure: Take the sanitized number.
When it is empty, refuse with "There is no IBAN code."
Otherwise continue with the country check.
records.formula: if the sanitized number is empty : refuse with "There is no IBAN code."

rounding.what: Nothing; the check reads a length.
rounding.step: First of the six validation steps.

result.name: the verdict of the first step
result.unit_or_currency: pass, or a refusal carrying its exact message
result.stored_or_displayed: Shown to the user as a refusal.

edge_cases.case: The number consists only of spaces and hyphens.
edge_cases.outcome: The sanitized form is empty and the refusal is raised.

edge_cases.case: The account is not of the international form.
edge_cases.outcome: The validation is not run at all; the type inference simply classifies the account as an ordinary bank account.

worked_examples.description: A number typed as three spaces
worked_examples.narrative: Nothing survives the sanitisation, so the first step refuses.

records.name: The country check of an account number
records.purpose: The second step of the validation: the first two characters must name a country the template table knows.

operands.name: the first two characters of the sanitized number
operands.constraints: lower-cased before the lookup

operands.name: the keys of the template table
operands.constraints: seventy two-letter country codes

preconditions.condition: The sanitized number is not empty.
preconditions.otherwise: The first step already refused.

procedure: Take the first two characters of the sanitized number and lower-case them.
When that pair is not a key of the template table, refuse with "The IBAN is invalid, it should begin with the country code"
Otherwise continue with the length and alphabet check.
records.formula:
cc = the first two characters of the sanitized number , lower-cased
if cc is not a key of the template table : refuse with "The IBAN is invalid, it should begin with the country code"

rounding.what: Nothing; the check reads two characters.
rounding.step: Second of the six validation steps.

result.name: the verdict of the second step and the template of the country
result.unit_or_currency: pass with a template, or a refusal carrying its exact message
result.stored_or_displayed: Shown to the user as a refusal; the template is carried into the next step.

edge_cases.case: The number begins with digits.
edge_cases.outcome: The pair is not a key and the refusal is raised.

edge_cases.case: The country is not among the seventy supported ones.
edge_cases.outcome: The same refusal is raised, whatever the rest of the number is.

worked_examples.description: A Belgian number
worked_examples.narrative: The pair is a key of the table, so the validation continues.

records.name: The length and alphabet check of an account number
records.purpose: The third step of the validation: the number must have exactly the length the country's template prescribes and must hold only letters and digits.

operands.name: the sanitized account number
operands.constraints: its length is compared with the template's

operands.name: the template of the country with its spaces removed
operands.constraints: its length is the required length

operands.name: the template of the country with its spaces
operands.constraints: reproduced inside the refusal message

preconditions.condition: The country check passed.
preconditions.otherwise: No template is available.

procedure: Remove the spaces from the template of the country.

When the length of the sanitized number differs from the length of that template, or when the number contains any character that is not a letter or a digit, refuse with the message that shows the expected shape.

The refusal is the two lines "The international bank account number does not seem to be correct. You should have entered something like this *the template with its spaces*" and "Where B = National bank code, S = Branch code, C = Account No, k = Check digit".
Otherwise continue with the rotation.
records.formula:
T = the template of the country with its spaces removed
if length( the sanitized number ) ≠ length( T ) , or the number contains a character that is neither a letter nor a digit : refuse

rounding.what: Nothing; the check compares two lengths.
rounding.step: Third of the six validation steps.

result.name: the verdict of the third step
result.unit_or_currency: pass, or a refusal carrying the expected template
result.stored_or_displayed: Shown to the user as a refusal.

edge_cases.case: The number is one character short.
edge_cases.outcome: The refusal is raised and the message shows the template in groups of four so the user can see the expected shape.

edge_cases.case: The sanitisation already removed every non-alphanumeric character.
edge_cases.outcome: The alphabet part of the check can only fail on a number that was never sanitized.

worked_examples.description: A Belgian number of sixteen characters
worked_examples.narrative: The two lengths agree and every character is a letter or a digit.

records.name: Rotating an account number
records.purpose: The fourth step of the validation: the four leading characters are moved to the end, which is what places the check digits where the modulo test expects them.

operands.name: the sanitized account number
operands.constraints: at least four characters, guaranteed by the length check

preconditions.condition: The length check passed.
preconditions.otherwise: The number might be shorter than four characters.

procedure: Take the characters of the number from the fifth position to the last, positions being counted from one and both ends included.
Append to them the first four characters of the number, in their original order.
The concatenation is the rotated text.
records.formula: R = N[5..len(N)] ‖ N[1..4]   , positions being one-based and inclusive

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule rearranges a text.
rounding.step: Fourth of the six validation steps.

result.name: the rotated text
result.unit_or_currency: a text of the same length as the number
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; consumed by the expansion step.

edge_cases.case: The number is exactly four characters long.
edge_cases.outcome: This cannot happen, because the shortest supported template is fifteen characters.

edge_cases.case: The first four characters are the country code and the two check digits.
edge_cases.outcome: They land at the end, which is exactly what the modulo test expects.

worked_examples.description: A Belgian number
worked_examples.narrative: The country code and the two check digits move to the end.

records.name: Expanding an account number into decimal digits
records.purpose: The fifth step of the validation: every character of the rotated text is replaced by its base-thirty-six value written in decimal, so that the whole text becomes one very large whole number.

operands.name: the rotated text
operands.constraints: only letters and digits

operands.name: the base-thirty-six value of each character
operands.constraints: a digit keeps its own value, and the letters run from ten to thirty-five

preconditions.condition: Every character is a letter or a digit.
preconditions.otherwise: The length and alphabet check already refused.

procedure: Read the value of each character: a digit contributes its own value from zero to nine, and a letter contributes its position in the alphabet plus nine, so that the first letter is ten and the last is thirty-five.
Write each value in decimal, so that a digit contributes one character and a letter contributes two.
Concatenate the written values in the order of the characters.
records.formula:
value( '0' ) = 0 , … , value( '9' ) = 9 , value( 'A' ) = 10 , value( 'B' ) = 11 , … , value( 'Z' ) = 35
D = decimal_text( value( R[1] ) ) ‖ decimal_text( value( R[2] ) ) ‖ … ‖ decimal_text( value( R[last] ) )

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule rewrites a text.
rounding.step: Fifth of the six validation steps.

result.name: the expanded decimal text
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; read as an integer by the modulo test.

edge_cases.case: The text holds no letter at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The expanded text is the text itself.

edge_cases.case: The text holds several letters.
edge_cases.outcome: Each contributes two characters, so the expanded text is longer than the original.

worked_examples.description: The rotated Belgian number
worked_examples.narrative: The two letters contribute eleven and fourteen, that is four characters in place of two, so the expanded text has eighteen digits.

records.name: The modulo ninety-seven test and its left-to-right fold
records.purpose: The sixth and last step of the validation: the expanded number must leave a remainder of one when divided by ninety-seven, computed by a fold so that no machine integer is ever exceeded.

operands.name: the expanded decimal text
operands.constraints: far too large to be read as a machine integer

operands.name: the divisor
operands.constraints: ninety-seven

preconditions.condition: The expansion produced a text of decimal digits.
preconditions.otherwise: There is nothing to fold.

procedure: Set the running remainder to zero.
Walk the characters of the expanded text from left to right.
For each character, multiply the running remainder by ten, add the value of the character and take the remainder of the division by ninety-seven.
The running remainder at the end is the remainder of the whole number.
When that remainder is not one, refuse with "This IBAN does not pass the validation check, please verify it."
records.formula:
D mod 97 = 1   is the test
the remainder is computed by :
    r ← 0
    for each character c of D , from left to right : r ← ( r × 10 + digit_value( c ) ) mod 97
    the result is r

rounding.what: Nothing; the fold works on whole numbers.
rounding.precision: Exact whole-number arithmetic, the running remainder never exceeding ninety-six.
rounding.step: Once per character, from left to right.

result.name: the remainder and the verdict
result.unit_or_currency: a whole number between zero and ninety-six, and a truth value
result.stored_or_displayed: The verdict decides the inferred type of the account and whether the number is stored in its pretty form.

edge_cases.case: The number is far too large for a machine integer.
edge_cases.outcome: The fold keeps the running remainder below ninety-seven at every step, so no overflow is possible.

edge_cases.case: One digit of the number is wrong.
edge_cases.outcome: The remainder differs from one and the number is rejected.

edge_cases.case: The remainder is one.
edge_cases.outcome: The number is valid and the account is inferred to be of the international form.

worked_examples.description: The Belgian number, folded character by character
worked_examples.narrative: The eighteen steps of the fold end at one, so the number passes.

worked_examples.description: The same number with the last digit changed from one to two

expected_outputs.message: This IBAN does not pass the validation check, please verify it.

worked_examples.narrative: From the sixty-one obtained after the tenth character the fold diverges and ends at twenty-eight, so the number is rejected.

records.name: Worked example: validating a Belgian account number
records.purpose: Carries one account number through the six validation steps with every intermediate value, and shows what one wrong digit does.

operands.name: the account number as typed
operands.constraints: written in groups of four

operands.name: the template of the country
operands.constraints: sixteen positions once the spaces are removed

preconditions.condition: The number is sanitized before the checks.
preconditions.otherwise: The spaces would break the length check.

procedure: Sanitize the number: the three spaces disappear and the sixteen characters remain; the number is not empty.
Read the country code: the first two characters lower-cased are a key of the template table.
Check the length and the alphabet: the template without spaces has sixteen characters, the number has sixteen, and every character is a letter or a digit.
Rotate: the first four characters move to the end.
Expand: every character except the two letters is a digit and contributes itself; the two letters contribute eleven and fourteen.
Fold from left to right, eighteen steps, reaching a remainder of one; the number is valid.

rounding.what: Nothing; every step is exact whole-number or text arithmetic.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the verdict and the eighteen running remainders
result.unit_or_currency: a truth value and whole numbers
result.stored_or_displayed: The verdict decides the inferred type of the account and whether the number is stored in its pretty form.

edge_cases.case: The last digit is changed from one to two.
edge_cases.outcome: The rotated text and the expanded text change, and the fold ends at twenty-eight rather than one, so the number is rejected with the message about the validation check.

worked_examples.description: The valid number as the document states it
worked_examples.narrative: Every step succeeds and the fold ends at one.

worked_examples.description: The same number with the last digit changed

expected_outputs.message: This IBAN does not pass the validation check, please verify it.

worked_examples.narrative: A single wrong digit changes the remainder from one to twenty-eight.

records.name: The pretty form of an account number
records.purpose: Rewrites a valid number in groups of four for display and storage, while leaving an invalid one exactly as the user typed it.

operands.name: the account number as typed
operands.constraints: stored unchanged when the validation fails

operands.name: the normalised number
operands.constraints: the input of the grouping

operands.name: the verdict of the validation
operands.constraints: decides between the two behaviours

preconditions.condition: The number validates.
preconditions.otherwise: It is stored exactly as typed.

procedure: Run the validation on the number.
When it validates, store the normalised form rewritten as groups of four characters separated by single spaces, the last group being shorter when the length is not a multiple of four.
When it does not validate, store the number exactly as typed.
Apply the same rewriting both when a Bank Account is created and when it is modified.
records.formula:
