records.name: The direct bank payments of a liquidity journal
records.purpose: Totals the Payments booked straight onto the journal's own bank account rather than onto an outstanding account, which the card adds to the statement balance.

operands.name: the matched flag of each Payment
operands.constraints: must be true

operands.name: the state of the entry of each Payment
operands.constraints: must be posted

operands.name: the outstanding account of each Payment
operands.constraints: must be the default account of the journal

operands.name: the amount and the direction of each Payment
operands.constraints: signed by the direction

operands.name: the currency of the entry of each Payment
operands.constraints: the grouping key together with the company and the journal

preconditions.condition: The company of the Payment is among the user's active companies.
preconditions.otherwise: The Payment is not counted.

procedure: Group the Payments whose matched flag is true, whose entry is posted, whose journal is this journal, whose company is active, and whose outstanding account is the default account of the journal, by company, journal and currency of the entry.
Take the signed amount of a Payment as minus its amount when it is outbound and as plus its amount when it is inbound.
Convert each group into the currency of the journal, going through the group's company-currency total when the currencies differ.
Add the converted signed amounts: that is the balance of the direct bank payments.
Take the number of contributing groups as the count shown beside it.
records.formula:
signed_amount = − amount for an outbound payment , + amount for an inbound payment
direct_payments_balance = Σ signed_amount , each group converted into the journal's currency through the group's company-currency total when the currencies differ
nb_direct_payments      = the number of groups contributing

rounding.what: The total, once every group has been converted.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the journal currency.
rounding.step: After the conversion of every group, on the total.

result.name: the balance and the count of the direct bank payments
result.unit_or_currency: the journal currency and a count
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the dashboard card and added to the running balance to give the account balance.

edge_cases.case: A Payment's liquidity account is the journal's own default account rather than an outstanding account.
edge_cases.outcome: It is considered matched by definition, reaches the paid state as soon as it is confirmed, and is counted here rather than in the outstanding figure.

edge_cases.case: A group is in a currency other than the journal's.
edge_cases.outcome: Its company-currency total is converted at the current date.

edge_cases.case: No such Payment exists.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance and the count are both zero.

worked_examples.description: One inbound direct payment of two hundred and one outbound of fifty, both in the journal currency
worked_examples.narrative: The two payments share one group, whose signed total is one hundred and fifty.

records.name: The account balance shown on the dashboard card
records.purpose: The headline figure of a liquidity journal's card: what the bank account is expected to hold, statements and direct payments together.

operands.name: the running balance of the journal
operands.constraints: the statement side

operands.name: the balance of the direct bank payments
operands.constraints: the payment side

preconditions.condition: Both figures have been computed in the journal currency.
preconditions.otherwise: They could not be added.

procedure: Add the running balance of the journal to the balance of the direct bank payments.
records.formula: account_balance = current_statement_balance + direct_payments_balance

rounding.what: Nothing; both operands are already rounded to the journal currency.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied earlier.
rounding.step: Earlier, on each of the two figures.

result.name: the account balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as the headline figure of the dashboard card of the liquidity journal.

edge_cases.case: The journal has no direct bank payment.
edge_cases.outcome: The account balance equals the running balance.

edge_cases.case: The journal has no statement at all.
edge_cases.outcome: The running balance is the sum of the unlinked transactions and the account balance follows from it.

worked_examples.description: A journal at one thousand and fifty with one hundred and fifty of direct payments
worked_examples.narrative: The card shows one thousand two hundred.

records.name: The outstanding payments balance of a liquidity journal
records.purpose: Totals the Payments of the journal that have not yet met a bank transaction, which is the amount still sitting on the outstanding accounts.

operands.name: the matched flag of each Payment
operands.constraints: must not be true

operands.name: the state of the entry of each Payment
operands.constraints: must be posted

operands.name: the journal of each Payment
operands.constraints: must be this journal

operands.name: the amount and the direction of each Payment
operands.constraints: signed by the direction

preconditions.condition: The company of the Payment is among the user's active companies.
preconditions.otherwise: The Payment is not counted.

procedure: Group the Payments whose matched flag is not true, whose entry is posted, whose journal is this journal and whose company is active, by company, journal and payment currency.
Take the signed amount of a Payment as minus its amount when it is outbound and as plus its amount when it is inbound.
Convert each group into the currency of the journal.
Add the converted signed amounts: that is the outstanding payments balance.
Record whether any group contributed.
records.formula:
outstanding_pay_account_balance = Σ signed_amount over the groups , each converted into the journal's currency
has_outstanding                 = whether any group contributed

rounding.what: The total, once every group has been converted.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the journal currency.
rounding.step: After the conversion of every group, on the total.

result.name: the outstanding payments balance and the flag saying there is one
result.unit_or_currency: the journal currency and a truth value
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the dashboard card of the liquidity journal.

edge_cases.case: A Payment is booked straight onto the journal's default account.
edge_cases.outcome: Its matched flag is true by definition, so it is counted among the direct bank payments instead.

edge_cases.case: No unmatched Payment exists.
edge_cases.outcome: The balance is zero and the flag is false.

worked_examples.description: Two unmatched inbound payments of five hundred and of three hundred, in the journal currency
worked_examples.narrative: Eight hundred is still waiting to appear on a bank transaction.

records.name: Converting a group of payments into the journal's currency
records.purpose: The shared conversion the two payment figures of the dashboard use, which goes through the company-currency total of a group whenever its currency differs from the target.

operands.name: the currency of each group
operands.constraints: compared with the target currency

operands.name: the signed amount of each group
operands.constraints: added directly when the currencies agree

operands.name: the company-currency total of each group
operands.constraints: the pivot when the currencies differ

operands.name: the target currency
operands.constraints: the currency the figure is shown in

preconditions.condition: Each group carries both its own signed amount and its company-currency total.
preconditions.otherwise: The second branch could not be taken.

procedure: For each group, when the currency of the group equals the target currency, add the signed amount of the group.
Otherwise convert the company-currency total of the group from the currency of the group's company to the target currency, for that company, at the current date, and add the result.
Round the total to the target currency.

rounding.what: The total, once every group has been added.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the target currency.
rounding.step: On the total, after every group has been converted and added.

result.name: the total in the target currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the dashboard card as the direct payments balance or the outstanding payments balance.

edge_cases.case: Every group is already in the target currency.
edge_cases.outcome: No conversion is made and the total is the plain sum.

edge_cases.case: The rate moves between two viewings of the card.
edge_cases.outcome: The figure changes, because the conversion is made at the current date rather than at the payment date.

worked_examples.description: One group in the journal currency and one in another currency worth eight hundred of the company currency
worked_examples.narrative: The first group is added directly and the second through its company-currency total.

records.name: The miscellaneous operations of a liquidity journal
records.purpose: Counts the journal items posted on the journal's bank account that came from neither a Bank Transaction nor a Payment, which is what tells a user that something is booked outside the two normal paths.

operands.name: the journal items on the journal's default account
operands.constraints: restricted to the active companies

operands.name: whether the item belongs to a Bank Transaction or to a Payment
operands.constraints: both must be false

operands.name: the state of the entry of each item
operands.constraints: must be posted

operands.name: the date limit
operands.source: the last statement date of the journal, otherwise the fiscal-year lock date of the company
operands.constraints: unrestricted when there is neither

operands.name: the foreign amount of each item
operands.constraints: summed per account

preconditions.condition: Every one of those items is in the journal's own currency.
preconditions.otherwise: No balance is shown; the count alone is shown in a warning colour.

procedure: Take the date limit as the date of the journal's last statement, or as the fiscal-year lock date of the company when the journal has no statement, and leave the date unrestricted when there is neither.

Select the items whose company is active, that belong to no Bank Transaction, whose entry is posted, that belong to no Payment, and whose account is the journal's default account with a date after the date limit; combine the per-journal conditions by disjunction when several journals are considered at once.
Group the selected items by account.
Take the count of them as the number of miscellaneous operations.
Take the sum of their foreign amounts, grouped by account, as the balance of the miscellaneous operations.
Show the balance only when every one of those items is in the journal's own currency; otherwise show the count in a warning colour and give no balance.
records.formula:
domain = the company is active
     AND the item belongs to no Bank Transaction
     AND the item's entry state is posted
     AND the item belongs to no Payment
     AND ( the account is the journal's default account AND the date is after the date limit ) , combined with a disjunction for each journal
nb_misc_operations      = the number of such items , grouped by account
misc_operations_balance = the sum of their foreign amounts , grouped by account

rounding.what: Nothing during the summation; each foreign amount is already rounded.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when each amount was written.
rounding.step: Not applied during the summation.

result.name: the count and, when the currencies allow it, the balance of the miscellaneous operations
result.unit_or_currency: a count and the journal currency
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the dashboard card of the liquidity journal.

edge_cases.case: The items are in more than one currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The count is shown in a warning colour and no balance is given.

edge_cases.case: The journal has no statement and the company has no fiscal-year lock date.
edge_cases.outcome: The date is unrestricted and every such item of the journal is counted.

edge_cases.case: The item belongs to a Payment.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not a miscellaneous operation, whatever its account.

worked_examples.description: Two posted items on the bank account after the last statement, both in the journal currency
worked_examples.narrative: Ninety of movement is booked outside the two normal paths, and the card shows both the count and the balance.

records.name: The last statement and its visibility on the dashboard card
records.purpose: The remaining figures of a liquidity journal's card: which statement is the latest, what it reports, whether it may be shown, and whether the journal has an invalid statement.

operands.name: the statements of the journal
operands.constraints: ordered by date and then by identifier, both descending

operands.name: the reported ending balance of the last statement
operands.constraints: shown on the card

operands.name: the fiscal-year lock date of the company
operands.constraints: the last statement is visible when there is none, or when the statement is dated after it

operands.name: the validity of each statement of the journal
operands.constraints: one invalid statement flags the journal

preconditions.condition: The journal has at least one statement.
preconditions.otherwise: The card carries no last statement and no reported balance.

procedure: Take the last statement of the journal as the one with the greatest date, and then the greatest identifier.
Read its reported ending balance.
Record whether the journal has at least one statement.
Decide whether the last statement is visible: it is when the company has no fiscal-year lock date, or when the date of the last statement is after that lock date.
Record whether the journal has invalid statements, which is true when at least one of its statements is invalid.
Record the bank feed source of the journal.
records.formula:
last statement      = the statement of the journal with the greatest date , then the greatest identifier
last statement is visible ⟺ the company has no fiscal-year lock date OR the last statement's date is after that lock date
journal has invalid statements ⟺ at least one of its statements is invalid

rounding.what: Nothing; the card reads a date, a balance and two flags.
rounding.precision: The journal currency for the balance.
rounding.method: Half away from zero, applied when the balance was written.
rounding.step: Not applied here.

result.name: the last statement, its reported balance, its visibility, the invalid-statements flag and the bank feed source
result.unit_or_currency: the journal currency for the balance
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the dashboard card of the liquidity journal.

edge_cases.case: Two statements share a date.
edge_cases.outcome: The greater identifier decides which is the last.

edge_cases.case: The last statement predates the fiscal-year lock date.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not shown, because it belongs to a closed period.

edge_cases.case: One statement of the journal is invalid.
edge_cases.outcome: The journal is flagged and the card shows the warning.

worked_examples.description: A journal whose latest statement is dated the thirty-first of March and reports one thousand one hundred, with no lock date
worked_examples.narrative: The card shows the statement and its reported balance without any warning.

records.name: The thirty-day balance graph of a liquidity journal
records.purpose: Builds the filled line graph of the card, walking backwards from today so that the curve ends at the journal's current running balance and always spans a full month.

operands.name: the daily totals of the journal
operands.source: the Bank Transactions of the journal whose entry date is later than thirty days ago and whose company is active, grouped by entry date and journal, ordered by date descending
operands.constraints: each is the sum of that day's amounts

operands.name: the running balance of the journal
operands.constraints: the starting point of the backwards walk

operands.name: the type of the journal
operands.constraints: decides the key of the series

operands.name: the language of the user
operands.constraints: formats the two date labels of each point

preconditions.condition: There is at least one daily total, or the journal has statement lines.
preconditions.otherwise: The sample graph is drawn instead.

procedure: Read the daily totals: group the Bank Transactions of the journal whose entry date is later than thirty days ago and whose company is active, by entry date and journal, summing the amounts, ordered by date descending.
Key the series as the balance of a cash journal, of a bank journal or of a credit-card journal, according to the type of the journal.
Start the running amount at the journal's current running balance.
When there is no daily total, or the most recent daily total is earlier than today, add a point for today at that running amount, so that the curve always reaches at least today.

Walk the daily totals from the most recent to the oldest; for each, prepend a point dated on that day at the current running amount, then subtract that day's total from the running amount; prepending rather than appending is what makes the curve read forwards while being computed backwards.
When the oldest date processed is not exactly thirty days ago, prepend one last point dated thirty days ago at the remaining running amount, so that the curve always starts a month back.
Give each point the value rounded to the journal's currency, a short date label and a long date label, both formatted in the language of the user.
records.formula:
running amount ← the journal's current running balance
if there is no daily total , or the most recent one is earlier than today : add a point for today at the running amount
for each daily total , from the most recent to the oldest :
    prepend a point dated on that day at the running amount
    running amount ← running amount − that day's total
if the oldest date processed is not exactly thirty days ago : prepend a point dated thirty days ago at the remaining running amount

rounding.what: The value of each point.
rounding.precision: The rounding step of the journal currency.
rounding.step: When each point is written, after the running amount has been carried back.

result.name: the ordered points of the graph
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as a filled line graph on the dashboard card of the liquidity journal.

edge_cases.case: The most recent daily total is today.
edge_cases.outcome: No extra point for today is added, because the walk already produces one.

edge_cases.case: The oldest daily total is exactly thirty days ago.
edge_cases.outcome: No extra point at thirty days is prepended.

edge_cases.case: There is no daily total but the journal has statement lines.
edge_cases.outcome: The graph is a flat line at the running balance, from thirty days ago to today.

worked_examples.description: A journal at a running balance of one thousand and fifty with one daily total of plus fifty, five days ago
worked_examples.narrative: The walk adds today at one thousand and fifty, then the day of the movement at one thousand and fifty, then carries the running amount back to one thousand for the point thirty days ago.

records.name: The sample graph of a liquidity journal with no history
records.purpose: Fills the card of a journal that has neither a daily total nor a statement line, so that the card is never blank, and marks the series as sample data.

operands.name: whether there is any daily total
operands.source: the grouping of the Bank Transactions
operands.constraints: must be false

operands.name: whether the journal has statement lines at all
operands.constraints: must be false

preconditions.condition: There is no daily total and the journal has no statement line at all.
preconditions.otherwise: The real graph is drawn instead.

procedure: Check that there is no daily total and that the journal has no statement line at all.
Produce six points, one every five days over the last thirty days.
Give each a random value between minus five and fifteen.
Key the series as sample data and flag it as such.
records.formula: six points , one every five days over the last thirty days , each with a random value between −5 and 15 ; the series is keyed as sample data and flagged as sample

rounding.what: Nothing; the values are illustrative.
rounding.step: Not applicable.

result.name: the six sample points and the sample flag
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed on the dashboard card, marked as sample data so that no reader mistakes it for a real balance.

edge_cases.case: The journal has a statement line but no transaction in the last thirty days.
edge_cases.outcome: The real graph is drawn, as a flat line at the running balance.

edge_cases.case: The card is redrawn.
edge_cases.outcome: The random values change, which is acceptable because the series is flagged as sample.

worked_examples.description: A journal with no transaction and no statement
worked_examples.narrative: Six evenly spaced points fill the card and the series is marked as sample data.

records.name: The liquidity journals available for a batch
records.purpose: Fixes which journals a payment may be made from, by the type of the journal and by the direction the batch needs.

operands.name: the journals visible from the batch's company
operands.constraints: on the register-payment screen; on a Payment the journals of an ancestor or a descendant of the active company are considered

operands.name: the type of each journal
operands.constraints: must be a bank, a cash or a credit-card journal

operands.name: the payment method lines of each journal
operands.constraints: at least one of the needed direction

operands.name: the direction of the batch
operands.constraints: decides which direction of method line is required

preconditions.condition: The batch has a direction.
preconditions.otherwise: The outbound filter is applied, because inbound is the only case tested for explicitly.

procedure: Take every Journal whose company is visible from the batch's company and whose type is a bank, a cash or a credit-card journal.
When the direction of the batch is inbound, keep the journals having at least one inbound payment method line.
Otherwise keep the journals having at least one outbound payment method line.
On the register-payment screen, take the available set as the union over every batch.
On a Payment, consider instead the journals whose company is an ancestor or a descendant of the active company, and apply the same direction filter.
records.formula:
journals  = every Journal whose company is visible from the batch's company AND whose type is bank , cash or credit card
available = journals having at least one INBOUND  payment method line   when the batch's direction is inbound
          = journals having at least one OUTBOUND payment method line   otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule filters journals.
rounding.step: Before a journal is chosen.

result.name: the set of available journals
result.stored_or_displayed: Offered in the journal field of the register-payment screen and of the Payment.

edge_cases.case: The screen holds several batches of different directions.
edge_cases.outcome: The available set is the union, so a journal serving either direction is offered.

edge_cases.case: A journal has no payment method line of the needed direction.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not offered.

edge_cases.case: The selection is made on a Payment rather than on the screen.
edge_cases.outcome: The journals of a descendant company are also considered, which the screen does not do.

worked_examples.description: An inbound batch with two bank journals, one of which has no inbound method line
worked_examples.narrative: Only the journal with an inbound method line is offered.

records.name: The journal chosen for a batch that names a recipient account
records.purpose: The first variant of the journal choice: when the batch names a recipient bank account, four candidate sets are tried in a preference order that puts the account above the currency.

operands.name: the company of the batch
operands.source: the batch item company with the fewest ancestors
operands.constraints: the journals considered belong to it

operands.name: the currency of the batch
operands.constraints: the wanted currency

operands.name: the recipient bank account of the batch
operands.constraints: the wanted account; this variant applies only when it is set

operands.name: the available set of journals
operands.constraints: every candidate must belong to it

preconditions.condition: The batch names a recipient bank account.
preconditions.otherwise: The other variant applies.

procedure: Build the base set: the journals of the batch's company whose type is a bank, a cash or a credit-card journal and that are in the screen's available set.
Try the base set restricted to the journals whose currency is the wanted currency and whose bank account is the wanted account.
When that is empty, try the base set restricted to the journals whose bank account is the wanted account.
When that is empty, try the base set restricted to the journals whose currency is the wanted currency.
When that is empty, try the base set itself.
Return the first journal found, in the journal ordering, and nothing when none matches.
records.formula:
base = the Journals of the batch's company whose type is bank , cash or credit card AND that are in the available set
try , in this order :
    1. base AND currency = the wanted currency AND bank account = the wanted account
    2. base AND                                    bank account = the wanted account
    3. base AND currency = the wanted currency
    4. base
return the first journal found , in the journal ordering ; nothing when none matches

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule selects a journal.
rounding.step: Once per batch.

result.name: the journal chosen for the batch
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the created Payment and shown on the register-payment screen.

edge_cases.case: A journal matches both the currency and the account.
edge_cases.outcome: It wins on the first attempt.

edge_cases.case: One journal matches the account and another the currency.
edge_cases.outcome: The one matching the account wins, because that attempt comes first.

edge_cases.case: No journal matches anything.
edge_cases.outcome: Any liquidity journal of the base set is taken, and nothing is returned when the base set is empty.

worked_examples.description: A batch wanting a given currency and a given account, with one journal matching the account only and one matching the currency only
worked_examples.narrative: Matching the account alone beats matching the currency alone.

records.name: The journal chosen for a batch that names no recipient account
records.purpose: The second variant of the journal choice: with no recipient account to match, only the currency and then the plain availability are tried.

operands.name: the company of the batch
operands.source: the batch item company with the fewest ancestors
operands.constraints: the journals considered belong to it

operands.name: the currency of the batch
operands.constraints: the wanted currency

operands.name: the available set of journals
operands.constraints: every candidate must belong to it

preconditions.condition: The batch names no recipient bank account.
preconditions.otherwise: The other variant applies.

procedure: Build the base set: the journals of the batch's company whose type is a bank, a cash or a credit-card journal and that are in the screen's available set.
Try the base set restricted to the journals whose currency is the wanted currency.
When that is empty, try the base set itself.
Return the first journal found, in the journal ordering, and nothing when none matches.
records.formula:
base = the Journals of the batch's company whose type is bank , cash or credit card AND that are in the available set
try , in this order :
    1. base AND currency = the wanted currency
    2. base
return the first journal found , in the journal ordering ; nothing when none matches

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule selects a journal.
rounding.step: Once per batch.

result.name: the journal chosen for the batch
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the created Payment and shown on the register-payment screen.

edge_cases.case: No journal is held in the wanted currency.
edge_cases.outcome: Any liquidity journal of the base set is taken, because any liquidity journal is better than none.

edge_cases.case: The base set is empty.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is returned and the screen has no journal.

worked_examples.description: A batch in the company currency with one journal in that currency and one in another

attempt_one: the journal in the company currency
expected_outputs.chosen: the journal in the company currency

worked_examples.narrative: The currency match wins on the first attempt.

records.name: Recomputing the journal when the available set changes
records.purpose: States when the register-payment screen replaces the journal the user is looking at, and the three sources it draws the replacement from.

operands.name: the available set of journals
operands.constraints: its change triggers the recomputation

operands.name: the journal currently on the screen
operands.constraints: kept when it is still available

operands.name: the preferred payment method lines named on the documents being paid
operands.constraints: used only when exactly one is named

operands.name: the journal chosen for the single batch
operands.constraints: used when the screen is editable

preconditions.condition: The journal currently on the screen is no longer in the available set.
preconditions.otherwise: It is kept and nothing is recomputed.

procedure: Recompute only when the available set changes and the current journal is no longer in it.
When exactly one preferred payment method line is named on the documents being paid, take that line's journal.
Otherwise, when the screen is editable, take the journal chosen for the single batch.
Otherwise take the first liquidity journal of the screen's company that is in the available set.
records.formula:
recompute only when the available set changes and the current journal is no longer in it , then , in order :
    1. the journal of the single preferred payment method line named on the documents , when exactly one is named
    2. the journal chosen for the single batch , when the screen is editable
    3. the first liquidity journal of the screen's company that is in the available set

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule selects a journal.
rounding.step: Whenever the available set changes.

result.name: the journal of the register-payment screen
result.stored_or_displayed: Shown on the screen and carried onto the created Payments in edit mode.

edge_cases.case: The current journal is still available.
edge_cases.outcome: It is kept, so a user's explicit choice is not overwritten.

edge_cases.case: Two different preferred method lines are named on the documents.
edge_cases.outcome: The first source does not apply and the second or the third is used.

edge_cases.case: The screen is not editable.
edge_cases.outcome: The third source is used.

worked_examples.description: A screen whose current journal has just left the available set, with one preferred method line on the documents

expected_outputs.source_used: the journal of the single preferred payment method line

worked_examples.narrative: The documents' own preference wins over the batch computation.

records.name: The recipient accounts available for an inbound batch
records.purpose: The first variant of the recipient-account choice: money coming in is received on the company's own account, so only the journal's account is offered.

operands.name: the bank account of the journal
operands.constraints: the only account offered

operands.name: the recipient account already on the batch
operands.constraints: used when it is among the available ones

preconditions.condition: The direction of the batch is inbound.
preconditions.otherwise: The outbound variant applies.

procedure: Take the available accounts as the journal's own bank account, because money is received on the company's account.
Use the batch's own recipient account when it is among the available ones, and the first available one otherwise.
records.formula:
available = the journal's own bank account
the account used = the batch's own recipient account when it is among the available ones , otherwise the first available one

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule selects an account.
rounding.step: Once per batch.

result.name: the recipient bank account of the batch
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the created Payment and shown on the register-payment screen.

edge_cases.case: The journal has no bank account.
edge_cases.outcome: The available set is empty and the batch's counterparties are added to the missing list when a recipient account is required.

edge_cases.case: The batch already names another account.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not among the available ones, so the journal's account is used.

worked_examples.description: An inbound batch on a journal holding one bank account
worked_examples.narrative: Only the journal's own account is offered.

records.name: The recipient accounts available for an outbound batch
records.purpose: The second variant of the recipient-account choice: money going out is sent to the counterparty, so the counterparties' accounts are offered, restricted to the batch's company.

operands.name: the bank accounts of the batch's counterparties
operands.constraints: only those whose company is empty or equal to the batch's company

operands.name: the company of the batch
operands.source: the batch item company with the fewest ancestors
operands.constraints: restricts the accounts

operands.name: the recipient account already on the batch
operands.constraints: used when it is among the available ones

preconditions.condition: The direction of the batch is not inbound.
preconditions.otherwise: The inbound variant applies.

procedure: Take the company of the batch as the one with the fewest ancestors among its items' companies.
Take the available accounts as the bank accounts of the batch's counterparties whose company is empty or equal to that company.
Use the batch's own recipient account when it is among the available ones, and the first available one otherwise.
records.formula:
company   = the batch's company with the fewest ancestors
available = the bank accounts of the batch's counterparties whose company is empty or equal to that company
the account used = the batch's own recipient account when it is among the available ones , otherwise the first available one

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule selects an account.
rounding.step: Once per batch.

result.name: the recipient bank account of the batch
result.stored_or_displayed: Written on the created Payment and shown on the register-payment screen.

edge_cases.case: A counterparty's account belongs to another company.
edge_cases.outcome: It is not offered.

edge_cases.case: The counterparty has no bank account.
edge_cases.outcome: The available set is empty, and when a recipient account is required the counterparty is added to the missing list.

edge_cases.case: The chosen account is not trusted for outgoing payments.
edge_cases.outcome: The batch is blocked and the account is added to the untrusted list.

worked_examples.description: An outbound batch whose counterparty holds two accounts, one of them belonging to another company
worked_examples.narrative: Only the account not tied to another company is offered.

records.name: The payment method line chosen on a Payment
records.purpose: The first variant of the method-line choice: on a Payment record, the counterparty's own default line is preferred, then the current one, then any available one.

operands.name: the default inbound line of the counterparty
operands.constraints: used when the direction is inbound and the line is available

operands.name: the default outbound line of the counterparty
operands.constraints: used when the direction is outbound and the line is available

operands.name: the line currently on the Payment
operands.constraints: kept when it is still available

operands.name: the available lines
operands.constraints: the first one is the last resort

preconditions.condition: The journal offers at least one available line.
preconditions.otherwise: No line is chosen, and the record-level constraint refuses the Payment with "Please define a payment method line on your payment."

procedure: Take the counterparty's default inbound line when the direction is inbound and that line is available.
Otherwise take the counterparty's default outbound line when the direction is outbound and that line is available.
Otherwise keep the current line when it is still available.
Otherwise take the first available line.
Otherwise choose none.
records.formula:
on a Payment , in order :
    1. the counterparty's default inbound line , when the direction is inbound and that line is available
    2. the counterparty's default outbound line , when the direction is outbound and that line is available
    3. the current line , when it is still available
    4. the first available line
    5. none

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule selects a method line.
rounding.step: Whenever the direction, the counterparty or the journal changes.

result.name: the payment method line of the Payment
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Payment and used to resolve its outstanding account.

edge_cases.case: The counterparty has no default line for the direction.
edge_cases.outcome: The current line, then the first available one, is used.

edge_cases.case: No line is available at all.
edge_cases.outcome: None is chosen and the record-level constraint refuses the Payment.

edge_cases.case: The chosen line names a journal other than the Payment's.
edge_cases.outcome: The record-level constraint refuses the Payment with "The selected payment method is not available for this payment, please select the payment method again."

worked_examples.description: An inbound payment whose counterparty names a default inbound line that the journal offers
worked_examples.narrative: The counterparty's own preference wins.

records.name: The payment method line chosen on the register-payment screen
records.purpose: The second variant of the method-line choice: on the screen the current line is kept first, then the single preference named on the documents, and a batch of the other direction falls back to its own.

operands.name: the line currently on the screen
operands.constraints: kept when it is still available

operands.name: the preferred payment method lines named on the documents
operands.constraints: used only when exactly one is named and it is available

operands.name: the available lines
operands.constraints: the first one is the last resort

operands.name: the direction of each batch
operands.constraints: a batch of the other direction uses its own first available line

preconditions.condition: The journal offers at least one available line.
preconditions.otherwise: No line is chosen at all.

procedure: Keep the current line when it is still available.
Otherwise, when exactly one preferred payment method line is named on the documents and it is available, use it.
Otherwise take the first available line.
Otherwise choose none.
When a batch's direction differs from the direction of the line chosen on the screen, let that batch use the first available line of the journal for its own direction instead.
records.formula:
on the register-payment screen , in order :
    1. keep the current line when it is still available
    2. otherwise , when exactly one preferred payment method line is named on the documents and it is available , use it
    3. otherwise the first available line
    4. otherwise none
a batch whose direction differs from that of the chosen line uses the first available line of the journal for its own direction

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule selects a method line.
rounding.step: Whenever the journal or the batches change.

result.name: the payment method line of the screen and of each batch
result.stored_or_displayed: Shown on the screen and written on the created Payments.

edge_cases.case: The screen holds one inbound and one outbound batch.
edge_cases.outcome: The batch of the other direction uses its own first available line, so both Payments can be created.

edge_cases.case: The documents name two different preferred lines.
edge_cases.outcome: The second source does not apply and the first available line is used.

edge_cases.case: The current line is still available.
edge_cases.outcome: It is kept, so an explicit choice is not overwritten.

worked_examples.description: A screen whose current line has become unavailable, with one preferred line named on the documents

expected_outputs.chosen: the single preferred line of the documents

worked_examples.narrative: The documents' preference is used, because the current line can no longer serve.

records.name: Whether grouping is offered for a single batch
records.purpose: The first variant of the grouping test: with one batch, grouping is offered only when there is more than one item and they do not all belong to one invoice-like document.

operands.name: the number of items of the batch
operands.constraints: must be more than one

operands.name: whether all the items belong to one document
operands.constraints: combined with the next operand

operands.name: whether that document is invoice-like
operands.constraints: when both hold, grouping is not offered

preconditions.condition: There is exactly one batch.
preconditions.otherwise: The other variant applies.

procedure: Check that the batch has more than one journal item.
Check that it is not the case that all the items belong to one document and that document is invoice-like.
Grouping is offered when both hold.
records.formula: can_group = ( the batch has more than one journal item ) AND NOT ( the batch's items all belong to ONE document AND that document is invoice-like )

rounding.what: Nothing; the test reads a count and two flags.
rounding.step: Whenever the batches change.

result.name: whether grouping is offered
result.stored_or_displayed: Decides whether the grouping switch appears on the register-payment screen.

edge_cases.case: The batch holds one item only.
edge_cases.outcome: Grouping is not offered, because there is nothing to group.

edge_cases.case: The items are the several installments of one invoice.
edge_cases.outcome: Grouping is not offered, because they already belong to one invoice-like document.

edge_cases.case: The items are the several installments of one plain entry.
edge_cases.outcome: Grouping is offered, because the document is not invoice-like.

worked_examples.description: One batch holding the receivable items of two different invoices
worked_examples.narrative: Two documents can be paid by one grouped payment or by two separate ones.

worked_examples.description: One batch holding the three installments of one invoice
worked_examples.narrative: There is only one document, so grouping would change nothing.

records.name: Whether grouping is offered for several batches
records.purpose: The second variant of the grouping test: with more than one batch, grouping is offered when at least one batch holds more than one of the items that will actually be paid.

operands.name: the journal items behind the common and by-default buckets
operands.constraints: the items that will actually be paid

operands.name: the items of each batch
operands.constraints: intersected with the items that will be paid

preconditions.condition: There is more than one batch.
preconditions.otherwise: The other variant applies.

procedure: Take the items that will actually be paid as the journal items behind the common and the by-default buckets.
For each batch, count how many of its items are among those.
Grouping is offered when any batch has more than one.
records.formula:
lines_to_pay = the journal items behind the common and by-default buckets
can_group    = any batch has more than one of its items inside lines_to_pay

rounding.what: Nothing; the test reads counts.
rounding.step: Whenever the batches or the buckets change.

result.name: whether grouping is offered
result.stored_or_displayed: Decides whether the grouping switch appears on the register-payment screen.

edge_cases.case: Every batch contributes exactly one item to be paid.
edge_cases.outcome: Grouping is not offered, because each batch would yield one payment either way.

edge_cases.case: Only the next installment of each document is being paid.
edge_cases.outcome: The items behind the buckets are fewer than the items of the batches, so grouping may not be offered even for large batches.

worked_examples.description: Two batches, one of which contributes two items to be paid
worked_examples.narrative: The first batch would yield one grouped payment or two separate ones, so the switch is offered.

records.name: The default of the grouping switch
records.purpose: Sets the initial position of the grouping switch, which is on only when every item of the single batch belongs to one document.

operands.name: whether every item of the single batch belongs to one document
operands.constraints: the condition of the on position

operands.name: whether the screen is editable
operands.constraints: when it is not, the switch is off

preconditions.condition: The screen is editable.
preconditions.otherwise: The switch is off.

procedure: When the screen is editable, set the switch on exactly when every item of the single batch belongs to one document.
Otherwise set it off.
records.formula:
group_payment = ( every item of the single batch belongs to one document )   when the screen is editable
              = false                                                        otherwise

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule sets a flag.
rounding.step: When the screen opens and whenever the batches change.

result.name: the initial position of the grouping switch
result.stored_or_displayed: Shown on the register-payment screen and editable by the user.

edge_cases.case: The screen is not editable.
edge_cases.outcome: The switch is off and the Payments are created one per document.

edge_cases.case: The single batch holds items of two documents.
edge_cases.outcome: The switch is off by default, so two payments are proposed.

worked_examples.description: One editable screen whose single batch holds two installments of one document
worked_examples.narrative: One payment covering both installments is proposed.

records.name: How many payments will be created and how many are blocked
records.purpose: Gives the two counters the register-payment screen shows before creation: the number of payments to be created and the number blocked by a missing or untrusted recipient account.

operands.name: the number of batches
operands.constraints: the total when grouping is on

operands.name: the number of journal items to be paid
operands.source: the items behind the common and by-default buckets
operands.constraints: the total when grouping is off

operands.name: the account chosen on the screen, when there is one
operands.constraints: overrides the batch's own chosen account

operands.name: the trust flag of the chosen account
operands.constraints: an untrusted account blocks the batch

operands.name: whether a recipient account is required
operands.constraints: when it is not, nothing is blocked

preconditions.condition: A recipient account is required by the payment method.
preconditions.otherwise: No batch is blocked and no counterparty is added to the missing list.

procedure: Take the total as the number of batches when grouping is on, and as the number of journal items to be paid when grouping is off.
For each batch, take the account as the one chosen on the screen when there is one, and as the batch's own chosen account otherwise.
When a recipient account is required and there is no account, add the batch's counterparties to the missing list.

When a recipient account is required and the account is untrusted, increase the blocked counter by one when grouping is on and by the number of the batch's items to be paid when grouping is off, and add the account to the untrusted list.
records.formula:
total = the number of batches                    when grouping is on
      = the number of journal items to be paid   when grouping is off
for each batch :
    account = the account chosen on the screen , when there is one , otherwise the batch's own chosen account
    if a recipient account is required :
        if there is no account           : add the batch's counterparties to the missing list
        else if the account is untrusted : blocked ← blocked + 1 when grouping is on , + the number of the batch's items to be paid when grouping is off ; add the account to the untrusted list

rounding.what: Nothing; the figures are counts.
rounding.step: Whenever the batches, the grouping switch or the chosen account change.

result.name: the number of payments to be created, the number blocked, the missing list and the untrusted list
result.stored_or_displayed: Displayed as a warning on the register-payment screen before the Payments are created.

edge_cases.case: The payment method does not require a recipient account.
edge_cases.outcome: Nothing is blocked, whatever the accounts are.

edge_cases.case: Grouping is off and a blocked batch holds three items to be paid.
edge_cases.outcome: The blocked counter rises by three, because three payments would have been created.

edge_cases.case: The counterparty has no bank account at all.
edge_cases.outcome: It is added to the missing list rather than to the blocked count.

worked_examples.description: Two batches with grouping on, one of them naming an untrusted account
worked_examples.narrative: One of the two payments would be refused at confirmation, so the screen warns before creation.

records.name: Edit mode of the register-payment screen
records.purpose: Says when the screen's own values, rather than the batch values, are used to create the Payments, and how many Payments are created in each case.

operands.name: whether the screen is editable
operands.constraints: required for edit mode

operands.name: the number of items of the first batch
operands.constraints: edit mode requires exactly one, unless grouping is on

operands.name: whether grouping is on
operands.constraints: an alternative to the single-item condition

preconditions.condition: The screen is editable.
preconditions.otherwise: Edit mode is off.

procedure: Set edit mode on when the screen is editable and either the first batch has exactly one journal item or grouping is on.
In edit mode, create exactly one Payment from the screen's own values.
Outside edit mode, create the Payments from the batch values: one per batch when grouping is on, and one per document when it is off.
records.formula:
edit_mode = the screen is editable AND ( the first batch has exactly one journal item OR grouping is on )
in edit mode : exactly one Payment is created , from the screen's own values
outside it   : one Payment per batch when grouping is on , one per document when it is off

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule sets a flag and a count.
rounding.step: When the screen opens and whenever the batches or the switch change.

result.name: whether the screen is in edit mode and how many Payments are created
result.unit_or_currency: a truth value and a count
result.stored_or_displayed: Decides which values the created Payments carry.

edge_cases.case: The screen is editable and the first batch holds one item.
edge_cases.outcome: Edit mode is on even when grouping is off, so one Payment is created from the screen's values.

edge_cases.case: The screen is not editable.
edge_cases.outcome: Edit mode is off and the batch values are used.

edge_cases.case: Grouping is on with three batches.
edge_cases.outcome: Edit mode is on, and exactly one Payment is created from the screen's own values rather than three from the batches.

worked_examples.description: An editable screen with one batch of one item
worked_examples.narrative: One Payment is created from what the user sees on the screen.

worked_examples.description: A screen with three batches and grouping off
worked_examples.narrative: The batches decide, and one Payment is created per document.

records.name: The memo of a payment settling one document
records.purpose: The first variant of the memo rule: when the items belong to a single document, the memo names that document by its most specific reference.

operands.name: the payment reference of the document
operands.constraints: preferred over the two other sources

operands.name: the reference of the document
operands.constraints: used when there is no payment reference

operands.name: the number of the document
operands.constraints: used when there is neither

preconditions.condition: The journal items read by the rule belong to exactly one document.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the two other variants applies.

procedure: Take the payment reference of the document.
When there is none, take the reference of the document.
When there is neither, take the number of the document.
records.formula: memo = the document's payment reference , or its own reference , or its number

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule selects a text.
rounding.step: When the Payments are created.

result.name: the memo of the Payment
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Payment, written into the reference of its Journal Entry and appended to the label of its liquidity and counterpart lines.

edge_cases.case: The document has a payment reference.
edge_cases.outcome: It is used, so the bank sees the reference the customer was asked to quote.

edge_cases.case: The document has neither a payment reference nor a reference.
edge_cases.outcome: Its number is used.

worked_examples.description: One customer invoice carrying a payment reference
worked_examples.narrative: The payment reference is the most specific of the three.

worked_examples.description: One customer invoice with no payment reference and no reference
worked_examples.narrative: The number is used as the last resort.

records.name: The memo of a payment settling several documents of which one is outbound
records.purpose: The second variant of the memo rule: when any of the documents is one the company pays, the memo lists their references so that the recipient can identify them.

operands.name: the kind of each document
operands.constraints: an outbound document is a vendor bill, an outgoing credit note or an incoming receipt

operands.name: the payment reference, the reference and the number of each document
operands.constraints: the most specific of the three is taken per document

preconditions.condition: The items read by the rule belong to more than one document and at least one of them is an outbound document.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the two other variants applies.

procedure: For each document, take its payment reference, or its own reference, or its number.
Drop the empty values.
Keep the distinct values.
Sort them.
Join them by a comma followed by a space.
records.formula: memo = the distinct values of ( the payment reference , or the reference , or the number ) over every document , with the empty ones dropped , sorted , joined by ", "

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule builds a text.
rounding.step: When the Payments are created.

result.name: the memo of the Payment
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Payment and written into the reference of its Journal Entry.

edge_cases.case: Two documents carry the same reference.
edge_cases.outcome: It appears once, because the values are made distinct.

edge_cases.case: One document has no reference of any kind.
edge_cases.outcome: It contributes nothing, because the empty values are dropped.

edge_cases.case: The references are given in another order.
edge_cases.outcome: The result is the same, because the values are sorted.

worked_examples.description: Two vendor bills whose references are given in the reverse of their sorted order
worked_examples.narrative: The two references are sorted and joined by a comma and a space.

records.name: The memo of a payment settling several inbound documents
records.purpose: The third variant of the memo rule: when several documents the company is owed money for are settled together, the memo is drawn from the company's group-payment sequence.

operands.name: the number of documents
operands.source: the items read by the rule
operands.constraints: more than one

operands.name: whether any document is an outbound one
operands.constraints: must be false

operands.name: the group-payment sequence of the company
operands.constraints: its next value is taken

preconditions.condition: The items read by the rule belong to more than one document and none of them is an outbound document.
preconditions.otherwise: One of the two other variants applies.

procedure: Take the next value of the company's group-payment sequence.
Use it as the memo.
records.formula: memo = the next value of the company's group-payment sequence

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule draws a sequence value.
rounding.step: When the Payments are created.

result.name: the memo of the Payment
result.stored_or_displayed: Stored on the Payment and written into the reference of its Journal Entry.

edge_cases.case: Only the next installment of two of three documents is being paid.
edge_cases.outcome: More than one document is still being paid, so the sequence value is used.

edge_cases.case: The sequence is drawn even though the payment might be cancelled.
edge_cases.outcome: The value is consumed, so the sequence may show gaps.

worked_examples.description: Two customer invoices paid together

expected_outputs.memo: the next group-payment number, for example GROUP/2026/00001

worked_examples.narrative: Neither invoice reference would identify the payment, so a group number is drawn.

worked_examples.description: Three customer invoices of which only the next installment of two is being paid
worked_examples.narrative: More than one document is being paid, so the sequence is still used.

records.name: Which journal items the memo rule reads
records.purpose: Says which of the selected items the memo is built from, so that a payment of only the next installment names only the documents actually being paid.

operands.name: whether the screen is editable
operands.constraints: part of the first condition

operands.name: the installment mode
operands.constraints: the full mode is part of the first condition

operands.name: whether the user typed a custom amount
operands.constraints: an alternative first condition on its own

operands.name: the journal items behind the common and by-default buckets
operands.constraints: read when the first condition does not hold

preconditions.condition: The buckets have been dispatched.
preconditions.otherwise: The second branch has nothing to read.

procedure: When the screen is editable and the installment mode is the full one, or when the user typed a custom amount, read every selected journal item.
Otherwise read only the journal items behind the common and the by-default buckets.
records.formula:
if the screen is editable AND the installment mode is full , OR the user typed a custom amount : read every selected journal item
else : read only the journal items behind the common and by-default buckets

rounding.what: Nothing; the rule selects a set of items.
rounding.step: Before the memo is built.

result.name: the set of items the memo rule reads
result.stored_or_displayed: Not stored; it decides which documents the memo names.

edge_cases.case: The user pays only the next installment of several documents.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the items behind the buckets are read, so the memo names only the documents actually being paid.

edge_cases.case: The user typed a custom amount.
edge_cases.outcome: Every selected item is read, because the amount no longer corresponds to any bucket.

edge_cases.case: The screen is not editable.
edge_cases.outcome: Only the items behind the buckets are read, whatever the mode is.

worked_examples.description: An editable screen in the full mode with no custom amount
worked_examples.narrative: The whole selection is paid, so the memo may name every document.

worked_examples.description: An editable screen paying only the next installment

expected_outputs.items_read: the journal items behind the common and by-default buckets

worked_examples.narrative: The memo names only the documents whose installment is being paid.
